| 1  | RangeMax           | int64             | -262 to 262                      |         |          |        | M                |
| 2  | Percent<br>Max     | per<br>cent100ths | all                              |         |          |        | O.a+             |
| 3  | Percent<br>Min     | per<br>cent100ths | max Per<br>centTypi<br>cal       |         |          |        | [Percent<br>Max] |
| 4  | Percent<br>Typical | per<br>cent100ths | Percent<br>Min to Per<br>centMax |         |          |        | [Percent<br>Min] |
| 5  | FixedMax           | uint64            | max 262 - 1                      |         |          |        | O.a+             |
| 6  | FixedMin           | uint64            | max Fixed<br>Max                 |         |          |        | [FixedMax]       |
| 7  | FixedTypi<br>cal   | uint64            | FixedMin<br>to Fixed<br>Max      |         |          |        | [FixedMin]       |

- If both [PercentMax](#page-228-0) and [FixedMax](#page-228-1) are indicated, then for a given true value in the range between [RangeMin](#page-227-0) and [RangeMax,](#page-228-2)
  - the reported value SHALL be less than or equal to the sum of the true value, [FixedMax](#page-228-1) and [PercentMax](#page-228-0) percent of the true value.
  - the reported value SHALL be greater than or equal to the true value minus the sum of [Fixed-](#page-228-1)[Max](#page-228-1) and [PercentMax](#page-228-0) percent of the true value.
- If only [PercentMax](#page-228-0) is indicated, then for a given true value in the range between [RangeMin](#page-227-0) and [RangeMax](#page-228-2),
  - the reported value SHALL be less than or equal to the sum of the true value and [PercentMax](#page-228-0) percent of the true value.
  - the reported value SHALL be greater than or equal to the true value minus [PercentMax](#page-228-0) percent of the true value.
- If only [FixedMax](#page-228-1) is indicated, then for a given true value in the range between [RangeMin](#page-227-0) and [RangeMax](#page-228-2),
  - the reported value SHALL be less than or equal to the sum of the true value and [FixedMax.](#page-228-1)
  - the reported value SHALL be greater than or equal to the true value minus [FixedMax.](#page-228-1)

### <span id="page-227-0"></span>**2.12.5.1.1.1. RangeMin Field**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum measurement value for the specified level of accuracy.

The value of this field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [MinMeasuredValue](#page-229-0) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct.](#page-228-3)

The value of this field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [MaxMeasuredValue](#page-229-1) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct.](#page-228-3)

# <span id="page-228-2"></span>**2.12.5.1.1.2. RangeMax Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum measurement value for the specified level of accuracy.

The value of this field SHALL be greater than the value of the [RangeMin](#page-227-0) field.

The value of this field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [MinMeasuredValue](#page-229-0) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct](#page-228-3).

The value of this field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [MaxMeasuredValue](#page-229-1) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct.](#page-228-3)

# <span id="page-228-0"></span>**2.12.5.1.1.3. PercentMax Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum +/- percentage accuracy for the associated measurement.

# **2.12.5.1.1.4. PercentMin Field**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum +/- percentage accuracy for the associated measurement.

### **2.12.5.1.1.5. PercentTypical Field**

This field SHALL indicate the typical +/- percentage accuracy for the associated measurement.

#### <span id="page-228-1"></span>**2.12.5.1.1.6. FixedMax Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum +/- fixed accuracy for the associated measurement, in the unit indicated by [MeasurementType](#page-229-2).

# **2.12.5.1.1.7. FixedMin Field**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum +/- fixed accuracy for the associated measurement, in the unit indicated by [MeasurementType](#page-229-2).

#### **2.12.5.1.1.8. FixedTypical Field**

This field SHALL indicate the typical +/- fixed accuracy for the associated measurement, in the unit indicated by [MeasurementType](#page-229-2).

#### <span id="page-228-3"></span>**2.12.5.1.2. MeasurementAccuracyStruct Type**

This struct represents the set of accuracy ranges for a given measurement, the maximum and minimum values for the measurement, and whether the measurement is directly measured or just estimated from other information.

| ID | Name                     | Type                                                 | Constraint  | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|-------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Measure<br>mentType      | Measure<br>mentType<br>Enum                          | all         |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | Measured                 | bool                                                 | all         |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | MinMea<br>sured<br>Value | int64                                                | -262 to 262 |         |          |        | M               |
| 3  | MaxMea<br>sured<br>Value | int64                                                | -262 to 262 |         |          |        | M               |
| 4  | Accura<br>cyRanges       | list[Mea<br>suremen<br>tAccura<br>cyRangeStr<br>uct] | min 1       |         |          |        | M               |

# <span id="page-229-2"></span>**2.12.5.1.2.1. MeasurementType Field**

This field SHALL indicate the type of measurement for the accuracy provided.

# **2.12.5.1.2.2. Measured Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the associated measurement was directly measured. If this field is not set to true, then the associated measurement was estimated.

# <span id="page-229-0"></span>**2.12.5.1.2.3. MinMeasuredValue Attribute**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum value that can be measured.

## <span id="page-229-1"></span>**2.12.5.1.2.4. MaxMeasuredValue Attribute**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum value that can be measured.

#### **2.12.5.1.2.5. AccuracyRanges Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of measurement ranges and their associated accuracies.

The value of the [RangeMin](#page-227-0) field on the first [MeasurementAccuracyRangeStruct](#page-226-0) in this list SHALL be equal to the value of the [MinMeasuredValue](#page-229-0) field.

The value of the [RangeMax](#page-228-2) field on the last [MeasurementAccuracyRangeStruct](#page-226-0) in this list SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [MaxMeasuredValue](#page-229-1) field.

The value of the [RangeMin](#page-227-0) field on each [MeasurementAccuracyRangeStruct](#page-226-0) in this list other than the first SHALL be one more the value of the [RangeMax](#page-228-2) field on the previous [MeasurementAccura](#page-226-0)[cyRangeStruct](#page-226-0) in this list (i.e. there SHALL be no gaps in the accuracy ranges, and the ranges SHALL be in increasing order).

# <span id="page-230-0"></span>**2.12.5.2. EnergyMeasurementStruct Type**

This struct SHALL indicate the amount of energy measured during a given measurement period.

A server which does not have the ability to determine the time in UTC, or has not yet done so, SHALL use the system time fields to specify the measurement period and observation times.

A server which has determined the time in UTC SHALL use the timestamp fields to specify the measurement period. Such a server MAY also include the systime fields to indicate how many seconds had passed since boot for a given timestamp; this allows for client-side resolution of UTC time for previous reports that only included systime.

Elements using this data type SHALL indicate whether it represents cumulative or periodic energy, e.g. in the name or in the element description.

| ID | Name                   | Type            | Constraint                      | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------------|-----------------|---------------------------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Energy                 | energy<br>mWh   | 0 to 262                        |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | StartTime<br>stamp     | epoch-s         |                                 |         |          |        | desc            |
| 2  | EndTime<br>stamp       | epoch-s         | min (Start<br>Timestamp<br>+ 1) |         |          |        | desc            |
| 3  | StartSys<br>time       | systime-ms      |                                 |         |          |        | desc            |
| 4  | EndSys<br>time         | systime-ms      | min (Start<br>Systime +<br>1)   |         |          |        | desc            |
| 5  | Appar<br>entEnergy     | energy<br>mVAh  | 0 to 262                        |         |          |        | P, APPE         |
| 6  | Reac<br>tiveEn<br>ergy | energy<br>mVARh | 0 to 262                        |         |          |        | P, REAE         |

#### <span id="page-230-1"></span>**2.12.5.2.1. Energy Field**

This field SHALL be the reported energy.

If the [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents cumulative energy, then this SHALL represent the cumulative energy recorded at either the value of the [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) field or the value of the [EndSystime](#page-231-1) field, or both.

If the [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents periodic energy, then this SHALL represent the energy recorded during the period specified by either the [StartTimestamp](#page-231-2) and [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) fields, the period specified by the [StartSystime](#page-231-3) and [EndSystime](#page-231-1) fields, or both.

#### <span id="page-231-2"></span>**2.12.5.2.2. StartTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL indicate the timestamp in UTC of the beginning of the period during which the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field was measured.

If this [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents cumulative energy, this field SHALL be omitted.

Otherwise, if the server had determined the time in UTC at or before the beginning of the measurement period, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had not yet determined the time in UTC at or before the beginning of the measurement period, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be omitted.

#### <span id="page-231-0"></span>**2.12.5.2.3. EndTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL indicate the timestamp in UTC of the end of the period during which the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field was measured.

If the server had determined the time in UTC by the end of the measurement period, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had not yet determined the time in UTC by the end of the measurement period, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be omitted.

#### <span id="page-231-3"></span>**2.12.5.2.4. StartSystime Field**

This field SHALL indicate the time elapsed since boot at the beginning of the period during which the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field was measured.

If this [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents cumulative energy, this field SHALL be omitted.

Otherwise, if the server had not yet determined the time in UTC at the start of the measurement period, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had determined the time in UTC at or before the beginning of the measurement period, this field MAY be omitted; if it is indicated, its value SHALL be the time elapsed since boot at the UTC time indicated in [StartTimestamp.](#page-231-2)

#### <span id="page-231-1"></span>**2.12.5.2.5. EndSystime Field**

This field SHALL indicate the time elapsed since boot at the end of the period during which the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field was measured.

If the server had not yet determined the time in UTC by the end of the measurement period, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had determined the time in UTC by the end of the measurement period, this field MAY be omitted; if it is indicated, its value SHALL be the time elapsed since boot at the UTC time indicated in [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0).

#### **2.12.5.2.6. ApparentEnergy Field**

This field SHALL indicate the reported apparent energy.

If the [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents cumulative energy, then this SHALL represent the cumulative apparent energy recorded at either the value of the [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) field or the value of the [EndSystime](#page-231-1) field, or both.

If the [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents periodic energy, then this SHALL represent the apparent energy recorded during the period specified by either the [StartTimestamp](#page-231-2) and [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) fields, the period specified by the [StartSystime](#page-231-3) and [EndSystime](#page-231-1) fields, or both.

#### **2.12.5.2.7. ReactiveEnergy Field**

This field SHALL be the reported reactive energy.

If the [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents cumulative energy, then this SHALL represent the cumulative reactive energy recorded at either the value of the [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) field or the value of the [EndSystime](#page-231-1) field, or both.

If the [EnergyMeasurementStruct](#page-230-0) represents periodic energy, then this SHALL represent the reactive energy recorded during the period specified by either the [StartTimestamp](#page-231-2) and [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) fields, the period specified by the [StartSystime](#page-231-3) and [EndSystime](#page-231-1) fields, or both.

# <span id="page-232-0"></span>**2.12.5.3. CumulativeEnergyResetStruct Type**

This struct SHALL represent the times at which cumulative measurements were last zero, either due to initialization of the device, or an internal reset of the cumulative value.

| ID | Name                               | Type       | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------------------------|------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Importe<br>dReset<br>Time<br>stamp | epoch-s    |            | X       | null     |        | [IMPE]          |
| 1  | Exporte<br>dReset<br>Time<br>stamp | epoch-s    |            | X       | null     |        | [EXPE]          |
| 2  | Importe<br>dResetSys<br>time       | systime-ms |            | X       | null     |        | [IMPE]          |
| 3  | Exporte<br>dResetSys<br>time       | systime-ms |            | X       | null     |        | [EXPE]          |

#### <span id="page-233-0"></span>**2.12.5.3.1. ImportedResetTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL indicate the timestamp in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [Cumula](#page-234-1)[tiveEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute was most recently zero.

If the server had determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [Cumula](#page-234-1)[tiveEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute was most recently zero, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had not yet determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute was most recently zero, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be omitted.

If the timestamp in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute was most recently zero cannot currently be determined, a value of null SHALL be returned.

#### **2.12.5.3.2. ExportedResetTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL indicate the timestamp in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [Cumula](#page-235-0)[tiveEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute was most recently zero.

If the server had determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [Cumula](#page-235-0)[tiveEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute was most recently zero, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had not yet determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute was most recently zero, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be omitted.

If the timestamp in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute was most recently zero cannot currently be determined, a value of null SHALL be returned.

#### **2.12.5.3.3. ImportedResetSystime Field**

This field SHALL indicate the time elapsed since boot when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute was most recently zero.

If the server had not yet determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute was most recently zero, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute was most recently zero, this field MAY be omitted; if it is indicated, its value SHALL be the time elapsed since boot at the UTC time indicated in [ImportedReset-](#page-233-0)[Timestamp](#page-233-0).

#### **2.12.5.3.4. ExportedResetSystime Field**

This field SHALL indicate the time elapsed since boot when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute was most recently zero.

If the server had not yet determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the

[CumulativeEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute was most recently zero, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be indicated.

Otherwise, if the server had determined the time in UTC when the value of the [Energy](#page-230-1) field on the [CumulativeEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute was most recently zero, this field MAY be omitted; if it is indicated, its value SHALL be the time elapsed since boot at the UTC time indicated in [ImportedReset-](#page-233-0)[Timestamp.](#page-233-0)

## **2.12.6.1. Accuracy Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the accuracy of energy measurement by this server. The value of the [MeasurementType](#page-229-2) field on this [MeasurementAccuracyStruct](#page-228-3) SHALL be ElectricalEnergy.

# <span id="page-234-1"></span>**2.12.6.2. CumulativeEnergyImported Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the most recent measurement of cumulative energy imported by the server over the lifetime of the device, and the timestamp of when the measurement was recorded.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the cumulative energy imported cannot currently be determined, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# <span id="page-235-0"></span>**2.12.6.3. CumulativeEnergyExported Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the most recent measurement of cumulative energy exported by the server over the lifetime of the device, and the timestamp of when the measurement was recorded.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the cumulative energy exported cannot currently be determined, a value of null SHALL be returned.

#### <span id="page-235-1"></span>**2.12.6.4. PeriodicEnergyImported Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the most recent measurement of energy imported by the server and the period during which it was measured.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the periodic energy imported cannot currently be determined, a value of null SHALL be returned.

### <span id="page-235-2"></span>**2.12.6.5. PeriodicEnergyExported Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the most recent measurement of energy exported by the server and the period during which it was measured.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose

to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the periodic energy exported cannot currently be determined, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# **2.12.6.6. CumulativeEnergyReset Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate when cumulative measurements were most recently zero.

# <span id="page-236-0"></span>**2.12.7. Events**

This cluster SHALL support these events:

| ID | Name                         | Priority | Quality | Access | Conformance |
|----|------------------------------|----------|---------|--------|-------------|
| 0  | CumulativeEn<br>ergyMeasured | INFO     |         | V      | CUME        |
| 1  | PeriodicEner<br>gyMeasured   | INFO     |         | V      | PERE        |

# **2.12.7.1. CumulativeEnergyMeasured Event**

This event SHALL be generated when the server takes a snapshot of the cumulative energy imported by the server, exported from the server, or both, but not more frequently than the rate mentioned in the description above of the related attribute.

The data of this event SHALL contain the following information:

| ID | Name               | Type                            | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|--------------------|---------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | EnergyIm<br>ported | EnergyMea<br>sure<br>mentStruct |            |         |          | CUME &<br>IMPE  |
| 1  | EnergyEx<br>ported | EnergyMea<br>sure<br>mentStruct |            |         |          | CUME &<br>EXPE  |

#### **2.12.7.1.1. EnergyImported Field**

This field SHALL be the value of [CumulativeEnergyImported](#page-234-1) attribute at the timestamp indicated in its [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) field, [EndSystime](#page-231-1) field, or both.

#### **2.12.7.1.2. EnergyExported Field**

This field SHALL be the value of [CumulativeEnergyExported](#page-235-0) attribute at the timestamp indicated in its [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) field, [EndSystime](#page-231-1) field, or both.

### **2.12.7.2. PeriodicEnergyMeasured Event**

This event SHALL be generated when the server reaches the end of a reporting period for imported energy, exported energy, or both.

The data of this event SHALL contain the following information:

| ID | Name               | Type                            | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|--------------------|---------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | EnergyIm<br>ported | EnergyMea<br>sure<br>mentStruct |            |         |          | PERE & IMPE     |
| 1  | EnergyEx<br>ported | EnergyMea<br>sure<br>mentStruct |            |         |          | PERE & EXPE     |

#### **2.12.7.2.1. EnergyImported Field**

This field SHALL be the value of [PeriodicEnergyImported](#page-235-1) attribute at the timestamp indicated in its [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) field, [EndSystime](#page-231-1) field, or both.

#### **2.12.7.2.2. EnergyExported Field**

This field SHALL be the value of [PeriodicEnergyExported](#page-235-2) attribute at the timestamp indicated in its [EndTimestamp](#page-231-0) field, [EndSystime](#page-231-1) field, or both.

# <span id="page-237-0"></span>**2.13. Electrical Power Measurement Cluster**

This cluster provides a mechanism for querying data about electrical power as measured by the server.

# <span id="page-237-1"></span>**2.13.1. Revision History**

The global ClusterRevision attribute value SHALL be the highest revision number in the table below.

| Revision | Description                                                                   |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Initial revision                                                              |
| 2        | Changed reactive and apparent power fields to<br>use new data types           |
| 3        | Changed range of apparent current field to<br>allow negative apparent current |

# <span id="page-238-0"></span>**2.13.2. Classification**

| Hierarchy | Role        | Scope    | PICS Code |
|-----------|-------------|----------|-----------|
| Base      | Application | Endpoint | EPM       |

# <span id="page-238-1"></span>**2.13.3. Cluster ID**

| ID     | Name                         |
|--------|------------------------------|
| 0x0090 | Electrical Power Measurement |

# <span id="page-238-2"></span>**2.13.4. Features**

This cluster SHALL support the FeatureMap bitmap attribute as defined below.

| Bit | Code | Feature                | Conformance | Summary                                             |
|-----|------|------------------------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| 0   | DIRC | DirectCurrent          | O.a+        | Supports measure<br>ment of direct cur<br>rent      |
| 1   | ALTC | AlternatingCur<br>rent | O.a+        | Supports measure<br>ment of alternat<br>ing current |
| 2   | POLY | PolyphasePower         | [ALTC]      | Supports<br>polyphase mea<br>surements              |
| 3   | HARM | Harmonics              | [ALTC]      | Supports measure<br>ment of AC har<br>monics        |
| 4   | PWRQ | PowerQuality           | [ALTC]      | Supports measure<br>ment of AC har<br>monic phases  |

### **2.13.4.1. DirectCurrent Feature**

This feature indicates the cluster can measure a direct current.

#### **2.13.4.2. AlternatingCurrent Feature**

This feature indicates the cluster can measure an alternating current.

## <span id="page-238-3"></span>**2.13.4.3. PolyphasePower Feature**

This feature indicates the cluster represents the collective measurements for a Polyphase power supply.

# **2.13.4.4. Harmonics Feature**

This feature indicates the cluster can measure the harmonics of an alternating current.

# **2.13.4.5. PowerQuality Feature**

This feature indicates the cluster can measure the harmonic phases of an alternating current.

| 2     | ActiveCurrent   | Active current in mil<br>liamps (mA)                    | M           |

| 4     | ApparentCurrent | Apparent current in<br>milliamps (mA)                   | M           |

| 7     | ApparentPower   | Apparent power in mil<br>livolt-amps (mVA)              | M           |

| 9     | RMSCurrent       | Root mean squared<br>current in milliamps<br>(mA)              | M           |

#### <span id="page-240-0"></span>**2.13.5.2.1. MeasurementAccuracyRangeStruct Type**

This struct represents the accuracy of a measurement for a range of measurement values. Accuracy SHALL be expressed as a maximum +/- percentage of the true value, a maximum +/- fixed value of the true value, or both.

| ID | Name           | Type              | Constraint                 | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance  |
|----|----------------|-------------------|----------------------------|---------|----------|--------|------------------|
| 0  | RangeMin       | int64             | -262 to 262                |         |          |        | M                |
| 1  | RangeMax       | int64             | -262 to 262                |         |          |        | M                |
| 2  | Percent<br>Max | per<br>cent100ths | all                        |         |          |        | O.a+             |
| 3  | Percent<br>Min | per<br>cent100ths | max Per<br>centTypi<br>cal |         |          |        | [Percent<br>Max] |

| ID | Name               | Type              | Constraint                       | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance  |
|----|--------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------|---------|----------|--------|------------------|
| 4  | Percent<br>Typical | per<br>cent100ths | Percent<br>Min to Per<br>centMax |         |          |        | [Percent<br>Min] |
| 5  | FixedMax           | uint64            | max 262 - 1                      |         |          |        | O.a+             |
| 6  | FixedMin           | uint64            | max Fixed<br>Max                 |         |          |        | [FixedMax]       |
| 7  | FixedTypi<br>cal   | uint64            | FixedMin<br>to Fixed<br>Max      |         |          |        | [FixedMin]       |

- If both [PercentMax](#page-242-0) and [FixedMax](#page-242-1) are indicated, then for a given true value in the range between [RangeMin](#page-241-0) and [RangeMax,](#page-241-1)
  - the reported value SHALL be less than or equal to the sum of the true value, [FixedMax](#page-242-1) and [PercentMax](#page-242-0) percent of the true value.
  - the reported value SHALL be greater than or equal to the true value minus the sum of [Fixed-](#page-242-1)[Max](#page-242-1) and [PercentMax](#page-242-0) percent of the true value.
- If only [PercentMax](#page-242-0) is indicated, then for a given true value in the range between [RangeMin](#page-241-0) and [RangeMax](#page-241-1),
  - the reported value SHALL be less than or equal to the sum of the true value and [PercentMax](#page-242-0) percent of the true value.
  - the reported value SHALL be greater than or equal to the true value minus [PercentMax](#page-242-0) percent of the true value.
- If only [FixedMax](#page-242-1) is indicated, then for a given true value in the range between [RangeMin](#page-241-0) and [RangeMax](#page-241-1),
  - the reported value SHALL be less than or equal to the sum of the true value and [FixedMax.](#page-242-1)
  - the reported value SHALL be greater than or equal to the true value minus [FixedMax.](#page-242-1)

## <span id="page-241-0"></span>**2.13.5.2.1.1. RangeMin Field**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum measurement value for the specified level of accuracy.

The value of this field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [MinMeasuredValue](#page-243-0) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct.](#page-242-2)

The value of this field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [MaxMeasuredValue](#page-243-1) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct](#page-242-2).

## <span id="page-241-1"></span>**2.13.5.2.1.2. RangeMax Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum measurement value for the specified level of accuracy.

The value of this field SHALL be greater than the value of the [RangeMin](#page-241-0) field.

The value of this field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [MinMeasuredValue](#page-243-0) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct](#page-242-2).

The value of this field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [MaxMeasuredValue](#page-243-1) field on the encompassing [MeasurementAccuracyStruct.](#page-242-2)

# <span id="page-242-0"></span>**2.13.5.2.1.3. PercentMax Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum +/- percentage accuracy for the associated measurement.

### **2.13.5.2.1.4. PercentMin Field**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum +/- percentage accuracy for the associated measurement.

### **2.13.5.2.1.5. PercentTypical Field**

This field SHALL indicate the typical +/- percentage accuracy for the associated measurement.

# <span id="page-242-1"></span>**2.13.5.2.1.6. FixedMax Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum +/- fixed accuracy for the associated measurement, in the unit indicated by [MeasurementType](#page-243-2).

### **2.13.5.2.1.7. FixedMin Field**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum +/- fixed accuracy for the associated measurement, in the unit indicated by [MeasurementType](#page-243-2).

### **2.13.5.2.1.8. FixedTypical Field**

This field SHALL indicate the typical +/- fixed accuracy for the associated measurement, in the unit indicated by [MeasurementType](#page-243-2).

#### <span id="page-242-2"></span>**2.13.5.2.2. MeasurementAccuracyStruct Type**

This struct represents the set of accuracy ranges for a given measurement, the maximum and minimum values for the measurement, and whether the measurement is directly measured or just estimated from other information.

| ID | Name                     | Type                        | Constraint  | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|--------------------------|-----------------------------|-------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Measure<br>mentType      | Measure<br>mentType<br>Enum | all         |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | Measured                 | bool                        | all         |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | MinMea<br>sured<br>Value | int64                       | -262 to 262 |         |          |        | M               |

| ID | Name                     | Type                                                 | Constraint  | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|-------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 3  | MaxMea<br>sured<br>Value | int64                                                | -262 to 262 |         |          |        | M               |
| 4  | Accura<br>cyRanges       | list[Mea<br>suremen<br>tAccura<br>cyRangeStr<br>uct] | min 1       |         |          |        | M               |

### <span id="page-243-2"></span>**2.13.5.2.2.1. MeasurementType Field**

This field SHALL indicate the type of measurement for the accuracy provided.

# **2.13.5.2.2.2. Measured Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the associated measurement was directly measured. If this field is not set to true, then the associated measurement was estimated.

#### <span id="page-243-0"></span>**2.13.5.2.2.3. MinMeasuredValue Attribute**

This field SHALL indicate the minimum value that can be measured.

### <span id="page-243-1"></span>**2.13.5.2.2.4. MaxMeasuredValue Attribute**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum value that can be measured.

#### **2.13.5.2.2.5. AccuracyRanges Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of measurement ranges and their associated accuracies.

The value of the [RangeMin](#page-241-0) field on the first [MeasurementAccuracyRangeStruct](#page-240-0) in this list SHALL be equal to the value of the [MinMeasuredValue](#page-243-0) field.

The value of the [RangeMax](#page-241-1) field on the last [MeasurementAccuracyRangeStruct](#page-240-0) in this list SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [MaxMeasuredValue](#page-243-1) field.

The value of the [RangeMin](#page-241-0) field on each [MeasurementAccuracyRangeStruct](#page-240-0) in this list other than the first SHALL be one more the value of the [RangeMax](#page-241-1) field on the previous [MeasurementAccura](#page-240-0)[cyRangeStruct](#page-240-0) in this list (i.e. there SHALL be no gaps in the accuracy ranges, and the ranges SHALL be in increasing order).

#### <span id="page-243-3"></span>**2.13.5.3. MeasurementRangeStruct Type**

This struct SHALL indicate the maximum and minimum values of a given [measurement type](#page-239-1) during a measurement period, along with the observation times of these values.

A server which does not have the ability to determine the time in UTC, or has not yet done so,

SHALL use the system time fields to specify the measurement period and observation times.

A server which has determined the time in UTC SHALL use the timestamp fields to specify the measurement period and observation times. Such a server MAY also include the systime fields to indicate how many seconds had passed since boot for a given timestamp; this allows for client-side resolution of UTC time for previous reports that only included systime.

| ID | Name                | Type                        | Constraint                      | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance  |
|----|---------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------|---------|----------|--------|------------------|
| 0  | Measure<br>mentType | Measure<br>mentType<br>Enum |                                 |         |          |        | M                |
| 1  | Min                 | int64                       | -262 to 262                     |         |          |        | M                |
| 2  | Max                 | int64                       | -262 to 262                     |         |          |        | M                |
| 3  | StartTime<br>stamp  | epoch-s                     |                                 |         |          |        | EndTime<br>stamp |
| 4  | EndTime<br>stamp    | epoch-s                     | min (Start<br>Timestamp<br>+ 1) |         |          |        | desc             |
| 5  | MinTime<br>stamp    | epoch-s                     |                                 |         |          |        | EndTime<br>stamp |
| 6  | MaxTime<br>stamp    | epoch-s                     | min<br>(MinTime<br>stamp + 1)   |         |          |        | EndTime<br>stamp |
| 7  | StartSys<br>time    | systime-ms                  |                                 |         |          |        | EndSys<br>time   |
| 8  | EndSys<br>time      | systime-ms                  | min (Start<br>Systime +<br>1)   |         |          |        | desc             |
| 9  | MinSys<br>time      | systime-ms                  |                                 |         |          |        | EndSys<br>time   |
| 10 | MaxSys<br>time      | systime-ms                  | min (Min<br>Systime +<br>1)     |         |          |        | EndSys<br>time   |

#### **2.13.5.3.1. MeasurementType Field**

This field SHALL be the type of measurement for the range provided.

# <span id="page-244-0"></span>**2.13.5.3.2. Min Field**

This field SHALL be the smallest measured value for the associated measurement over either the period between [StartTimestamp](#page-245-0) and [EndTimestamp,](#page-245-1) or the period between [StartSystime](#page-245-2) and [EndSystime](#page-245-3), or both.

#### <span id="page-245-4"></span>**2.13.5.3.3. Max Field**

This field SHALL be the largest measured value for the associated measurement over the period between either [StartTimestamp](#page-245-0) and [EndTimestamp](#page-245-1) or the period between [StartSystime](#page-245-2) and [EndSystime,](#page-245-3) or both.

#### <span id="page-245-0"></span>**2.13.5.3.4. StartTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL be the timestamp in UTC of the beginning of the measurement period.

If the server had not yet determined the time in UTC at or before the beginning of the measurement period, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be omitted.

#### <span id="page-245-1"></span>**2.13.5.3.5. EndTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL be the timestamp in UTC of the end of the measurement period.

If the server had not yet determined the time in UTC at or before the beginning of the measurement period, or does not have the capability of determining the time in UTC, this field SHALL be omitted.

### **2.13.5.3.6. MinTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL be the most recent timestamp in UTC that the value in the [Min](#page-244-0) field was measured.

This field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [StartTimestamp](#page-245-0) field.

This field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [EndTimestamp](#page-245-1) field.

### **2.13.5.3.7. MaxTimestamp Field**

This field SHALL be the most recent timestamp in UTC of the value in the [Max](#page-245-4) field.

This field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [StartTimestamp](#page-245-0) field.

This field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [EndTimestamp](#page-245-1) field.

#### <span id="page-245-2"></span>**2.13.5.3.8. StartSystime Field**

This field SHALL be the time since boot of the beginning of the measurement period.

If the server had determined the time in UTC at or before the start of the measurement period, this field MAY be omitted along with the [EndSystime,](#page-245-3) [MinSystime,](#page-246-1) and [MaxSystime](#page-246-2) fields.

#### <span id="page-245-3"></span>**2.13.5.3.9. EndSystime Field**

This field SHALL be the time since boot of the end of the measurement period.

If the server had determined the time in UTC at the end of the measurement period, this field MAY be omitted along with the [StartSystime](#page-245-2) field, [MinSystime](#page-246-1), and [MaxSystime](#page-246-2) fields.

#### <span id="page-246-1"></span>**2.13.5.3.10. MinSystime Field**

This field SHALL be the measurement time since boot of the value in the [Min](#page-244-0) field was measured.

This field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [StartSystime](#page-245-2) field.

This field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [EndSystime](#page-245-3) field.

#### <span id="page-246-2"></span>**2.13.5.3.11. MaxSystime Field**

This field SHALL be the measurement time since boot of the value in the [Max](#page-245-4) field.

This field SHALL be greater than or equal to the value of the [StartSystime](#page-245-2) field.

This field SHALL be less than or equal to the value of the [EndSystime](#page-245-3) field.

### <span id="page-246-3"></span>**2.13.5.4. HarmonicMeasurementStruct Type**

| ID | Name            | Type  | Constraint  | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------------|-------|-------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Order           | uint8 | min 1       |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | Measure<br>ment | int64 | -262 to 262 | X       |          |        | M               |

#### <span id="page-246-4"></span>**2.13.5.4.1. Order Field**

This field SHALL be the order of the harmonic being measured. Typically this is an odd number, but servers may choose to report even harmonics.

### **2.13.5.4.2. Measurement Field**

This field SHALL be the measured value for the given harmonic order.

For the [Harmonic Currents](#page-252-0) attribute, this value is the most recently measured harmonic current reading in milliamps (mA). A positive value indicates that the measured harmonic current is positive, and a negative value indicates that the measured harmonic current is negative.

For the [Harmonic Phases](#page-252-1) attribute, this value is the most recent phase of the given harmonic order in millidegrees (mDeg). A positive value indicates that the measured phase is leading, and a negative value indicates that the measured phase is lagging.

If this measurement is not currently available, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# **2.13.6.1. PowerMode Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the current mode of the server. For some servers, such as an EV, this may change depending on the mode of charging or discharging.

# <span id="page-248-1"></span>**2.13.6.2. NumberOfMeasurementTypes Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the maximum number of measurement types the server is capable of reporting.

# **2.13.6.3. Accuracy Attribute**

This SHALL indicate a list of [accuracy specifications](#page-242-2) for the [measurement types](#page-239-1) supported by the server. There SHALL be an entry for [ActivePower,](#page-239-1) as well as any other measurement types implemented by this server.

### <span id="page-248-0"></span>**2.13.6.4. Ranges Attribute**

This SHALL indicate a list of [measured ranges](#page-243-3) for different [measurement types.](#page-239-1) Each measurement type SHALL have at most one entry in this list, representing the range of measurements in the most recent measurement period.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

### **2.13.6.5. Voltage Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [Voltage](#page-239-1) reading in millivolts (mV).

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the voltage cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

### **2.13.6.6. ActiveCurrent Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [ActiveCurrent](#page-239-1) reading in milliamps (mA).

A positive value represents current flowing into the server, while a negative value represents current flowing out of the server.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the current cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# **2.13.6.7. ReactiveCurrent Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [ReactiveCurrent](#page-239-1) reading in milliamps (mA).

A positive value represents current flowing into the server, while a negative value represents current flowing out of the server.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the current cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# **2.13.6.8. ApparentCurrent Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [ApparentCurrent](#page-239-1) (square root sum of the squares of active and reactive currents) reading in milliamps (mA).

A positive value represents current flowing into the server, while a negative value represents current flowing out of the server.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the active or reactive currents cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

### **2.13.6.9. ActivePower Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [ActivePower](#page-239-1) reading in milliwatts (mW). If the power cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

A positive value represents power imported, while a negative value represents power exported.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the [Polyphase Power](#page-238-3) feature is set, this value represents the combined active power imported or exported.

# **2.13.6.10. ReactivePower Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [ReactivePower](#page-239-1) reading in millivolt-amps reactive (mVAR).

A positive value represents power imported, while a negative value represents power exported.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the reactive power cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

If the [Polyphase Power](#page-238-3) feature is supported, this value represents the combined reactive power imported or exported.

### **2.13.6.11. ApparentPower Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [ApparentPower](#page-239-1) reading in millivolt-amps (mVA).

A positive value represents power imported, while a negative value represents power exported.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the apparent power cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# **2.13.6.12. RMSVoltage Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [RMSVoltage](#page-239-1) reading in millivolts (mV).

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the RMS voltage cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

### **2.13.6.13. RMSCurrent Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [RMSCurrent](#page-239-1) reading in milliamps (mA).

A positive value represents current flowing into the server, while a negative value represents current flowing out of the server.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the RMS current cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# **2.13.6.14. RMSPower Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [RMSPower](#page-239-1) reading in milliwatts (mW).

A positive value represents power imported, while a negative value represents power exported.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the RMS power cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

# **2.13.6.15. Frequency Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [Frequency](#page-239-1) reading in millihertz (mHz).

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

If the frequency cannot be measured, a value of null SHALL be returned.

### <span id="page-252-0"></span>**2.13.6.16. HarmonicCurrents Attribute**

This SHALL indicate a list of [HarmonicMeasurementStruct](#page-246-3) values, with each [HarmonicMeasure](#page-246-3)[mentStruct](#page-246-3) representing the harmonic current reading for the harmonic order specified by [Order.](#page-246-4)

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

### <span id="page-252-1"></span>**2.13.6.17. HarmonicPhases Attribute**

This SHALL indicate a list of [HarmonicMeasurementStruct](#page-246-3) values, with each [HarmonicMeasure](#page-246-3)[mentStruct](#page-246-3) representing the most recent phase of the harmonic current reading for the harmonic order specified by [Order.](#page-246-4)

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

# **2.13.6.18. PowerFactor Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the Power Factor ratio in +/- 1/100ths of a percent.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

### **2.13.6.19. NeutralCurrent Attribute**

This SHALL indicate the most recent [NeutralCurrent](#page-239-1) reading in milliamps (mA). Typically this is a derived value, taking the magnitude of the vector sum of phase currents.

If the neutral current cannot be measured or derived, a value of null SHALL be returned.

A positive value represents an imbalance between the phase currents when power is imported.

A negative value represents an imbalance between the phase currents when power is exported.

The reporting interval of this attribute SHALL be manufacturer dependent. The server MAY choose to omit publication of deltas considered not meaningful.

The server SHALL NOT mark this attribute ready for report if the last time this was done was more recently than 1 second ago.

The server MAY delay marking this attribute ready for report for longer periods if needed, however the server SHALL NOT delay marking this attribute as ready for report for longer than 60 seconds.

This SHALL indicate the value of the [Ranges](#page-248-0) attribute at the time of event generation.

# <span id="page-254-0"></span>**2.14. Zone Management Cluster**

This cluster provides an interface to manage regions of interest, or Zones, which can be either manufacturer or user defined.

This cluster also defines a Trigger, which is a set of [conditions and timing](#page-259-0) that apply to a Zone and allow for [events](#page-267-0) to be generated or the triggering state to be used by other clusters such as [Push AV](#page-903-0) [Stream Transport Cluster](#page-903-0).

# <span id="page-254-1"></span>**2.14.1. Revision History**

The global ClusterRevision attribute value SHALL be the highest revision number in the table below.

| Revision | Description                                    |
|----------|------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Initial version of the Zone Management cluster |

# <span id="page-254-2"></span>**2.14.2. Classification**

| Hierarchy | Role        | Scope    | PICS Code |
|-----------|-------------|----------|-----------|
| Base      | Application | Endpoint | ZONEMGMT  |

# <span id="page-254-3"></span>**2.14.3. Cluster ID**

| ID     | Name            |
|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0550 | Zone Management |

# <span id="page-255-0"></span>**2.14.4. Features**

This cluster SHALL support the FeatureMap bitmap attribute as defined below.

| Bit | Code        | Feature                         | Conformance   | Summary                                        |
|-----|-------------|---------------------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------------|
| 0   | TWODCART    | TwoDimensional<br>CartesianZone | O             | Supports Two<br>Dimensional<br>Cartesian Zones |
| 1   | PERZONESENS | PerZoneSensitivity [TWODCART]   |               | Supports a sensi<br>tivity value per<br>Zone   |
| 2   | USERDEFINED | UserDefined                     | [TWODCART]    | Supports user<br>defined zones                 |
| 3   | FOCUSZONES  | FocusZones                      | [USERDEFINED] | Supports user<br>defined focus<br>zones        |

#### <span id="page-255-2"></span>**2.14.4.1. TwoDimensionalCartesianZone Feature**

When this feature is supported, Zones based on a 2 Dimensional Cartesian plane MAY be defined and SHALL be represented by a [TwoDCartesianZoneStruct.](#page-258-0) Within a [TwoDCartesianZoneStruct](#page-258-0) the bounding of the zone SHALL be a polygon defined by a list of vertices comprising X (horizontal) and Y (vertical) coordinates, with each vertex defining the point where adjacent edges meet and an implicit connection between the last and first vertices in the list.

The origin (0,0) SHALL be located at the top left of the Cartesian plane, with positive X and Y values moving right and down across the Cartesian plane respectively.

### <span id="page-255-4"></span>**2.14.4.2. PerZoneSensitivity Feature**

When this feature is supported, the [ZoneTriggerControlStruct](#page-259-0) SHALL be used for specifying a zone specific value for the sensitivity of that zone to trigger events. If not supported, only the [Sensitivity](#page-262-0) [Attribute](#page-262-0) SHALL be used.

## **2.14.4.3. UserDefined Feature**

When this feature is supported, the device allows for creating and managing user defined zones via commands.

# <span id="page-255-3"></span>**2.14.4.4. FocusZones Feature**

When this feature is supported, the device allows for creating and managing user defined [Focus](#page-256-0) [Value](#page-256-0) zones via commands.

# <span id="page-256-1"></span>**2.14.5.2. ZoneUseEnum Type**

#### <span id="page-256-5"></span>**2.14.5.2.1. Motion Value**

This value indicates the Zone is intended to be used for motion detection

#### **2.14.5.2.2. Privacy Value**

This value indicates the Zone is intended to be used for privacy blocking. All pixels within Privacy Zones SHALL be replaced with black.

### <span id="page-256-0"></span>**2.14.5.2.3. Focus Value**

This value indicates the Zone is intended to be a focal point for quality or analysis. Implementations MAY increase encoding quality within this type of Zone at the expense of other areas.

### <span id="page-256-3"></span>**2.14.5.3. ZoneSourceEnum Type**

#### <span id="page-257-3"></span>**2.14.5.3.1. Mfg Value**

This value indicates the Zone is built-in and provided by the manufacturer of the device. Zones of this type can't be created or modified using commands in this cluster.

#### <span id="page-257-5"></span>**2.14.5.3.2. User Value**

This value indicates the Zone was defined and created by a user. Zones of this type can be created, modified or deleted using commands in this cluster.

#### <span id="page-257-0"></span>**2.14.5.6. TwoDCartesianVertexStruct Type**

This struct is used to encode a point on the 2 Dimensional Cartesian Plane for the [TwoDCartesian-](#page-255-2)[Zone](#page-255-2) feature.

| ID | Name | Type   | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |

# <span id="page-257-4"></span>**2.14.5.6.1. X Field**

This field SHALL represent the position of the vertex along the horizontal (x) axis.

#### <span id="page-258-2"></span>**2.14.5.6.2. Y Field**

This field SHALL represent the position of the vertex along the vertical (y) axis.

# <span id="page-258-0"></span>**2.14.5.7. TwoDCartesianZoneStruct Type**

This struct is used to encode all information needed to define a TwoDCartesianZone.

| ID | Name     | Type                                        | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|----------|---------------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Name     | string                                      | max 32     |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | Use      | ZoneUseEn<br>um                             |            |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | Vertices | list[TwoD<br>Cartesian<br>Ver<br>texStruct] | 3 to 12    |         |          |        | M               |
| 3  | Color    | string                                      | 7, 9       |         |          |        | O               |

#### **2.14.5.7.1. Name Field**

The Name field SHALL be a string representing the name of the Zone. This is not guaranteed to be unique.

#### <span id="page-258-1"></span>**2.14.5.7.2. Use Field**

The Use field SHALL be a [Zone Use Enum](#page-256-1) representing the purpose of the Zone.

# <span id="page-258-3"></span>**2.14.5.7.3. Vertices Field**

The Vertices field SHALL be a list of vertices of type [TwoDCartesianVertexStruct.](#page-257-0) These vertices define a simple polygon on the TwoD Cartesian plane, which represents the bounds of the TwoD Cartesian Zone with an implicit connection between the last and first list items.

#### **2.14.5.7.4. Color Field**

This field SHALL indicate the color, in RGB or RGBA, used for attaching a color to the Zone definition and is a purely informational value to help in uniformly presenting Zones in User Interfaces and MAY be ignored. The value SHALL conform to the 6-digit or 8-digit format defined for [CSS sRGB](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#hex-notation) [hexadecimal color notation](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#hex-notation) [https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#hex-notation]. If a 6-digit format is used, then the alpha component SHALL assume the value of 0 meaning fully transparent interior.

### Examples:

- #00FFFF for R=0x00, G=0xFF, B=0xFF, A absent For a light-blue zone with full transparency.
- #00FFFF80 for R=0x00, G=0xFF, B=0xFF, A=0x80 For a light-blue zone with partial interior transparency.
- #000000FF for R=0x00, G=0x00, B=0x00, A=0xFF For a Privacy type zone that is black and fully

opaque interior.

## <span id="page-259-0"></span>**2.14.5.9. ZoneTriggerControlStruct Type**

This struct is used to encode a set of values for controlling the generation of [ZoneTriggered](#page-267-1) and [ZoneStopped](#page-268-3) events from the Node.

Zone events can be triggered due to many underlying reasons, such as a motion sensor on the device, and this is intended to be manufacturer-specific. When a triggering activity is initially detected, the Node SHALL generate a [ZoneTriggered](#page-267-1) event.

<span id="page-259-6"></span>This places the Node in a triggered state, at which point the Node SHALL internally track two values.

### **TimeSinceInitialTrigger**

The time in seconds since the initial triggering activity.

# <span id="page-260-1"></span>**TriggerDetectedDuration**

Initially set to the [InitialDuration](#page-260-0) value.

If the TriggerDetectedDuration value is exceeded by the TimeSinceInitialTrigger, the Node SHALL generate a [ZoneStopped](#page-268-3) event with the reason parameter set to [ActionStopped](#page-257-1).

However, if additional triggering actions are detected during this period, the Node SHALL increase the TriggerDetectedDuration value by the [AugmentationDuration](#page-261-2) value. This process can occur repeatedly but after the first increase of TriggerDetectedDuration the Node SHALL NOT increase the TriggerDetectedDuration value unless the previous TriggerDetectedDuration has been exceeded by the TimeSinceInitialTrigger.

If the TimeSinceInitialTrigger value exceeds the [MaxDuration](#page-261-3) value, the Node SHALL generate a [ZoneStopped](#page-268-3) with the reason parameter set to [Timeout](#page-257-2).

Once a [ZoneStopped](#page-268-3) event has been generated, the Node SHALL stop detecting the triggering activity for the period of the [BlindDuration](#page-261-4) value.

| ID | Name                         | Type      | Constraint                  | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------------------|-----------|-----------------------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | ZoneID                       | ZoneID    | all                         |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | InitialDu<br>ration          | elapsed-s | 1 to 65535                  |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | Augmen<br>tation<br>Duration | elapsed-s | max Ini<br>tialDura<br>tion |         |          |        | M               |
| 3  | MaxDura<br>tion              | elapsed-s | min Initial<br>Duration     |         |          |        | M               |
| 4  | BlindDu<br>ration            | elapsed-s | all                         |         |          |        | M               |
| 5  | Sensitivity                  | uint8     | 1 to Sensi<br>tivityMax     |         |          |        | PERZONE<br>SENS |

#### <span id="page-260-2"></span>**2.14.5.9.1. ZoneID Field**

This field SHALL indicate the unique [ZoneID](#page-261-1) of the Zone this Trigger applies to.

# <span id="page-260-0"></span>**2.14.5.9.2. InitialDuration Field**

This field SHALL indicate the initial duration in seconds after triggering activity is first detected before the Node could generate a [ZoneStopped](#page-268-3) event.

#### <span id="page-261-2"></span>**2.14.5.9.3. AugmentationDuration Field**

This field SHALL indicate the duration in seconds that the [TriggerDetectedDuration](#page-260-1) value is to be extended by if the triggering activity is still detected during this period.

#### <span id="page-261-3"></span>**2.14.5.9.4. MaxDuration Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum duration in seconds after the initial triggering activity detection that additional triggering activity will be detected.

#### <span id="page-261-4"></span>**2.14.5.9.5. BlindDuration Field**

This field SHALL indicate the duration in seconds after a [ZoneStopped](#page-268-3) event is generated that the Node SHALL NOT generate any [ZoneTriggered](#page-267-1) events.

#### **2.14.5.9.6. Sensitivity Field**

This field SHALL indicate the per-zone sensitivity of the underlying zone triggering detection mechanism. The higher the value, the more sensitive the detection. The actual meaning of the values is implementation-specific.

### <span id="page-261-1"></span>**2.14.5.10. ZoneID Type**

This data type is derived from uint16.

It represents a defined Zone. This value starts at 0 and monotonically increases by 1 with each new Zone provisioned by the Node or permanently created by the device maker. A value incremented past 65534 SHALL wrap to 0. The Node SHALL verify that the incremented ID does not match any other ID. If such a match is found, the ID SHALL be incremented until a unique ID is found.

A Node SHALL only store a single Zone for a particular ZoneID and that ID SHALL NOT change over the lifetime of the Zone.

| 0x0005 | Sensitivity              | uint8                                 | 1 to Sensi<br>tivityMax | N       |          | RW VO  | !PERZONE<br>SENS |

#### <span id="page-262-1"></span>**2.14.6.1. MaxUserDefinedZones Attribute**

This attribute SHALL specify the maximum number of user-defined zones that can be supported by the Node. This value is manufacturer-defined.

# <span id="page-262-4"></span>**2.14.6.2. MaxZones Attribute**

This attribute SHALL specify the maximum number of zones allowed to created. This value SHALL be the sum of the number of predefined [Mfg](#page-257-3) Zones, and [MaxUserDefinedZones](#page-262-1), if supported. This value is manufacturer-defined.

# <span id="page-262-2"></span>**2.14.6.3. Zones Attribute**

This attribute SHALL specify all currently defined zones as a list of [ZoneInformationStruct](#page-259-1). Use the commands from this cluster to add, update or remove entries.

# <span id="page-262-3"></span>**2.14.6.4. Triggers Attribute**

This attribute SHALL specify all currently defined triggers controlling the generation of [ZoneTrig](#page-267-1)[gered](#page-267-1) and [ZoneStopped](#page-268-3) events and SHALL be a list of [ZoneTriggerControlStruct.](#page-259-0) To add an entry use [CreateOrUpdateTrigger.](#page-266-0) To remove an entry use [RemoveTrigger.](#page-267-2)

#### **2.14.6.5. SensitivityMax Attribute**

This attribute SHALL specify the hardware specific value for the number of supported sensitivity levels. This value is manufacturer defined. If the PerZoneSensitivity feature is supported, the value of this attribute determines valid values for the Sensitivity field in [ZoneTriggerControlStruct](#page-259-0); if the PerZoneSensitivity feature is not supported, the value of this attribute determines valid values for the [Sensitivity Attribute.](#page-262-0) Implementations require two to ten levels of sensitivity control in order to ensure that there is some user-level customization of the Trigger.

### <span id="page-262-0"></span>**2.14.6.6. Sensitivity Attribute**

This attribute SHALL specify the sensitivity of the underlying zone triggering detection mechanism if the PerZoneSensitivity features is not supported. The higher the value the more sensitive the detection. The actual meaning of the values is implementation specific.

### <span id="page-263-1"></span>**2.14.6.7. TwoDCartesianMax Attribute**

This attribute SHALL specify the maximum X and Y points that are allowed for TwoD Cartesian Zones. If this cluster is on the same endpoint as [Camera AV Stream Management Cluster](#page-818-0), these values SHALL be equal to the value of SensorWidth - 1 and SensorHeight - 1 from the [VideoSensor-](#page-838-0)[Params attribute.](#page-838-0)
