### <span id="page-355-0"></span>**4.3.9.1. Calculated Local Temperature**

The local temperature SHALL be calculated from the *measured temperature*, including any adjustments applied by [LocalTemperatureCalibration](#page-356-6) attribute (if any) as follows:

[Calculated Local Temperature](#page-355-0) = (*measured temperature*) + [LocalTemperatureCalibration](#page-356-6)

The *measured temperature* value may be local, or remote, depending on the value of the [Remote-](#page-359-4)[Sensing](#page-359-4) attribute when supported.

All setpoint attributes in the Thermostat cluster SHALL be triggered based off this calculated value (i.e., measured temperature and any calibration offset).

If the LocalTemperatureNotExposed feature is present, the behavior of the thermostat SHALL be that the equipment's temperature control uses the calculated local temperature even if that value is not reported in the [LocalTemperature](#page-355-1) attribute.

#### <span id="page-355-1"></span>**4.3.9.2. LocalTemperature Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current [Calculated Local Temperature](#page-355-0), when available.

- If the LTNE feature is not supported:
  - If the [LocalTemperatureCalibration](#page-356-6) is invalid or currently unavailable, the attribute SHALL report null.
  - If the [LocalTemperatureCalibration](#page-356-6) is valid, the attribute SHALL report that value.
- Otherwise, if the LTNE feature is supported, there is no feedback externally available for the [LocalTemperatureCalibration.](#page-356-6) In that case, the LocalTemperature attribute SHALL always report null.

### <span id="page-356-4"></span>**4.3.9.3. OutdoorTemperature Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the outdoor temperature, as measured locally or remotely (over the network).

# <span id="page-356-5"></span>**4.3.9.4. Occupancy Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate whether the heated/cooled space is occupied or not, as measured locally or remotely (over the network).

# <span id="page-356-0"></span>**4.3.9.5. AbsMinHeatSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the absolute minimum level that the heating setpoint MAY be set to. This is a limitation imposed by the manufacturer.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints

# <span id="page-356-1"></span>**4.3.9.6. AbsMaxHeatSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the absolute maximum level that the heating setpoint MAY be set to. This is a limitation imposed by the manufacturer.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints

### <span id="page-356-2"></span>**4.3.9.7. AbsMinCoolSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the absolute minimum level that the cooling setpoint MAY be set to. This is a limitation imposed by the manufacturer.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints

### <span id="page-356-3"></span>**4.3.9.8. AbsMaxCoolSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the absolute maximum level that the cooling setpoint MAY be set to. This is a limitation imposed by the manufacturer.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints

#### **4.3.9.9. HVACSystemTypeConfiguration Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the HVAC system type controlled by the thermostat. If the thermostat uses physical DIP switches to set these parameters, this information SHALL be available read-only from the DIP switches. If these parameters are set via software, there SHALL be read/write access in order to provide remote programming capability.

#### <span id="page-356-6"></span>**4.3.9.10. LocalTemperatureCalibration Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the offset the Thermostat server SHALL make to the measured temperature (locally or remotely) to adjust the [Calculated Local Temperature](#page-355-0) prior to using, displaying or reporting it.

The purpose of this attribute is to adjust the calibration of the Thermostat server per the user's

preferences (e.g., to match if there are multiple servers displaying different values for the same HVAC area) or compensate for variability amongst temperature sensors.

If a Thermostat client attempts to write [LocalTemperatureCalibration](#page-356-6) attribute to an unsupported value (e.g., out of the range supported by the Thermostat server), the Thermostat server SHALL respond with a status of SUCCESS and set the value of [LocalTemperatureCalibration](#page-356-6) to the upper or lower limit reached.

**NOTE**

Prior to revision 8 of this cluster specification the value of this attribute was constrained to a range of -2.5°C to 2.5°C.

### <span id="page-357-1"></span>**4.3.9.11. OccupiedCoolingSetpoint Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the cooling mode setpoint when the room is occupied.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints.

If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value greater than [MaxCoolSetpointLimit](#page-359-2) or less than [MinCoolSetpointLimit](#page-359-1), a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If this attribute is set to a value that is less than ([OccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) + [MinSetpointDeadBand](#page-359-3)), the value of [OccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) SHALL be adjusted to ([OccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-357-1) - [MinSet](#page-359-3)[pointDeadBand](#page-359-3)).

If the occupancy status of the room is unknown, this attribute SHALL be used as the cooling mode setpoint.

If a client changes the value of this attribute, the server supports the PRES feature, and the server either does not support the OCC feature or the Occupied bit is set on the [Occupancy](#page-356-5) attribute, the value of the [ActivePresetHandle](#page-364-2) attribute SHALL be set to null.

#### <span id="page-357-0"></span>**4.3.9.12. OccupiedHeatingSetpoint Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the heating mode setpoint when the room is occupied.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints.

If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value greater than [MaxHeatSetpointLimit](#page-359-0) or less than [MinHeatSetpointLimit](#page-358-0), a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If this attribute is set to a value that is greater than ([OccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-357-1) - [MinSetpointDead-](#page-359-3)[Band](#page-359-3)), the value of [OccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-357-1) SHALL be adjusted to ([OccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) + [MinSetpointDeadBand](#page-359-3)).

If the occupancy status of the room is unknown, this attribute SHALL be used as the heating mode setpoint.

If a client changes the value of this attribute, the server supports the PRES feature, and the server either does not support the OCC feature or the Occupied bit is set on the [Occupancy](#page-356-5) attribute, the value of the [ActivePresetHandle](#page-364-2) attribute SHALL be set to null.

## <span id="page-358-2"></span>**4.3.9.13. UnoccupiedCoolingSetpoint Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the cooling mode setpoint when the room is unoccupied.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints.

If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value greater than [MaxCoolSetpointLimit](#page-359-2) or less than [MinCoolSetpointLimit,](#page-359-1) a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If this attribute is set to a value that is less than [\(UnoccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-358-1) + [MinSetpointDead-](#page-359-3)[Band\)](#page-359-3), the value of [UnoccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-358-1) SHALL be adjusted to ([UnoccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-358-2) - [MinSetpointDeadBand\)](#page-359-3).

If the occupancy status of the room is unknown, this attribute SHALL NOT be used.

If a client changes the value of this attribute, the server supports the PRES and OCC features, and the Occupied bit is not set on the [Occupancy](#page-356-5) attribute, the value of the [ActivePresetHandle](#page-364-2) attribute SHALL be set to null.

## <span id="page-358-1"></span>**4.3.9.14. UnoccupiedHeatingSetpoint Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the heating mode setpoint when the room is unoccupied.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints.

If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value greater than [MaxHeatSetpointLimit](#page-359-0) or less than [MinHeatSetpointLimit,](#page-358-0) a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If this attribute is set to a value that is greater than [\(UnoccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-358-2) - [MinSetpointDead-](#page-359-3)[Band\)](#page-359-3), the value of [UnoccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-358-2) SHALL be adjusted to ([UnoccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-358-1) + [MinSetpointDeadBand](#page-359-3)).

If the occupancy status of the room is unknown, this attribute SHALL NOT be used.

If a client changes the value of this attribute, the server supports the PRES and OCC features, and the Occupied bit is not set on the [Occupancy](#page-356-5) attribute, the value of the [ActivePresetHandle](#page-364-2) attribute SHALL be set to null.

#### <span id="page-358-0"></span>**4.3.9.15. MinHeatSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the minimum level that the heating setpoint MAY be set to.

This attribute, and the following three attributes, allow the user to define setpoint limits more constrictive than the manufacturer imposed ones. Limiting users (e.g., in a commercial building) to such setpoint limits can help conserve power.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which conflicts with setpoint values then those setpoints SHALL be adjusted by the minimum amount to permit this attribute to be set to the desired value. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which is not consistent with the constraints and cannot be resolved by modifying setpoints then a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

#### <span id="page-359-0"></span>**4.3.9.16. MaxHeatSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum level that the heating setpoint MAY be set to.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which conflicts with setpoint values then those setpoints SHALL be adjusted by the minimum amount to permit this attribute to be set to the desired value. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which is not consistent with the constraints and cannot be resolved by modifying setpoints then a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

### <span id="page-359-1"></span>**4.3.9.17. MinCoolSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the minimum level that the cooling setpoint MAY be set to.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which conflicts with setpoint values then those setpoints SHALL be adjusted by the minimum amount to permit this attribute to be set to the desired value. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which is not consistent with the constraints and cannot be resolved by modifying setpoints then a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

# <span id="page-359-2"></span>**4.3.9.18. MaxCoolSetpointLimit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum level that the cooling setpoint MAY be set to.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which conflicts with setpoint values then those setpoints SHALL be adjusted by the minimum amount to permit this attribute to be set to the desired value. If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value which is not consistent with the constraints and cannot be resolved by modifying setpoints then a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

# <span id="page-359-3"></span>**4.3.9.19. MinSetpointDeadBand Attribute**

On devices which support the AUTO feature, this attribute SHALL indicate the minimum difference between the Heat Setpoint and the Cool Setpoint.

Refer to [Setpoint Limits](#page-333-0) for constraints.

**NOTE** Prior to revision 8 of this cluster specification the value of this attribute was constrained to a range of 0°C to 2.5°C.

**NOTE** For backwards compatibility, this attribute is optionally writeable. However any writes to this attribute SHALL be silently ignored.

# <span id="page-359-4"></span>**4.3.9.20. RemoteSensing Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate when the local temperature, outdoor temperature and occupancy are being sensed by remote networked sensors, rather than internal sensors.

If the LTNE feature is present in the server, the LocalTemperature RemoteSensing bit value SHALL always report a value of 0.

If the LocalTemperature RemoteSensing bit is written with a value of 1 when the LTNE feature is present, the write SHALL fail and the server SHALL report a CONSTRAINT\_ERROR.

# <span id="page-360-1"></span>**4.3.9.21. ControlSequenceOfOperation Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the overall operating environment of the thermostat, and thus the possible system modes that the thermostat can operate in.

If an attempt is made to write to this attribute, the server SHALL silently ignore the write and the value of this attribute SHALL remain unchanged. This behavior is in place for backwards compatibility with existing thermostats.

### <span id="page-360-0"></span>**4.3.9.22. SystemMode Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current operating mode of the thermostat. Its value SHALL be limited by the [ControlSequenceOfOperation](#page-360-1) attribute.

### **4.3.9.23. ThermostatRunningMode Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the running mode of the thermostat. This attribute uses the same values as [SystemModeEnum](#page-341-0) but can only be Off, Cool or Heat. This attribute is intended to provide additional information when the thermostat's system mode is in auto mode.

## **4.3.9.24. StartOfWeek Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the day of the week that this thermostat considers to be the start of week for weekly setpoint scheduling.

This attribute MAY be able to be used as the base to determine if the device supports weekly scheduling by reading the attribute. Successful response means that the weekly scheduling is supported.

# **4.3.9.25. NumberOfWeeklyTransitions Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate how many weekly schedule transitions the thermostat is capable of handling.

#### **4.3.9.26. NumberOfDailyTransitions Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate how many daily schedule transitions the thermostat is capable of handling.

#### <span id="page-360-2"></span>**4.3.9.27. TemperatureSetpointHold Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the temperature hold status on the thermostat. If hold status is on, the thermostat SHOULD maintain the temperature setpoint for the current mode until a system mode change. If hold status is off, the thermostat SHOULD follow the setpoint transitions specified by its internal scheduling program. If the thermostat supports setpoint hold for a specific duration, it SHOULD also implement the [TemperatureSetpointHoldDuration](#page-361-0) attribute.

If the server supports a setpoint hold for a specific duration, it SHOULD also implement the [Set](#page-367-1)[pointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) attribute.

If this attribute is updated to SetpointHoldOn and the [TemperatureSetpointHoldDuration](#page-361-0) has a nonnull value and the [SetpointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) is supported, the server SHALL update the [Set](#page-367-1)[pointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) with a value of current UTC timestamp, in seconds, plus the value in [TemperatureSetpointHoldDuration](#page-361-0) multiplied by 60.

If this attribute is updated to SetpointHoldOff and the [SetpointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) is supported, the server SHALL set the [SetpointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) to null.

# <span id="page-361-0"></span>**4.3.9.28. TemperatureSetpointHoldDuration Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the period in minutes for which a setpoint hold is active. Thermostats that support hold for a specified duration SHOULD implement this attribute. The null value indicates the field is unused. All other values are reserved.

If this attribute is updated to a non-null value and the [TemperatureSetpointHold](#page-360-2) is set to SetpointHoldOn and the [SetpointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) is supported, the server SHALL update [Set](#page-367-1)[pointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) with a value of current UTC timestamp, in seconds, plus the new value of this attribute multiplied by 60.

If this attribute is set to null and the [SetpointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) is supported, the server SHALL set the [SetpointHoldExpiryTimestamp](#page-367-1) to null.

## **4.3.9.29. ThermostatRunningState Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current relay state of the heat, cool, and fan relays.

Unimplemented outputs SHALL be treated as if they were Off.

#### <span id="page-361-1"></span>**4.3.9.30. SetpointChangeSource Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the source of the current active [OccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-357-1) or [Occu](#page-357-0)[piedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) (i.e., who or what determined the current setpoint).

This attribute enables service providers to determine whether changes to setpoints were initiated due to occupant comfort, scheduled programming or some other source (e.g., electric utility or other service provider). Because automation services MAY initiate frequent setpoint changes, this attribute clearly differentiates the source of setpoint changes made at the thermostat.

### <span id="page-361-2"></span>**4.3.9.31. SetpointChangeAmount Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the delta between the current active [OccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-357-1) or [OccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) and the previous active setpoint. This attribute is meant to accompany the [SetpointChangeSource](#page-361-1) attribute; devices implementing [SetpointChangeAmount](#page-361-2) SHOULD also implement [SetpointChangeSource](#page-361-1).

The null value indicates that the previous setpoint was unknown.

# **4.3.9.32. SetpointChangeSourceTimestamp Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the time in UTC at which the [SetpointChangeAmount](#page-361-2) attribute change was recorded.

### <span id="page-362-0"></span>**4.3.9.33. EmergencyHeatDelta Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the delta between the [Calculated Local Temperature](#page-355-0) and the [Occu](#page-357-0)[piedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) or [UnoccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-358-1) attributes at which the Thermostat server will operate in emergency heat mode.

If the difference between the [Calculated Local Temperature](#page-355-0) and [OccupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-357-1) or [Unoc](#page-358-2)[cupiedCoolingSetpoint](#page-358-2) is greater than or equal to the [EmergencyHeatDelta](#page-362-0) and the Thermostat server's [SystemMode](#page-360-0) attribute is in a heating-related mode, then the Thermostat server SHALL immediately switch to the [SystemMode](#page-360-0) attribute value that provides the highest stage of heating (e.g., emergency heat) and continue operating in that running state until the [OccupiedHeatingSet](#page-357-0)[point](#page-357-0) value is reached. For example:

- [Calculated Local Temperature](#page-355-0) = 10.0°C
- [OccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) = 16.0°C
- [EmergencyHeatDelta](#page-362-0) = 2.0°C
- ⇒ [OccupiedHeatingSetpoint](#page-357-0) - [Calculated Local Temperature](#page-355-0) ≥? [EmergencyHeatDelta](#page-362-0)
  - ⇒ 16°C 10°C ≥? 2°C
- ⇒ TRUE >>> Thermostat server changes its SystemMode to operate in 2nd stage or emergency heat mode

The purpose of this attribute is to provide Thermostat clients the ability to configure rapid heating when a setpoint is of a specified amount greater than the measured temperature. This allows the heated space to be quickly heated to the desired level set by the user.

#### **4.3.9.34. ACType Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the type of Mini Split [ACTypeEnum](#page-338-0) of Mini Split AC is defined depending on how Cooling and Heating condition is achieved by Mini Split AC.

### <span id="page-362-1"></span>**4.3.9.35. ACCapacity Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate capacity of Mini Split AC in terms of the format defined by the [ACCa](#page-363-2)[pacityFormat](#page-363-2) attribute

#### **4.3.9.36. ACRefrigerantType Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate type of refrigerant used within the Mini Split AC.

### **4.3.9.37. ACCompressorType Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the type of compressor used within the Mini Split AC.

# **4.3.9.38. ACErrorCode Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the type of errors encountered within the Mini Split AC.

## **4.3.9.39. ACLouverPosition Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the position of Louver on the AC.

## **4.3.9.40. ACCoilTemperature Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the temperature of the AC coil, as measured locally or remotely (over the network).

### <span id="page-363-2"></span>**4.3.9.41. ACCapacityFormat Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the format for the [ACCapacity](#page-362-1) attribute.

# <span id="page-363-3"></span>**4.3.9.42. PresetTypes Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the supported [PresetScenarioEnum](#page-339-0) values, limits on how many presets can be created for each [PresetScenarioEnum,](#page-339-0) and whether or not a thermostat can transition automatically to a given scenario.

The list SHALL contain at least one entry.

The list SHALL NOT be larger than the number of supported [PresetScenarioEnum](#page-339-0) values (maximum 7).

The list SHALL NOT contain any [PresetTypeStruct](#page-344-0) entries with duplicate [PresetScenarioEnum](#page-339-0) values.

# <span id="page-363-5"></span>**4.3.9.43. ScheduleTypes Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the supported SystemMode values for Schedules, limits on how many schedules can be created for each SystemMode value, and whether or not a given SystemMode value supports transitions to Presets, target setpoints, or both.

The list SHALL contain at least one entry.

The list SHALL NOT be larger than the number of supported schedule SystemMode values (maximum 3, since the data type only allows Auto, Heat and Cool).

The list SHALL NOT contain any [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) entries with duplicate [SystemModeEnum](#page-341-0) values.

### <span id="page-363-4"></span>**4.3.9.44. NumberOfPresets Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum number of [entries](#page-342-0) supported by the Presets attribute.

# <span id="page-363-1"></span>**4.3.9.45. NumberOfSchedules Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum number of [entries](#page-345-0) supported by the Schedules attribute.

# <span id="page-363-0"></span>**4.3.9.46. NumberOfScheduleTransitions Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum number of [transitions](#page-346-0) per [Schedules](#page-345-0) attribute entry.

### <span id="page-364-1"></span>**4.3.9.47. NumberOfScheduleTransitionPerDay Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum number of [transitions](#page-346-0) per day of the week supported by each Schedules attribute entry. If this value is null, there is no limit on the number of transitions per day.

### <span id="page-364-2"></span>**4.3.9.48. ActivePresetHandle Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) of the active preset. If this attribute is null, then there is no active preset.

# <span id="page-364-3"></span>**4.3.9.49. ActiveScheduleHandle Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) of the active schedule. A null value in this attribute indicates that there is no active schedule.

#### <span id="page-364-0"></span>**4.3.9.50. Presets Attribute**

This attribute SHALL contain the current list of configured [presets.](#page-342-0)

On receipt of a write request:

- 1. If the [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field is null, the [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) SHALL be treated as an added preset, and the device SHALL create a new unique value for the [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field.
  - a. If the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field is true, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- 2. If the [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field is not null, the [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) SHALL be treated as a modification of an existing preset.
  - a. If the value of the [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field does not match any of the existing [presets,](#page-342-0) a response with the status code NOT\_FOUND SHALL be returned.
  - b. If the value of the [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field is duplicated on multiple [presets](#page-342-0) in the updated list, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
  - c. If the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field is true, and the [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) in the current value with a matching [Pre](#page-343-0)[setHandle](#page-343-0) field has a [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field set to false, a response with the status code CONSTRAIN-T\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
  - d. If the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field is false, and the [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) in the current value with a matching [Pre](#page-343-0)[setHandle](#page-343-0) field has a [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field set to true, a response with the status code CONSTRAIN-T\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- 3. If the specified [PresetScenarioEnum](#page-339-0) value does not exist in [PresetTypes,](#page-363-3) a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- 4. If the [Name](#page-343-2) is set, but the associated [PresetTypeStruct](#page-344-0) does not have the [SupportsNames](#page-335-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- 5. If appending the received [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) to the pending list of Presets would cause the total number of pending [presets](#page-342-0) to exceed the value of the [NumberOfPresets](#page-363-4) attribute, a response with the status code RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED SHALL be returned.
- 6. If appending the received [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) to the pending list of Presets would cause the total num-

ber of pending [presets](#page-342-0) whose PresetScenario field matches the appended preset's PresetScenario field to exceed the value of the [NumberOfPresets](#page-344-1) field on the [PresetTypeStruct](#page-344-0) whose [Pre](#page-344-2)[setScenario](#page-344-2) matches the appended preset's PresetScenario field, a response with the status code RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED SHALL be returned.

- 7. Otherwise, the write SHALL be pended until receipt of a commit request, and the status code SUCCESS SHALL be returned.
  - a. If the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field is null:
    - i. If there is a [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) in the current value with a matching [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field, the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field on the pending [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) SHALL be set to the value of the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) on the matching [PresetStruct](#page-342-0).
    - ii. Otherwise, the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field on the pending [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) SHALL be set to false.

On an attempt to commit, the status of this attribute SHALL be determined as follows:

- 1. For all existing [presets:](#page-342-0)
  - a. If, after applying all pending changes, the updated value of the [Presets](#page-364-0) attribute would not contain a [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) with a matching [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field, indicating the removal of the [Pre](#page-342-0)[setStruct](#page-342-0), the server SHALL check for invalid removal of the [PresetStruct:](#page-342-0)
    - i. If the [BuiltIn](#page-343-1) field is true on the removed [PresetStruct](#page-342-0), the attribute status SHALL be CONSTRAINT\_ERROR.
    - ii. If the MSCH feature is supported and the removed [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) would be referenced by any [PresetHandle](#page-348-2) on any [ScheduleTransitionStruct](#page-346-0) on any [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) in the updated value of the [Schedules](#page-365-0) attribute, the attribute status SHALL be INVALID\_IN\_STATE.
    - iii. If the removed [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) is equal to the value of the [ActivePresetHandle](#page-364-2) attribute, the attribute status SHALL be INVALID\_IN\_STATE.
- 2. Otherwise, the attribute status SHALL be SUCCESS.

### <span id="page-365-0"></span>**4.3.9.51. Schedules Attribute**

This attribute SHALL contain a list of [ScheduleStructs](#page-345-0).

On receipt of a write request:

- 1. For all [schedules](#page-345-0) in the write request:
  - a. If the [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field is null, the [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) SHALL be treated as an added schedule, and the device SHALL create a new unique value for the [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field.
    - i. If the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field is true, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
  - b. Otherwise, if the [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field is not null, the [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) SHALL be treated as a modification of an existing schedule.
    - i. If the value of the [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field does not match any of the existing [schedules](#page-345-0), a response with the status code NOT\_FOUND SHALL be returned.
    - ii. If the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field is true, and the [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) in the current value with a matching [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field has a [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field set to false, a response with the status code CON-

STRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

- iii. If the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field is false, and the [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) in the current value with a matching [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field has a [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field set to true, a response with the status code CON-STRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- c. If the specified [SystemMode](#page-345-1) does not exist in [ScheduleTypes](#page-363-5), a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- d. If the number of [transitions](#page-346-0) exceeds the [NumberOfScheduleTransitions](#page-363-0) value, a response with the status code RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED SHALL be returned.
- e. If the value of the [NumberOfScheduleTransitionPerDay](#page-364-1) attribute is not null, and the number of [transitions](#page-346-0) on any single day of the week exceeds the [NumberOfScheduleTransitionPer-](#page-364-1)[Day](#page-364-1) value, a response with the status code RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED SHALL be returned.
- f. If the [PresetHandle](#page-345-3) field is present, but the associated [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) does not have the [SupportsPresets](#page-336-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- g. If the [PresetHandle](#page-345-3) field is present, but after applying all pending changes, the [Presets](#page-364-0) attribute would not contain a [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) whose [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field matches the value of the [PresetHandle](#page-345-3) field, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- h. If the [Name](#page-345-2) is set, but the associated [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) does not have the [SupportsNames](#page-336-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- i. For all [transitions](#page-346-0) in all [schedules](#page-345-0) in the write request:
  - i. If the [PresetHandle](#page-348-2) field is present, but the [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) matching the value of the [SystemMode](#page-345-1) field on the encompassing [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) does not have the [SupportsP](#page-336-0)[resets](#page-336-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- j. If the [PresetHandle](#page-348-2) field is present, but after applying all pending changes, the [Presets](#page-364-0) attribute would not contain a [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) whose [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field matches the value of the [PresetHandle](#page-348-2) field, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
  - i. If the [SystemMode](#page-348-5) field is present, but the [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) matching the value of the [SystemMode](#page-345-1) field on the encompassing [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) does not have the [SupportsSet](#page-336-0)[points](#page-336-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
  - ii. If the [SystemMode](#page-348-5) field is has a value of SystemModeOff, but the [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) matching the value of the [SystemMode](#page-345-1) field on the encompassing [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) does not have the [SupportsOff](#page-336-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- k. If the [HeatingSetpoint](#page-348-3) field is present, but the [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) matching the value of the [SystemMode](#page-345-1) field on the encompassing [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) does not have the [SupportsSetpoints](#page-336-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- l. If the [CoolingSetpoint](#page-348-4) field is present, but the [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) matching the value of the [SystemMode](#page-345-1) field on the encompassing [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) does not have the [SupportsSetpoints](#page-336-0) bit set, a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.
- 2. If appending the received [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) to the pending list of Schedules would cause the total

number of pending [schedules](#page-345-0) to exceed the value of the [NumberOfSchedules](#page-363-1) attribute, a response with the status code RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED SHALL be returned.

- 3. If appending the received [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) to the pending list of Schedules would cause the total number of pending [schedules](#page-345-0) whose [SystemMode](#page-345-1) field matches the appended schedule's [Sys](#page-345-1)[temMode](#page-345-1) field to exceed the value of the [NumberOfSchedules](#page-349-4) field on the [ScheduleTypeStruct](#page-349-3) whose [SystemMode](#page-349-2) field matches the appended schedule's [SystemMode](#page-345-1) field, a response with the status code RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED SHALL be returned.
- 4. Otherwise, the write SHALL be pended until receipt of a commit request, and the attribute status SHALL be SUCCESS.
  - a. If the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field is null:
    - i. If there is a [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) in the current value with a matching [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field, the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field on the pending [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) SHALL be set to the value of the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) on the matching [ScheduleStruct.](#page-345-0)
    - ii. Otherwise, the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field on the pending [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) SHALL be set to false.

On an attempt to commit, the status of this attribute SHALL be determined as follows:

- 1. For all existing [schedules:](#page-345-0)
  - a. If, after applying all pending changes, the updated value of the [Schedules](#page-365-0) attribute would not contain a [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) with a matching [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field, indicating the removal of the [ScheduleStruct,](#page-345-0) the server SHALL check for invalid removal of the [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0):
    - i. If the [BuiltIn](#page-346-2) field is true on the removed [ScheduleStruct,](#page-345-0) the attribute status SHALL be CONSTRAINT\_ERROR.
    - ii. If the removed [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) is equal to the value of the [ActiveScheduleHandle](#page-364-3) attribute, the attribute status SHALL be INVALID\_IN\_STATE.
- 2. Otherwise, the attribute status SHALL be SUCCESS.

### <span id="page-367-1"></span>**4.3.9.52. SetpointHoldExpiryTimestamp Attribute**

If there is a known time when the [TemperatureSetpointHold](#page-360-2) SHALL be cleared, this attribute SHALL contain the timestamp in UTC indicating when that will happen. If there is no such known time, this attribute SHALL be null.

If the [TemperatureSetpointHold](#page-360-2) is set to SetpointHoldOn and the [TemperatureSetpointHoldDura](#page-361-0)[tion](#page-361-0) is set to null, this attribute SHALL be set to null indicating there is a hold on the Thermostat without a duration.

If the [TemperatureSetpointHold](#page-360-2) is set to SetpointHoldOff, this attribute SHALL be set to null indicating there is no hold on the Thermostat.

# <span id="page-367-0"></span>**4.3.10. Commands**

| ID   | Name                             | Direction       | Response | Access | Conformance |
|------|----------------------------------|-----------------|----------|--------|-------------|
| 0x00 | Set<br>pointRaiseLo<br>wer       | client ⇒ server | Y        | O      | M           |
| 0x05 | SetAc<br>tiveSched<br>uleRequest | client ⇒ server | Y        | O      | MSCH        |
| 0x06 | SetActivePre<br>setRequest       | client ⇒ server | Y        | O      | PRES        |

### **4.3.10.1. SetpointRaiseLower Command**

This command will raise or lower the setpoint based on the provided values.

| ID | Name   | Type                                   | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|--------|----------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | Mode   | Set<br>pointRaiseLo<br>werMod<br>eEnum | desc       |         |          | M               |
| 1  | Amount | int8                                   | all        |         |          | M               |

# **4.3.10.1.1. Mode Field**

The field SHALL specify which setpoints are to be adjusted.

#### **4.3.10.1.1.1. Heat Value**

If the server does not support the HEAT feature then it SHALL respond with INVALID\_COMMAND. If the server supports the AUTO feature and the resulting setpoint would be invalid solely due to [Min-](#page-359-3)[SetpointDeadBand](#page-359-3) then the Cooling setpoint SHALL be increased sufficiently to maintain the deadband.

#### **4.3.10.1.1.2. Cool Value**

If the server does not support the COOL feature then it SHALL respond with INVALID\_COMMAND. If the server supports the AUTO feature and the resulting setpoint would be invalid solely due to [MinSetpointDeadBand](#page-359-3) then the Heating setpoint SHALL be decreased sufficiently to maintain the deadband.

# **4.3.10.1.1.3. Both Value**

The client MAY indicate Both regardless of the server feature support. The server SHALL only adjust the setpoint that it supports and not respond with an error.

#### **4.3.10.1.2. Amount Field**

This field SHALL indicate the amount (possibly negative) that should be added to the setpoint(s), in steps of 0.1°C.

#### **4.3.10.1.3. Effect on Receipt**

Upon receipt, the attributes for the indicated setpoint(s) SHALL have the amount specified in the Amount field added to them. If the Occupancy feature is supported, the affected setpoints(s) SHALL be determined based on the current occupancy state, otherwise the occupied setpoints SHALL be adjusted. If the resulting value is outside the limits imposed by [MinCoolSetpointLimit](#page-359-1), [MaxCoolSet](#page-359-2)[pointLimit,](#page-359-2) [MinHeatSetpointLimit](#page-358-0) and [MaxHeatSetpointLimit,](#page-359-0) the value is clamped to those limits. This is not considered an error condition.

### **4.3.10.2. SetActiveScheduleRequest Command**

This command will set the active schedule to the provided schedule handle.

| ID | Name               | Type   | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|--------------------|--------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | Schedule<br>Handle | octstr | max 16     |         |          | M               |

#### <span id="page-369-0"></span>**4.3.10.2.1. ScheduleHandle Field**

This field SHALL specify the value of the [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field on the [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) to be made active.

#### **4.3.10.2.2. Effect on Receipt**

Upon receipt, if the [Schedules](#page-365-0) attribute contains a [ScheduleStruct](#page-345-0) whose [ScheduleHandle](#page-345-4) field matches the value of the [ScheduleHandle](#page-369-0) field, the server SHALL set the thermostat's [ActiveSched](#page-364-3)[uleHandle](#page-364-3) attribute to the value of the [ScheduleHandle](#page-369-0) field.

Otherwise, the server SHALL return a status code of INVALID\_COMMAND.

# **4.3.10.3. SetActivePresetRequest Command**

This command will set the active preset to the provided preset handle.

| ID | Name             | Type   | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------|--------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | Pre<br>setHandle | octstr | max 16     | X       |          | M               |

#### <span id="page-369-1"></span>**4.3.10.3.1. PresetHandle Field**

This field SHALL specify the value of the [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field on the [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) to be made active. If the field is set to null, that indicates there should be no active preset.

#### **4.3.10.3.2. Effect on Receipt**

Upon receipt of this command,

- 1. If the [PresetHandle](#page-369-1) field is null, the server SHALL clear the [ActivePresetHandle](#page-364-2) attribute by setting it to null.
- 2. Otherwise,
  - a. If this command is received with a [PresetHandle](#page-369-1) such that the [Presets](#page-364-0) attribute does not contain a [PresetStruct](#page-342-0) whose [PresetHandle](#page-343-0) field matches the value of the [PresetHandle,](#page-369-1) the server SHALL return a status code of INVALID\_COMMAND.
  - b. The server SHALL set the [ActivePresetHandle](#page-364-2) attribute to the value of the [PresetHandle](#page-369-1) field.
  - c. The server SHALL adjust the thermostat's setpoints according to the preset identified by the [PresetHandle](#page-369-1) field. If the Occupancy feature is supported, the server SHALL determine the setpoints to set based on the current occupancy state, otherwise the occupied setpoints SHALL be set.
- 3. The server SHALL return a status code of SUCCESS.

# <span id="page-370-0"></span>**4.4. Fan Control Cluster**

This cluster specifies an interface to control the speed of a fan.

# <span id="page-370-1"></span>**4.4.1. Revision History**

The global ClusterRevision attribute value SHALL be the highest revision number in the table below.

| Revision | Description                                                                                |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Mandatory global ClusterRevision attribute<br>added                                        |
| 2        | New data model format and notation; Percent,<br>speed and motion settings; General cleanup |
| 3        | Addition of AirflowDirection and Step command                                              |
| 4        | Change conformance for FanModeSe<br>quenceEnum                                             |
| 5        | Clarified attribute usage, added conformance<br>column                                     |
| 6        | Removed Zigbee related elements, removed P<br>quality                                      |

# <span id="page-370-2"></span>**4.4.2. Classification**

| Hierarchy | Role        | Scope    | PICS Code |
|-----------|-------------|----------|-----------|
| Base      | Application | Endpoint | FAN       |

# <span id="page-371-0"></span>**4.4.3. Cluster ID**

| ID     | Name        |
|--------|-------------|
| 0x0202 | Fan Control |

# <span id="page-371-1"></span>**4.4.4. Features**

This cluster SHALL support the FeatureMap bitmap attribute as defined below.

| Bit | Code | Feature          | Conformance | Summary                                         |
|-----|------|------------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| 0   | SPD  | MultiSpeed       | O           | 0-SpeedMax Fan<br>Speeds                        |
| 1   | AUT  | Auto             | O           | Automatic mode<br>supported for fan<br>speed    |
| 2   | RCK  | Rocking          | O           | Rocking move<br>ment supported                  |
| 3   | WND  | Wind             | O           | Wind emulation<br>supported                     |
| 4   | STEP | Step             | O           | Step command<br>supported                       |
| 5   | DIR  | AirflowDirection | O           | Airflow Direction<br>attribute is sup<br>ported |

#### <span id="page-371-3"></span>**4.4.4.1. MultiSpeed Feature**

Legacy Fan Control cluster revision 0-1 defined 3 speeds (low, medium and high) plus automatic speed control but left it up to the implementer to decide what was supported. Therefore, it is assumed that legacy client implementations are capable of determining, from the server, the number of speeds supported between 1, 2, or 3, and whether automatic speed control is supported.

The [MultiSpeed](#page-371-3) feature includes attributes that support a running fan speed value from 0 to Speed-Max.

See [Section 4.4.6.6.1, "Speed Rules"](#page-377-0) for more details.

#### **4.4.5.2.2. NaturalWind Bit**

#### <span id="page-374-0"></span>**4.4.6.1. FanMode Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current speed mode of the fan.

This attribute SHALL be set to one of the values in [FanModeEnum](#page-373-1) supported by the server as indicated in the [FanModeSequence](#page-375-0) attribute. The Low value SHALL be supported if and only if the [Fan-](#page-375-0)[ModeSequence](#page-375-0) attribute value is less than 4. The Medium value SHALL be supported if and only if the [FanModeSequence](#page-375-0) attribute value is 0 or 2.

This attribute MAY be written by a client to request a different fan mode. The server SHALL return INVALID\_IN\_STATE to indicate that the fan is not in a state where this attribute can be changed to the requested value.

The server MAY have values that this attribute can never be set to or that will be ignored by the server. For example, where this cluster appears on the same or another endpoint as other clusters with a system dependency, for example the Thermostat cluster, attempting to set this attribute to Off may not be allowed by the system.

If an attempt is made to set this attribute to a value not supported by the server as indicated in the [FanModeSequence](#page-375-0) attribute, the server SHALL respond with CONSTRAINT\_ERROR.

When this attribute is successfully written to, the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) and [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) (if present) attributes SHALL be set to appropriate values, as defined by [Section 4.4.6.3.1, "Percent Rules"](#page-376-1) and [Section 4.4.6.6.1, "Speed Rules"](#page-377-0) respectively, unless otherwise specified below.

When this attribute is set to any valid value, the [PercentCurrent](#page-377-2) and [SpeedCurrent](#page-379-0) (if present) attributes SHALL indicate the actual currently operating fan speed, unless otherwise specified below.

#### **4.4.6.1.1. Off Value**

Successfully setting the attribute value to Off SHALL set the values of these attributes to 0 (zero):

- [PercentSetting](#page-376-0)
- [PercentCurrent](#page-377-2)
- [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) (if present)
- [SpeedCurrent](#page-379-0) (if present)

#### **4.4.6.1.2. Auto Value**

Successfully setting the attribute value to Auto SHALL set the values of these attributes to null:

- [PercentSetting](#page-376-0)
- [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) (if present)

These attributes SHALL continue to indicate the current state of the fan while this attribute value is Auto:

- [PercentCurrent](#page-377-2)
- [SpeedCurrent](#page-379-0) (if present)

### **4.4.6.1.3. On Value**

If a client attempts to write a value of On, the attribute SHALL be set to High.

### **4.4.6.1.4. Smart Value**

If a client attempts to write a value of Smart, this attribute SHALL be set to Auto if the AUT feature is supported, otherwise the attribute SHALL be set to High.

# <span id="page-375-0"></span>**4.4.6.2. FanModeSequence Attribute**

This attribute indicates the fan speed ranges that SHALL be supported by the server.

## <span id="page-376-0"></span>**4.4.6.3. PercentSetting Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the speed setting for the fan with a value of 0 indicating that the fan is off and a value of 100 indicating that the fan is set to run at its maximum speed. If the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute is set to Auto, the value of this attribute SHALL be set to null.

This attribute MAY be written to by a client to indicate a new fan speed. If a client writes null to this attribute, the attribute value SHALL NOT change. If the fan is in a state where this attribute cannot be changed to the requested value, the server SHALL return INVALID\_IN\_STATE.

When this attribute is successfully written, the server SHALL set the value of the [FanMode](#page-374-0) and [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) (if present) attributes to values that abide by the mapping requirements listed below.

#### <span id="page-376-1"></span>**4.4.6.3.1. Percent Rules**

It is up to the server implementation to map between ranges of the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attribute, the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) (if present) attribute, and the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute enumerated values that are supported as indicated in the [FanModeSequence](#page-375-0) attribute per the requirements below.

There SHALL be a mapping between the values of the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute and the values of this attribute by dividing the domain of values of this attribute into ranges as follows:

- The ranges SHALL be non-overlapping, contiguous, and in ascending order.
- Every value from 0 to 100 SHALL be in exactly 1 range.
- Every value in a lower range shall be less than every value in any higher range.
- The value 0 (zero) in this attribute SHALL be in a range by itself. This range SHALL map to Off.
- If Auto is supported by the server, the null value SHALL be in a range by itself. This range SHALL map to Auto.
- There shall be a one-to-one mapping between each range and each value in [FanMode](#page-374-0).
- Every range SHALL map to a greater value in the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute than all lower-valued ranges.

The following table illustrates an example of such a mapping. The actual mapping provided by the server is determined by the manufacturer subject to the rules mandated in this specification. Note that the values in this example are contiguous, non-overlapping and span from 0 to 100 with no missing values. Note also that each range appears in an ascending order, 0 appears by itself in a range that maps to Off, and null appears by itself in a range that maps to Auto.

| Attribute      | Values |         |          |           |      |  |
|----------------|--------|---------|----------|-----------|------|--|
| FanMode        | Off    | Low     | Medium   | High      | Auto |  |
| PercentSetting | 0      | 1 to 33 | 34 to 66 | 67 to 100 | null |  |

If a client successfully sets the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute, the server SHALL set the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attribute to some value within the range which maps to the [FanMode](#page-374-0) setting. If no such value exists, the attribute value SHALL NOT change. If a client successfully sets the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attribute, the server SHALL set the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute to the value of the corresponding range, and the [SpeedSet](#page-377-1)[ting](#page-377-1) attribute (if present) according to the equation below. If a client successfully sets the [Per-](#page-376-0) [centSetting](#page-376-0) attribute to 0, the server SHALL set the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute to Off and the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) (if present) attribute to 0.

If the [MultiSpeed](#page-371-3) feature is supported, the value of the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) and [SpeedCurrent](#page-379-0) (speed) attributes SHALL be calculated from the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) or [PercentCurrent](#page-377-2) (percent) attributes respectively using the following formula:

• speed = ceil( SpeedMax \* (percent \* 0.01) )

For example: If the SpeedMax attribute is 42 (42 speed fan) and PercentSetting is changed to 25, then [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) and [SpeedCurrent](#page-379-0) become 11 (rounding up 10.5).

# <span id="page-377-2"></span>**4.4.6.4. PercentCurrent Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the actual currently operating fan speed, or zero to indicate that the fan is off. There MAY be a temporary mismatch between the value of this attribute and the value of the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attribute due to other system requirements or constraints that would not allow the fan to operate at the requested setting.

For example, if the value of this attribute is currently 50%, and the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attribute is newly set to 25%, the value of this attribute MAY stay above 25% for a period necessary to dissipate internal heat, maintain product operational safety, etc.

When the value of the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute is AUTO, the value of this attribute MAY vary across the range over time.

See [Section 4.4.6.3.1, "Percent Rules"](#page-376-1) for more details.

# <span id="page-377-3"></span>**4.4.6.5. SpeedMax Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum value to which the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) attribute can be set.

### <span id="page-377-1"></span>**4.4.6.6. SpeedSetting Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the speed setting for the fan. This attribute MAY be written by a client to indicate a new fan speed. If the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute is set to Auto, the value of this attribute SHALL be set to null.

The server SHALL support all values between 0 and [SpeedMax](#page-377-3).

If a client writes null to this attribute, the attribute value SHALL NOT change. If the fan is in a state where this attribute cannot be changed to the requested value, the server SHALL return INVALID\_IN\_STATE.

When this attribute is successfully written to, the server SHALL set the value of the [FanMode](#page-374-0) and [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attributes to values that abide by the mapping requirements listed below.

#### <span id="page-377-0"></span>**4.4.6.6.1. Speed Rules**

It is up to the server implementation to map between ranges of the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) attribute, the [Per-](#page-376-0)

[centSetting](#page-376-0) attribute, and the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute enumerated values that are supported as indicated in the [FanModeSequence](#page-375-0) attribute per the requirements below.

There SHALL be a mapping between the values of the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute and the values of this attribute by dividing the domain of values of this attribute into ranges as follows:

- The ranges SHALL be non-overlapping, contiguous, and in ascending order.
- Every value from 0 to SpeedMax SHALL be in exactly 1 range.
- Every value in any lower range shall be less than every value in any higher range.
- The value 0 (zero) in this attribute SHALL be in a range by itself. This range SHALL map to Off.
- If Auto is supported by the server, the null value SHALL be in a range by itself. This range SHALL map to Auto.
- There shall be a one-to-one mapping between each range and each value in [FanMode](#page-374-0).
- Every range SHALL map to a greater value in the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute than all lower-valued ranges.

If a client successfully sets the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute, the server SHALL set the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) attribute to some value within the range which maps to the [FanMode](#page-374-0) setting, as well as the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attribute according to the equation below. If no such value exists, the attribute value SHALL NOT change.

If a client successfully sets the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) attribute to 0, the server SHALL set the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute to Off and the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) attribute to 0.

The following table illustrates an example of such a mapping with a value of 6 for the [SpeedMax](#page-377-3) attribute. The actual mapping provided by the server is determined by the manufacturer subject to the rules mandated in this specification. Note that the values in this example are contiguous, nonoverlapping and span from 0 to 6 with no missing values. Note also that each range appears in an ascending order, 0 appears by itself in a range that maps to Off, and null appears by itself in a range that maps to Auto.

| Attribute    | Values |        |        |        |      |  |
|--------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|------|--|
| FanMode      | Off    | Low    | Medium | High   | Auto |  |
| SpeedSetting | 0      | 1 to 2 | 3 to 4 | 5 to 6 | null |  |

The value of the [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) and [PercentCurrent](#page-377-2) (percent) attributes SHALL be calculate from the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) and [SpeedCurrent](#page-379-0) (speed) attributes respectively using the following formula:

• percent = floor( speed/SpeedMax \* 100 )

For example: If the SpeedMax attribute is 42 (42 speed fan) and [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) attribute is changed to 11, then [PercentSetting](#page-376-0) and [PercentCurrent](#page-377-2) become 26.

### <span id="page-379-0"></span>**4.4.6.7. SpeedCurrent Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the actual currently operating fan speed, or zero to indicate that the fan is off. There MAY be a temporary mismatch between the value of this attribute and the value of the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) attribute due to other system requirements or constraints that would not allow the fan to operate at the requested setting.

For example, if the value of this attribute is currently 5, and the [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1) attribute is newly set to 2, the value of this attribute MAY stay above 2 for a period necessary to dissipate internal heat, maintain product operational safety, etc.

When the value of the [FanMode](#page-374-0) attribute is AUTO, the value of this attribute MAY vary across the range over time.

See [Section 4.4.6.6.1, "Speed Rules"](#page-377-0) for more details.

### **4.4.6.8. RockSupport Attribute**

This attribute is a bitmap that indicates the rocking motions that are supported by the server.

If this attribute is supported by the server, at least one bit SHALL be set in this attribute.

# **4.4.6.9. RockSetting Attribute**

This attribute is a bitmap that indicates the currently active fan rocking motion setting. Each bit SHALL only be set to 1, if the corresponding bit in the RockSupport attribute is set to 1, otherwise a status code of CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If a combination of supported bits is set by a client, and the server does not support the combination, the lowest supported single bit in the combination SHALL be set and active, and all other bits SHALL indicate zero.

For example: If RockUpDown and RockRound are both set, but this combination is not possible, then only RockUpDown becomes active.

#### **4.4.6.10. WindSupport Attribute**

This attribute is a bitmap that indicates what wind modes are supported by the server.

If this attribute is supported by the server, at least one bit SHALL be set in this attribute.

#### **4.4.6.11. WindSetting Attribute**

This attribute is a bitmap that indicates the current active fan wind feature settings. Each bit SHALL only be set to 1, if the corresponding bit in the WindSupport attribute is set to 1, otherwise a status code of CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If a combination of supported bits is set by a client, and the server does not support the combination, the lowest supported single bit in the combination SHALL be set and active, and all other bits SHALL indicate zero.

For example: If Sleep Wind and Natural Wind are set, but this combination is not possible, then only Sleep Wind becomes active.

## **4.4.6.12. AirflowDirection Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current airflow direction of the fan. This attribute MAY be written by a client to indicate a new airflow direction for the fan. This attribute SHALL be set to one of the values in the [AirflowDirectionEnum](#page-372-1) table.

# <span id="page-380-0"></span>**4.4.7. Commands**

| ID   | Name | Direction       | Response | Access | Conformance |
|------|------|-----------------|----------|--------|-------------|
| 0x00 | Step | client ⇒ server | Y        | O      | STEP        |

### **4.4.7.1. Step Command**

This command indirectly changes the speed-oriented attributes of the fan in steps rather than using the speed-oriented attributes, [FanMode,](#page-374-0) [PercentSetting,](#page-376-0) or [SpeedSetting](#page-377-1), directly. This command supports, for example, a user-operated and wall-mounted toggle switch that can be used to increase or decrease the speed of the fan by pressing the toggle switch up or down until the desired fan speed is reached. How this command is interpreted by the server and how it affects the values of the speed-oriented attributes is implementation specific.

For example, a fan supports this command, and the value of the FanModeSequence attribute is 0. The current value of the FanMode attribute is 2, or Medium. This command is received with the Direction field set to Increase. As per it's specific implementation, the server reacts to the command by setting the value of the FanMode attribute to 3, or High, which in turn sets the PercentSetting and SpeedSetting (if present) attributes to appropriate values, as defined by [Section 4.4.6.3.1, "Percent Rules"](#page-376-1) and [Section 4.4.6.6.1, "Speed Rules"](#page-377-0) respectively.

This command supports these fields:

| ID | Name      | Type                  | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------|-----------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | Direction | StepDirectio<br>nEnum |            |         |          | M               |
| 1  | Wrap      | bool                  |            |         | false    | O               |
| 2  | LowestOff | bool                  |            |         | true     | O               |

### **4.4.7.1.1. Direction Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the speed-oriented attributes increase or decrease to the next step value.

#### **4.4.7.1.2. Wrap Field**

This field SHALL indicate if the speed-oriented attributes wrap between highest and lowest step value.

#### **4.4.7.1.3. LowestOff Field**

This field SHALL indicate that the fan being off (FanMode = Off, PercentSetting = 0, or SpeedSetting = 0) is included as a step value.

#### **4.4.7.1.4. When Generated**

A client sends this command to change the speed-oriented attributes up or down in a step by step fashion.

#### **4.4.7.1.5. Effect Upon Receipt**

The successful receipt of this command could result in one or more of the speed-oriented attributes, FanMode, PercentSetting, or SpeedSetting, to change.

- This command SHALL be executed even if the speed-oriented attributes are not currently at an implemented step value.
- If the Direction field is Increase,
  - If the speed-oriented attributes are lower than the highest step value, the speed-oriented attributes SHALL change to the lowest step value that is higher than the current speed-oriented attributes.
  - Else if Wrap is TRUE, the speed-oriented attributes SHALL change to the lowest step value.
  - Else the speed-oriented attributes SHALL change to (or remain at) the highest step value.
- If the Direction field is Decrease,
  - If the speed-oriented attributes are higher than the lowest step value, the speed-oriented attributes SHALL change to the highest step value that is lower than the current speed-oriented attributes.
  - Else if Wrap is TRUE, the speed-oriented attributes SHALL change to the highest step value.
  - Else the speed-oriented attributes SHALL change to (or remain at) the lowest step value.
- Although the effect of the Step command is implementation specific, the effect on receipt of the Step command SHALL adhere to the conformance of the affected attributes.

# <span id="page-381-0"></span>**4.5. Thermostat User Interface Configuration Cluster**

This cluster provides an interface to allow configuration of the user interface for a thermostat, or a thermostat controller device, that supports a keypad and LCD screen.

The global ClusterRevision attribute value SHALL be the highest revision number in the table below.

| Revision | Description                                                                                            |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Mandatory global ClusterRevision attribute<br>added                                                    |
| 2        | New data model format and notation, added<br>"Conversion of Temperature Values for Display"<br>section |

| Hierarchy | Role        | Scope    | PICS Code |
|-----------|-------------|----------|-----------|
| Base      | Application | Endpoint | TSUIC     |

# <span id="page-382-1"></span>**4.5.3. Cluster ID**

| ID     | Name                                    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------|
| 0x0204 | Thermostat User Interface Configuration |

See the Temperature Conversion section in the Data Model for unit conversion between Fahrenheit and Celsius.

# <span id="page-383-1"></span>**4.5.5.3. ScheduleProgrammingVisibilityEnum Type**

This data type is derived from enum8.

| Value | Name                             | Summary                                                                           | Conformance |

## **4.5.6.1. TemperatureDisplayMode Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the units of the temperature displayed on the thermostat screen.

# **4.5.6.2. KeypadLockout Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the level of functionality that is available to the user via the keypad.

# **4.5.6.3. ScheduleProgrammingVisibility Attribute**

This attribute is used to hide the weekly schedule programming functionality or menu on a thermostat from a user to prevent local user programming of the weekly schedule. The schedule programming MAY still be performed via a remote interface, and the thermostat MAY operate in schedule programming mode.

This attribute is designed to prevent local tampering with or disabling of schedules that MAY have been programmed by users or service providers via a more capable remote interface. The programming schedule SHALL continue to run even though it is not visible to the user locally at the thermostat.

### **4.6.4.1. TimeSync Feature**

This feature SHALL indicate that the valve uses Time Synchronization and UTC time to indicate duration and auto close time.

This feature SHALL NOT be supported unless the device supports the Time Synchronization cluster.

# **4.6.4.2. Level Feature**

This feature SHALL indicate that the valve is capable of being adjusted to a specific position, as a percentage, of its full range of motion.

### <span id="page-387-0"></span>**4.6.7.1. OpenDuration Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the total duration, in seconds, for which the valve will remain open for this current opening.

A value of null SHALL indicate the duration is not set, meaning that the valve will remain open until closed by the user or some other automation.

# <span id="page-387-2"></span>**4.6.7.2. DefaultOpenDuration Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the default duration, in seconds, for which the valve will remain open, if the OpenDuration field is not present in the [Open](#page-389-1) command.

A value of null SHALL indicate the duration is not set, meaning that the valve will remain open until closed by the user or some other automation.

# <span id="page-387-3"></span>**4.6.7.3. AutoCloseTime Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the UTC time when the valve will close, depending on value of the [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) attribute.

This attribute SHALL be null:

- When [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) is null, or
- When the valve does not have a synchronized UTCTime in the Time Synchronization cluster, or
- When the valve is closed.

When the value of this attribute is earlier or equal to the current UTC time, the valve SHALL automatically transition to its closed position. The behavior of transitioning to the closed position, SHALL match the behavior described in the [Close](#page-391-1) command.

If this attribute is not null and the Time Synchronization cluster receives a SetUTCTime command, modifying the current UTC time of the device, the value of this attribute SHALL be adjusted to match the new UTC time plus the value of the [RemainingDuration](#page-387-1) attribute.

# <span id="page-387-1"></span>**4.6.7.4. RemainingDuration Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the remaining duration, in seconds, until the valve closes.

This attribute SHALL be null:

- When [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) is null, or
- When the valve is closed.

The value of this attribute SHALL only be reported in the following cases:

- When it changes from null to any other value and vice versa, or
- When it changes to 0, or
- When it increases, or
- When the closing time changes.

Meaning that clients SHOULD NOT rely on the reporting of this attribute in order to keep track of the remaining duration, due to this attribute not being reported during regular countdown.

When reading this attribute it SHALL return the remaining duration, in seconds, until the valve closes.

When the value of this attribute counts down to 0, the valve SHALL automatically transition to its closed position. The behavior of transitioning to the closed position SHALL match the behavior described in the [Close](#page-391-1) command.

# <span id="page-388-2"></span>**4.6.7.5. CurrentState Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current state of the valve.

A value of null SHALL indicate that the current state is not known.

### <span id="page-388-1"></span>**4.6.7.6. TargetState Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the target state, while changing the state, of the valve.

A value of null SHALL indicate that no target position is set, since the change in state is either done or failed.

## <span id="page-388-0"></span>**4.6.7.7. CurrentLevel Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current level of the valve as a percentage value, between fully closed and fully open. During a transition from one level to another level, the valve SHOULD keep this attribute updated to the best of its ability, in order to represent the actual level of the valve during the movement.

A value of 100 percent SHALL indicate the fully open position.

A value of 0 percent SHALL indicate the fully closed position.

A value of null SHALL indicate that the current state is not known.

### <span id="page-389-2"></span>**4.6.7.8. TargetLevel Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the target level of the valve as a percentage value, between fully closed and fully open.

The interpretation of the percentage value is the same as for the [CurrentLevel](#page-388-0) attribute.

A value of null SHALL indicate that no target position is set, since the change of level is either done or failed.

# <span id="page-389-4"></span>**4.6.7.9. DefaultOpenLevel Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the default value used for the [TargetLevel](#page-389-2) attribute, when a valve transitions from the closed to the open state, caused by an [Open](#page-389-1) command, if a TargetLevel field is not present in the [Open](#page-389-1) command.

If the [LevelStep](#page-389-3) attribute is present and the value of a write interaction to this attribute field is not 100, the value SHALL be a supported value as defined by the [LevelStep](#page-389-3) attribute, such that (Value received in the write interaction) % (Value of [LevelStep](#page-389-3) attribute) equals 0. If the resulting value is not 0, the requested DefaultOpenLevel value is considered an unsupported value and a CON-STRAINT\_ERROR status SHALL be returned.

# <span id="page-389-5"></span>**4.6.7.10. ValveFault Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate any faults registered by the valve.

#### <span id="page-389-3"></span>**4.6.7.11. LevelStep Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the step size the valve can support.

The step size defined by this attribute is counted from 0 and the final step towards 100 MAY be different than what is defined in this attribute. For example, if the value of this attribute is 15, it results in these target values being supported; 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90 and 100.

The values of 0 and 100 SHALL always be supported, regardless of the value of this attribute.

# <span id="page-389-0"></span>**4.6.8. Commands**

| ID   | Name  | Direction       | Response | Access | Conformance |
|------|-------|-----------------|----------|--------|-------------|
| 0x00 | Open  | client ⇒ server | Y        | O      | M           |
| 0x01 | Close | client ⇒ server | Y        | O      | M           |

### <span id="page-389-1"></span>**4.6.8.1. Open Command**

This command is used to set the valve to its open position.

| ID | Name             | Type      | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------|-----------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | OpenDura<br>tion | elapsed-s | min 1      | X       |          | O               |
| 1  | TargetLevel      | percent   | min 1      |         |          | [LVL]           |

### **4.6.8.1.1. OpenDuration Field**

This field SHALL indicate the duration that the valve will remain open for this specific Open command.

A value of null SHALL indicate the duration is not set, meaning that the valve will remain open until closed by the user or some other automation.

#### **4.6.8.1.2. TargetLevel Field**

This field SHALL indicate the target level used for this specific Open command.

### **4.6.8.1.3. Effect on Receipt**

If the device has registered a fault, that prevents it from performing the requested action, the command SHALL be ignored and a FailureDueToFault status SHALL be returned.

The device SHALL set the [TargetState](#page-388-1) attribute to the Open value and set the [CurrentState](#page-388-2) attribute to the Transitioning value.

If the OpenDuration field is present, the value of the [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) attribute SHALL be set to the value of the OpenDuration field.

If the OpenDuration field is not present, the value of [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) attribute SHALL be set to the value of the [DefaultOpenDuration](#page-387-2) attribute.

If the [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) attribute is null, it SHALL indicate that there is no auto close defined for the current Open action and the device SHALL set the [RemainingDuration](#page-387-1) attribute to null. If the device supports the TimeSync feature, the device SHALL set the [AutoCloseTime](#page-387-3) attribute to null.

If the [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) attribute is not null, it indicates that an auto close duration is defined for the current open action and the device SHALL set the value of the [RemainingDuration](#page-387-1) attribute equal to the value of the [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) attribute. If the device supports the TimeSync feature, the device SHALL set the [AutoCloseTime](#page-387-3) attribute to the UTC value of the time when command was received plus the value of the [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) attribute.

If the [LevelStep](#page-389-3) attribute and the TargetLevel field are both present and the value of the TargetLevel field is not 100, the value of the TargetLevel field SHALL be a supported value as defined by the [LevelStep](#page-389-3) attribute, such that (Value of TargetLevel field) % (Value of [LevelStep](#page-389-3) attribute) equals 0. If the resulting value is not 0, the requested TargetLevel value is considered an unsupported value and a CONSTRAINT\_ERROR status SHALL be returned.

If the device supports the Level feature, the [TargetLevel](#page-389-2) attribute SHALL be set to the value of the TargetLevel field, if present. If the TargetLevel field is not present, the [TargetLevel](#page-389-2) attribute SHALL be set to the value of the [DefaultOpenLevel](#page-389-4) attribute, if implemented. If the [DefaultOpenLevel](#page-389-4) attribute is not present, the [TargetLevel](#page-389-2) attribute SHALL be set to 100.

When the relevant target and duration attributes have been set, the device SHALL start the movement towards the target value and start the countdown of the [RemainingDuration](#page-387-1) attribute. If the device supports the Level feature, the device SHALL update the [CurrentLevel](#page-388-0) attribute at the start of the movement, and SHOULD update it as appropriate during movement, especially if it is slow. When the movement is complete, the device SHALL set the [CurrentState](#page-388-2) attribute to the Open value.

### <span id="page-391-1"></span>**4.6.8.2. Close Command**

This command is used to set the valve to its closed position.

#### **4.6.8.2.1. Effect on Receipt**

If the device has registered a fault that causes it to prevent the valve to perform the requested action, the command SHALL be ignored and a FailureDueToFault status SHALL be returned.

The [OpenDuration](#page-387-0) and [RemainingDuration](#page-387-1) attribute SHALL be set to null.

If the device supports the TimeSync feature, the [AutoCloseTime](#page-387-3) attribute SHALL be set to null.

The device SHALL set the [TargetState](#page-388-1) attribute to the Closed value and set the [CurrentState](#page-388-2) attribute to the Transitioning value.

If the device supports the Level feature, it SHALL set the [TargetLevel](#page-389-2) attribute to 0.

When the relevant target attributes have been set, the device SHALL start the movement towards the target value. If the device supports the Level feature, the device SHALL update the [CurrentLevel](#page-388-0) attribute, accordingly during the movement. When the movement is complete, the device SHALL set the [CurrentState](#page-388-2) attribute to the Closed value.

#### **4.6.9.1. ValveStateChanged Event**
