# <span id="page-733-5"></span>**9.4.6. Attributes**

| ID     | Name               | Type | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|--------|--------------------|------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0000 | Support<br>edModes |      |            |         |          |        |                 |
| 0x0001 | Current<br>Mode    |      |            |         |          |        |                 |
| 0x0002 | StartUp<br>Mode    |      |            |         |          |        | X               |
| 0x0003 | OnMode             |      |            |         |          |        | X               |

### **9.4.6.1. SupportedModes Attribute**

At least one entry in the SupportedModes attribute SHALL include the Manual mode tag in the ModeTags field list.

Modes with entries in the SupportedModes attribute which contain multiple mode tags permitting charging or discharging under different conditions SHALL permit the charging or discharging to occur if any of the conditions are satisfied.

Modes SHALL NOT have both the Manual tag and the TimeOfUse or SolarCharging tags defined in the SupportedModes attribute.

# <span id="page-734-0"></span>**9.4.7. Derived Cluster Namespace**

This namespace includes definitions for data associated exclusively with the derived cluster.

#### **9.4.7.1. Mode Tags**

The following table defines the base and derived-cluster-specific ModeTag values.

| Mode Tag Value | Name      |  |  |
|----------------|-----------|--|--|
| 0x0000         | Auto      |  |  |
| 0x0001         | Quick     |  |  |
| 0x0002         | Quiet     |  |  |
| 0x0003         | LowNoise  |  |  |
| 0x0004         | LowEnergy |  |  |
| 0x0005         | Vacation  |  |  |
| 0x0006         | Min       |  |  |
| 0x0007         | Max       |  |  |
| 0x0008         | Night     |  |  |
| 0x0009         | Day       |  |  |
| 0x4000         | Manual    |  |  |

| Mode Tag Value | Name          |  |
|----------------|---------------|--|
| 0x4001         | TimeOfUse     |  |
| 0x4002         | SolarCharging |  |
| 0x4003         | V2X           |  |

## **9.4.7.1.1. Manual Tag**

While in modes with this tag, and once enabled with the EnableCharging command, the EVSE will permit charging based on demand from the EV.

#### **9.4.7.1.2. TimeOfUse Tag**

While in modes with this tag, and once enabled with the EnableCharging command, the EVSE will attempt to automatically start charging based on the user's charging targets (for example, set based on a Time of Use tariff to charge at the cheapest times of the day).

### **9.4.7.1.3. SolarCharging Tag**

While in modes with this tag, and once enabled with the EnableCharging, the EVSE will attempt to automatically start charging based on available excess solar PV generation, limiting the charging power to avoid importing energy from the grid.

#### **9.4.7.1.4. V2X Tag**

While in modes with this tag, and once enabled with the EnableDischarging command, the EVSE will permit discharging based on the current charge state of the EV, and its control from an associated Device Energy Management cluster.

**NOTE**

being in a mode with this tag set or not does not affect the handling of the EnableDischarging command by the Energy EVSE cluster, but once enabled, only modes with this tag enable the discharging to actually occur.

# <span id="page-735-1"></span>**9.5. Water Heater Management Cluster**

This cluster is used to allow clients to control the operation of a hot water heating appliance so that

it can be used with energy management.

Heating of hot water is one of the main energy uses in homes, and when coupled with the Energy Management cluster, it can help consumers save cost (e.g. using power at cheaper times or from local solar PV generation).

| 2        | Added events and simplified data types |  |

# <span id="page-736-4"></span>**9.5.5. Dependencies**

This cluster SHALL be on an endpoint that also includes the Thermostat cluster as this cluster is dependent on the Thermostat cluster.

|----|---------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|---------|----------|--------|------------------------|
| 0  | Duration                  | elapsed-s       | min 1                        |         |          |        | M                      |
| 1  | OneShot                   | bool            | all                          |         | False    |        | [!TP],<br>[TP].a       |
| 2  | Emergen<br>cyBoost        | bool            | all                          |         | False    |        | O                      |

| 5  | TargetRe<br>heat          | percent         | max Tar<br>getPercent<br>age |         |          |        | [TP].a                 |

#### <span id="page-738-4"></span>**9.5.6.3.1. Duration Field**

This field SHALL indicate the time period, in seconds, for which the boost state is activated.

### <span id="page-738-3"></span>**9.5.6.3.2. OneShot Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the boost state SHALL be automatically canceled once the hot water has reached either:

- the set point temperature (from the thermostat cluster)
- the [TemporarySetpoint](#page-738-0) temperature (if specified)
- the [TargetPercentage](#page-738-1) (if specified).

#### **9.5.6.3.3. EmergencyBoost Field**

This field SHALL indicate that the consumer wants the water to be heated quickly. This MAY cause multiple heat sources to be activated (e.g. a heat pump and direct electric immersion heating element).

The choice of which heat sources are activated is manufacturer specific.

#### <span id="page-738-0"></span>**9.5.6.3.4. TemporarySetpoint Field**

This field SHALL indicate the target temperature to which the water will be heated.

If included, it SHALL be used instead of the thermostat cluster set point temperature whilst the boost state is activated.

The value of this field SHALL be within the constraints of the MinHeatSetpointLimit and MaxHeat-SetpointLimit attributes (inclusive), of the thermostat cluster.

#### <span id="page-738-1"></span>**9.5.6.3.5. TargetPercentage Field**

This field SHALL indicate the target percentage of hot water in the tank that the TankPercentage attribute must reach before the heating is switched off.

#### <span id="page-738-2"></span>**9.5.6.3.6. TargetReheat Field**

This field SHALL indicate the percentage to which the hot water in the tank SHALL be allowed to fall before again beginning to reheat it.

For example if the [TargetPercentage](#page-738-1) was 80%, and the [TargetReheat](#page-738-2) was 40%, then after initial heating to 80% hot water, the tank may have hot water drawn off until only 40% hot water remains. At this point the heater will begin to heat back up to 80% of hot water. If this field and the [OneShot](#page-738-3) field were both omitted, heating would begin again after any water draw which reduced the [TankPercentage](#page-740-0) below 80%.

This field SHALL be less than or equal to the [TargetPercentage](#page-738-1) field.

# <span id="page-739-0"></span>**9.5.7. Attributes**

| ID     | Name                          | Type                                        | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|--------|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0000 | Heater<br>Types               | Water<br>Heater<br>Heat<br>SourceBit<br>map | all        | F       |          | R V    | M               |
| 0x0001 | HeatDe<br>mand                | Water<br>Heater<br>Heat<br>SourceBit<br>map | all        |         |          | R V    | M               |
| 0x0002 | TankVol<br>ume                | uint16                                      | all        |         |          | R V    | EM              |
| 0x0003 | Estimated<br>HeatRe<br>quired | energy<br>mWh                               | min 0      |         |          | R V    | EM              |
| 0x0004 | TankPer<br>centage            | percent                                     | all        |         |          | R V    | TP              |
| 0x0005 | BoostState                    | BoostSta<br>teEnum                          | all        |         |          | R V    | M               |

#### **9.5.7.1. HeaterTypes Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the heat sources that the water heater can call on for heating. If a bit is set then the water heater supports the corresponding heat source.

# **9.5.7.2. HeatDemand Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate if the water heater is heating water. If a bit is set then the corresponding heat source is active.

### **9.5.7.3. TankVolume Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the volume of water that the hot water tank can hold (in units of Litres). This allows an energy management system to estimate the required heating energy needed to reach the target temperature.

# **9.5.7.4. EstimatedHeatRequired Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the estimated heat energy needed to raise the water temperature to the target setpoint. This can be computed by taking the specific heat capacity of water (4182 J/kg °C) and by knowing the current temperature of the water, the tank volume and target temperature.

For example, if the target temperature was 60°C, the current temperature was 20°C and the tank volume was 100L:

```
Mass of water = 1kg per Litre
Total Mass = 100 x 1kg = 100kg
Δ Temperature = (target temperature - current temperature)
  = (60°C - 20°C) = 40°C
Energy required to
heat the water to 60°C = 4182 x 40 x 100 = 16,728,000 J
```

```
Converting Joules in to Wh of heat (divide by 3600):
  = 16,728,000 J / 3600
  = 4647 Wh (4.65kWh)
```

If the TankPercent feature is supported, then this estimate SHALL also take into account the percentage of the water in the tank which is already hot.

**NOTE**

The electrical energy required to heat the water depends on the heating system used to heat the water. For example, a direct electric immersion heating element can be close to 100% efficient, so the electrical energy needed to heat the hot water is nearly the same as the EstimatedHeatEnergyRequired. However some forms of heating, such as an air-source heat pump which extracts heat from ambient air, requires much less electrical energy to heat hot water. Heat pumps can be produce 3kWh of heat output for 1kWh of electrical energy input. The conversion between heat energy and electrical energy is outside the scope of this cluster.

### <span id="page-740-0"></span>**9.5.7.5. TankPercentage Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate an approximate level of hot water stored in the tank, which might help consumers understand the amount of hot water remaining in the tank. The accuracy of this attribute is manufacturer specific.

In most hot water tanks, there is a stratification effect where the hot water layer rests above a cooler layer of water below. For this reason cold water is fed in at the bottom of the tank and the hot water is drawn from the top.

Some water tanks might use multiple temperature probes to estimate the level of the hot water layer. A water heater with multiple temperature probes is likely to implement an algorithm to estimate the hot water tank percentage by taking into account the temperature values of each probe to determine the height of the hot water.

However it might be possible with a single temperature probe to estimate how much hot water is left using a simpler algorithm:

For example, if the target temperature was 60°C, the CurrentTemperature was 40°C from a single temperature probe measuring the average water temperature and the temperature of incoming cold water (COLD\_WATER\_TEMP) was assumed to be 20°C:

```
TankPercentage = int(((current temperature - COLD_WATER_TEMP) / (target
temperature - COLD_WATER_TEMP)) * 100)
TankPercentage = min( max(TankPercentage,0), 100)
```

TankPercentage = 50%

#### <span id="page-741-2"></span>**9.5.7.6. BoostState Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate whether the Boost, as triggered by a [Boost](#page-741-1) command, is currently Active or Inactive.

See [Section 9.5.8.1, "Boost Command"](#page-741-1) and [Section 9.5.8.2, "CancelBoost Command"](#page-742-1) for more details.

# <span id="page-741-0"></span>**9.5.8. Commands**

| ID   | Name        | Direction       | Response | Access | Conformance |
|------|-------------|-----------------|----------|--------|-------------|
| 0x00 | Boost       | client ⇒ server | Y        | M      | M           |
| 0x01 | CancelBoost | client ⇒ server | Y        | M      | M           |

### <span id="page-741-1"></span>**9.5.8.1. Boost Command**

Allows a client to request that the water heater is put into a Boost state.

| ID | Name      | Type        | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------|-------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | BoostInfo | Water       | all        |         |          | M               |
|    |           | HeaterBoost |            |         |          |                 |
|    |           | InfoStruct  |            |         |          |                 |

#### **9.5.8.1.1. Effect on receipt**

On receipt of this command, this SHALL allow the water heater to attempt to heat the water, which may override other settings, for example, if the Water Heater Mode is set to Off, or Timed and it is during one of the Off periods.

If the duration field is too short for the water heater to accept, for example a heat pump may take several minutes to ramp up in operation, then the boost command SHALL be rejected with a status of INVALID\_IN\_STATE.

If successful, the value of the [BoostState](#page-741-2) attribute SHALL transition to Active, and a response with

status of SUCCESS SHALL be returned, and a [BoostStarted](#page-742-2) event SHALL be generated to include the field values received in the command.

The water in the tank SHALL be heated until one of the following conditions is met:

- the temperature reaches the set point in the corresponding thermostat cluster or the [Tempo](#page-738-0)[rarySetpoint](#page-738-0) (if included)
- the [TankPercentage](#page-740-0) attribute value reaches the [TargetPercentage](#page-738-1) (if it was included)

If [OneShot](#page-738-3) is specified then once the hot water has reached the set point temperature (or the [Tem](#page-738-0)[porarySetpoint](#page-738-0) temperature, if specified) or the [TargetPercentage](#page-738-1) (if specified), or the boost command's duration times out after the specified [Duration](#page-738-4), then [BoostState](#page-741-2) transitions to Inactive. This SHALL cause the [BoostEnded](#page-743-6) event to be generated.

If the Water Heater was already in the [BoostState](#page-741-2) 'Active' when this command is received, it SHALL continue in this [BoostState,](#page-741-2) but SHALL discard the effect of the values of the fields from the previous [Boost](#page-741-1) commands, and SHALL continue with the values of the fields from the new [Boost](#page-741-1) command. A new [BoostStarted](#page-742-2) event SHALL be generated to include the field values received in the new command.

### <span id="page-742-1"></span>**9.5.8.2. CancelBoost Command**

Allows a client to cancel an ongoing Boost operation.

This command has no payload.

### **9.5.8.2.1. Effect on receipt**

If the [BoostState](#page-741-2) attribute value was already Inactive when this command is received, the [Boost-](#page-741-2)[State](#page-741-2) attribute value shall remain Inactive and the server SHALL return SUCCESS.

Otherwise the Water Heater SHALL transition the [BoostState](#page-741-2) to Inactive, generate a [BoostEnded](#page-743-6) event, and the water heating reverts to being controlled through the current Water Heater Mode (e.g. Off, Manual or Timed).

# <span id="page-742-0"></span>**9.5.9. Events**

| ID   | Name         | Priority | Quality | Access | Conformance |
|------|--------------|----------|---------|--------|-------------|
| 0x00 | BoostStarted | INFO     |         | V      | M           |
| 0x01 | BoostEnded   | INFO     |         | V      | M           |

### <span id="page-742-2"></span>**9.5.9.1. BoostStarted Event**

This event SHALL be generated whenever a [Boost](#page-741-1) command is accepted.

| ID | Name      | Type                               | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------|------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | BoostInfo | Water<br>HeaterBoost<br>InfoStruct | all        |         |          | M               |

The corresponding structure fields within the [WaterHeaterBoostInfoStruct](#page-737-3) are copied from the [Boost](#page-741-1) command.

### <span id="page-743-6"></span>**9.5.9.2. BoostEnded Event**

This event SHALL be generated whenever the [BoostState](#page-741-2) transitions from Active to Inactive.

### **9.6.7.1.1. Off Tag**

While in modes with this tag, the device will not attempt to keep the water warm.

#### **9.6.7.1.2. Manual Tag**

While in modes with this tag, the device will attempt to keep the water warm based on the OccupiedHeatingSetpoint attribute of the associated Thermostat cluster.

#### **9.6.7.1.3. Timed Tag**

While in modes with this tag, the device will attempt to keep the water warm based on the Schedules attribute of the associated Thermostat cluster.

| Bit | Code | Feature                     | Conformance | Summary                                                                 |
|-----|------|-----------------------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0   | BALA | EnergyBalance               | O.a+        | Device can bal<br>ance energy con<br>sumption vs.<br>another priority   |

# **9.7.4.1. EnergyBalance Feature**

This feature allows a user to select from a list of energy balances with associated descriptions of which strategies a device will use to target the specified balance.

# **9.7.4.2. LowPowerModeSensitivity Feature**

This feature allows the user to select a condition or set of conditions which will cause the device to switch to a mode using less power. For example, a device might provide a scale of durations that must elapse without user interaction before it goes to sleep.

# <span id="page-746-4"></span>**9.7.5. Data Types**

### <span id="page-747-1"></span>**9.7.5.1. EnergyPriorityEnum Type**

This data type is derived from enum8.

| Value | Name             | Summary                                     | Conformance |
|-------|------------------|---------------------------------------------|-------------|
| 0     | Comfort          | User comfort                                | M           |
| 1     | Speed            | Speed of operation                          | M           |
| 2     | Efficiency       | Amount of Energy con<br>sumed by the device | M           |
| 3     | WaterConsumption | Amount of water con<br>sumed by the device  | M           |

#### **9.7.5.1.1. Comfort Value**

This value SHALL emphasize user comfort; e.g. local temperature for a thermostat.

#### **9.7.5.1.2. Speed Value**

This value SHALL emphasize how quickly a device accomplishes its targeted use; e.g. how quickly a robot vacuum completes a cleaning cycle.

#### **9.7.5.1.3. Efficiency Value**

This value SHALL emphasize how much energy a device uses; e.g. electricity usage for a Pump.

### **9.7.5.1.4. Water consumption Value**

This value SHALL emphasize how much water is consumed during device use; e.g. how much water a dishwasher uses during a cleaning cycle.

# <span id="page-747-0"></span>**9.7.5.2. BalanceStruct Type**

This represents a step along a scale of preferences.

| ID | Name  | Type    | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-------|---------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Step  | percent | all        | F       |          |        | M               |

This field SHALL indicate the relative value of this step.

#### **9.7.5.2.2. Label Field**

This field SHALL indicate an optional string explaining which actions a device might take at the given step value.

# <span id="page-748-0"></span>**9.7.6. Attributes**

| ID     | Name                                       | Type                             | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|--------|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0000 | Energy<br>Balances                         | list[Bal<br>anceStruct]          | 2 to 10    | F       |          | R V    | BALA            |
| 0x0001 | Cur<br>rentEner<br>gyBalance               | uint8                            | all        | N       |          | RW VO  | BALA            |
| 0x0002 | EnergyPri<br>orities                       | list[Ener<br>gyPriori<br>tyEnum] | 2          | F       |          | R V    | BALA            |
| 0x0003 | LowPow<br>erMode<br>Sensitivi<br>ties      | list[Bal<br>anceStruct]          | 2 to 10    | F       |          | R V    | LPMS            |
| 0x0004 | Current<br>LowPow<br>erMode<br>Sensitivity | uint8                            | all        | N       |          | RW VO  | LPMS            |

### <span id="page-748-1"></span>**9.7.6.1. EnergyBalances Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a list of [BalanceStructs,](#page-747-0) each representing a step along a linear scale of relative priorities. A [Step](#page-747-2) field with a value of zero SHALL indicate that the device SHOULD entirely favor the priority specified by the first element in [EnergyPriorities](#page-749-1); whereas a [Step](#page-747-2) field with a value of 100 SHALL indicate that the device SHOULD entirely favor the priority specified by the second element in [EnergyPriorities](#page-749-1). The midpoint value of 50 SHALL indicate an even split between the two priorities.

This SHALL contain at least two [BalanceStructs](#page-747-0).

Each [BalanceStruct](#page-747-0) SHALL have a [Step](#page-747-2) field larger than the [Step](#page-747-2) field on the previous [BalanceStruct](#page-747-0) in the list.

The first [BalanceStruct](#page-747-0) SHALL have a [Step](#page-747-2) value of zero, and the last [BalanceStruct](#page-747-0) SHALL have a [Step](#page-747-2) value of 100.

#### <span id="page-748-2"></span>**9.7.6.2. CurrentEnergyBalance Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current preference of the user for balancing different priorities during device use. The value of this attribute is the index, 0-based, into the [EnergyBalances](#page-748-1) attribute for the currently selected balance.

If an attempt is made to set this attribute to an index outside the maximum index for [EnergyBal](#page-748-1)[ances](#page-748-1), a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If the value of [EnergyBalances](#page-748-1) changes after an update, the device SHALL migrate the value of the CurrentEnergyBalance attribute to the index which the manufacturer specifies most closely matches the previous value, while preserving extreme preferences as follows:

- 1. If the previous value of [CurrentEnergyBalance](#page-748-2) was zero, indicating a total preference for the priority specified by the first element in [EnergyPriorities](#page-749-1), the new value of [CurrentEnergyBal](#page-748-2)[ance](#page-748-2) SHALL also be zero.
- 2. If the previous value of [CurrentEnergyBalance](#page-748-2) was the index of the last [BalanceStruct](#page-747-0) in the previous value of [EnergyBalances](#page-748-1), indicating a total preference for the priority specified by the last element in [EnergyPriorities](#page-749-1), the new value of [CurrentEnergyBalance](#page-748-2) SHALL be the index of the last element in the updated value of [EnergyBalances.](#page-748-1)

### <span id="page-749-1"></span>**9.7.6.3. EnergyPriorities Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate two extremes for interpreting the values in the [EnergyBalances](#page-748-1) attribute. These two priorities SHALL be in opposition to each other; e.g. Comfort vs. Efficiency or Speed vs. WaterConsumption.

If the value of [EnergyPriorities](#page-749-1) changes after an update to represent a new balance between priorities, the value of the [CurrentEnergyBalance](#page-748-2) attribute SHALL be set to its default.

# <span id="page-749-2"></span>**9.7.6.4. LowPowerModeSensitivities Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a list of [BalanceStructs,](#page-747-0) each representing a condition or set of conditions for the device to enter a low power mode.

This SHALL contain at least two [BalanceStructs.](#page-747-0)

Each [BalanceStruct](#page-747-0) SHALL have a [Step](#page-747-2) field larger than the [Step](#page-747-2) field on the previous [BalanceStruct](#page-747-0) in the list.

### **9.7.6.5. CurrentLowPowerModeSensitivity Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current preference of the user for determining when the device should enter a low power mode. The value of this attribute is the index, 0-based, into the [LowPow](#page-749-2)[erModeSensitivities](#page-749-2) attribute for the currently selected preference.

If an attempt is made to set this attribute to an index outside the maximum index for [LowPower-](#page-749-2)[ModeSensitivities](#page-749-2), a response with the status code CONSTRAINT\_ERROR SHALL be returned.

If the value of [LowPowerModeSensitivities](#page-749-2) changes after an update, the device SHALL migrate the value of the LowPowerModeSensitivity attribute to the index which the manufacturer specifies most closely matches the previous value.

# <span id="page-749-0"></span>**9.8. Device Energy Management Mode Cluster**

This cluster is derived from the Mode Base cluster and defines additional mode tags and namespaced enumerated values for Device Energy Management devices.

#### **9.8.5.1. ModeOptionStruct Type**

The table below lists the changes relative to the Mode Base cluster for the fields of the ModeOption-Struct type. A blank field indicates no change.

| ID | Name     | Type | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|----------|------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Label    |      |            |         |          |        | M               |

# <span id="page-750-5"></span>**9.8.6. Attributes**

| ID     | Name               | Type | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|--------|--------------------|------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0000 | Support<br>edModes |      |            |         |          |        |                 |
| 0x0001 | Current<br>Mode    |      |            |         |          |        |                 |
| 0x0002 | StartUp<br>Mode    |      |            |         |          |        | X               |
| 0x0003 | OnMode             |      |            |         |          |        | X               |

### **9.8.6.1. SupportedModes Attribute**

At least one entry in the SupportedModes attribute SHALL include the NoOptimization mode tag in the ModeTags field.

At least one entry in the SupportedModes attribute SHALL include the LocalOptimization mode tag in the ModeTags field list.

At least one entry in the SupportedModes attribute SHALL include the GridOptimization mode tag in the ModeTags field list.

An entry in the SupportedModes attribute that includes one of an DeviceOptimization, LocalOptimization, or GridOptimization tags SHALL NOT also include NoOptimization tag.

# <span id="page-751-0"></span>**9.8.7. Derived Cluster Namespace**

This namespace includes definitions for data associated exclusively with the derived cluster.

## **9.8.7.1. Mode Tags**

The following table defines the base and derived-cluster-specific ModeTag values.

| Mode Tag Value | Name      |
|----------------|-----------|
| 0x0000         | Auto      |
| 0x0001         | Quick     |
| 0x0002         | Quiet     |
| 0x0003         | LowNoise  |
| 0x0004         | LowEnergy |
| 0x0005         | Vacation  |
| 0x0006         | Min       |
| 0x0007         | Max       |
| 0x0008         | Night     |
| 0x0009         | Day       |

| Mode Tag Value | Name               |
|----------------|--------------------|
| 0x4000         | NoOptimization     |
| 0x4001         | DeviceOptimization |
| 0x4002         | LocalOptimization  |
| 0x4003         | GridOptimization   |

#### **9.8.7.1.1. NoOptimization Tag**

The device prohibits optimization of energy usage management: its energy usage is determined only by the user configuration and internal device needs.

### **9.8.7.1.2. DeviceOptimization Tag**

The device is permitted to manage its own energy usage. For example, using tariff information it may obtain.

#### **9.8.7.1.3. LocalOptimization Tag**

The device permits management of energy usage by an energy manager to optimize the local energy usage.

#### **9.8.7.1.4. GridOptimization Tag**

The device permits management of energy usage by an energy manager to optimize the grid energy usage.

# <span id="page-752-0"></span>**9.8.8. Mode Examples**

A few examples of Device Energy Management modes and their mode tags are provided below.

- For the "No Energy Management (Forecast reporting only)" mode, tags: 0x4000 (NoOptimization).
- For the "Device Energy Management" mode, tags: 0x4001 (DeviceOptimization).
- For the "Home Energy Management" mode, tags: 0x4001 (DeviceOptimization), 0x4002 (LocalOptimization).
- For the "Grid Energy Management" mode, tags: 0x4003 (GridOptimization).
- For the "Full Energy Management" mode, tags: 0x4001 (DeviceOptimization), 0x4002 (LocalOptimization), 0x4003 (GridOptimization).

# <span id="page-752-1"></span>**9.9. Commodity Price Cluster**

The Commodity Price Cluster provides the mechanism for communicating Gas, Energy, or Water pricing information within the premises.

| 3        | CCBs 2043 2706 2810 2912 3566                       |
| 4        | Initial Matter revision                             |

# <span id="page-753-1"></span>**9.9.2. Classification**

| Hierarchy | Role        | Scope    | PICS Code |
|-----------|-------------|----------|-----------|
| Base      | Application | Endpoint | SEPR      |

# <span id="page-753-2"></span>**9.9.3. Cluster ID**

| ID     | Name            |
|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0095 | Commodity Price |

# <span id="page-753-3"></span>**9.9.4. Features**

This cluster SHALL support the FeatureMap bitmap attribute as defined below.

| Bit | Code | Feature     | Conformance | Summary                        |
|-----|------|-------------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| 0   | FORE | Forecasting | O           | Forecasts upcom<br>ing pricing |

# <span id="page-753-4"></span>**9.9.5. Data Types**

#### <span id="page-753-5"></span>**9.9.5.1. CommodityPriceDetailBitmap Type**

This data type is derived from map16.

| Bit | Name        | Summary                                                                                 | Conformance |
|-----|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| 0   | Description | A textual description of<br>a price; e.g. the name of<br>a rate plan.                   | M           |
| 1   | Components  | A breakdown of the<br>component parts of a<br>price; e.g. generation,<br>delivery, etc. | M           |

## <span id="page-754-2"></span>**9.9.5.2. CommodityPriceComponentStruct Type**

This represents a component of a given price; it is only used in the [Components](#page-755-0) field.

| ID | Name                      | Type                    | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------------|-------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Price                     | money                   | all        |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | Source                    | TariffPrice<br>TypeEnum | all        |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | Descrip<br>tion           | string                  | max 32     |         |          |        | O               |
| 3  | Tariff<br>Compo<br>nentID | uint32                  | all        |         |          |        | O               |

#### <span id="page-754-1"></span>**9.9.5.2.1. Price Field**

This field SHALL indicate the component price of the commodity per [TariffUnit](#page-756-1), with the currency indicated by the currency of the [Price](#page-755-1) field of the parent [CommodityPriceStruct](#page-754-0).

#### **9.9.5.2.2. PriceLevel Field**

This field SHALL indicate the tariff component price level.

#### **9.9.5.2.3. Source Field**

This field SHALL indicate the source of the price component.

#### **9.9.5.2.4. Description Field**

This field SHALL indicate a description of the pricing plan yielding the value of the [Price](#page-754-1) field. For example, this field may contain the name of the current block of the selected billing plan, or the name of the time of usage tier.

### **9.9.5.2.5. TariffComponentID Field**

This field SHALL indicate the [ID](#page-774-0) of the associated [TariffComponent](#page-773-0) for this price component. If there is no associated TariffComponent, this field SHALL be omitted.

## <span id="page-754-0"></span>**9.9.5.3. CommodityPriceStruct Type**

This represents a price over a given period.

| ID | Name            | Type    | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------------|---------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Period<br>Start | epoch-s | all        |         |          |        | M               |

| ID | Name            | Type                                                | Constraint                | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 1  | PeriodEnd       | epoch-s                                             | min (Peri<br>odStart + 1) | X       |          |        | M               |
| 2  | Price           | money                                               | all                       |         |          |        | O.b+            |
| 3  | PriceLevel      | int16                                               | all                       |         |          |        | O.b+            |
| 4  | Descrip<br>tion | string                                              | max 32                    |         |          |        | O               |
| 5  | Compo<br>nents  | list[Com<br>modi<br>tyPrice<br>Compo<br>nentStruct] | max 10                    |         | empty    |        | [Price]         |

#### <span id="page-755-5"></span>**9.9.5.3.1. PeriodStart Field**

This field SHALL indicate the beginning timestamp in UTC of the period covered by the price indicated in the [Price](#page-755-1) field, or the price level indicated in the [Price Level](#page-755-2) field, or both.

### <span id="page-755-4"></span>**9.9.5.3.2. PeriodEnd Field**

This field SHALL indicate the ending timestamp in UTC of the period covered by the price indicated in the [Price](#page-755-1) field, or the price level indicated in the [Price Level](#page-755-2) field, or both.

If this field is null, then the period has no definite end.

#### <span id="page-755-1"></span>**9.9.5.3.3. Price Field**

This field SHALL indicate the price of the commodity per [TariffUnit](#page-756-1).

#### <span id="page-755-2"></span>**9.9.5.3.4. PriceLevel Field**

This field SHALL indicate the tariff price level.

#### <span id="page-755-3"></span>**9.9.5.3.5. Description Field**

This field SHALL indicate a description of the pricing plan yielding the value of the [Price](#page-755-1) field, or the [Price Level](#page-755-2) field. For example, this field may contain the name of the selected billing plan.

#### <span id="page-755-0"></span>**9.9.5.3.6. Components Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of the components that comprise the value in the [Price](#page-755-1) field. For example, if a pricing plan has a base price and a surcharge for a given time of day, it may have two entries in the Components field.

If this field is not empty, the [Price](#page-754-1) fields in the list SHALL sum to the value in the [Price](#page-755-1) field.

# <span id="page-756-0"></span>**9.9.6. Attributes**

| ID     | Name              | Type                                   | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|--------|-------------------|----------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0000 | TariffUnit        | TariffU<br>nitEnum                     | all        |         |          | R V    | M               |
| 0x0001 | Currency          | currency                               | all        | X       |          | R V    | M               |
| 0x0002 | Current<br>Price  | Commodi<br>tyPriceS<br>truct           | all        | X       |          | R V    | M               |
| 0x0003 | PriceFore<br>cast | list[Com<br>modi<br>tyPriceS<br>truct] | max 56     |         |          | R V    | FORE            |

### <span id="page-756-1"></span>**9.9.6.1. TariffUnit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the unit of measure for all pricing reported by this cluster.

# **9.9.6.2. Currency Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the currency for all pricing reported by this cluster. If the current currency is unknown, or cannot be determined, the value SHALL be null.

# <span id="page-756-2"></span>**9.9.6.3. CurrentPrice Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current price. If the current price is unknown, or cannot be determined, the value SHALL be null.

The [Description](#page-755-3) and [Components](#page-755-0) fields SHALL be omitted in this attribute's value.

# <span id="page-756-3"></span>**9.9.6.4. PriceForecast Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the forecast of upcoming price changes. If the forecast is unable to be determined, this list SHALL be empty.

The list entries SHALL be in time order:

- All entries except the last one SHALL have a non-null [PeriodEnd](#page-755-4).
- For all entries except the first one, [PeriodStart](#page-755-5) SHALL be greater than the previous entry's [Peri](#page-755-4)[odEnd](#page-755-4).

The [Description](#page-755-3) and [Components](#page-755-0) fields SHALL be omitted from [CommodityPriceStruct](#page-754-0)s in this attribute's value.

If the [PeriodEnd](#page-755-4) field is null on the value of the [CurrentPrice](#page-756-2) attribute, then this list SHALL be empty.

# <span id="page-757-0"></span>**9.9.7. Commands**

| ID   | Name                                    | Direction          | Response                            | Access | Quality | Confor<br>mance                    |
|------|-----------------------------------------|--------------------|-------------------------------------|--------|---------|------------------------------------|
| 0x00 | GetDe<br>tailed<br>PriceReques<br>t     | client ⇒<br>server | GetDetailed<br>PriceRe<br>sponse    | O      |         | O                                  |
| 0x01 | GetDe<br>tailed<br>PriceRe<br>sponse    | client ⇐<br>server | N                                   |        |         | GetDetailed<br>PriceRequest        |
| 0x02 | GetDe<br>tailedFore<br>castRequest      | client ⇒<br>server | GetDetailed<br>ForecastRe<br>sponse | O      | L       | [FORE]                             |
| 0x03 | GetDe<br>tailedFore<br>castRe<br>sponse | client ⇐<br>server | N                                   |        | L       | GetDetailed<br>ForecastRe<br>quest |

# **9.9.7.1. GetDetailedPriceRequest Command**

Upon receipt, this SHALL generate a GetDetailedPrice Response command.

| ID | Name    | Type                               | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------|------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | Details | Commodi<br>tyPriceDe<br>tailBitmap | all        |         |          | M               |

#### <span id="page-757-1"></span>**9.9.7.1.1. Details Field**

This field SHALL indicate which fields on the [CommodityPriceStruct](#page-754-0) in the [GetDetailedPriceRespon](#page-758-1)[seCurrentPrice](#page-758-1) field will be included.

### **9.9.7.2. GetDetailedPriceResponse Command**

This command SHALL be generated in response to a GetDetailedPrice Request command. The data for this command SHALL be as follows:

| ID | Name             | Type                     | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------|--------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | Current<br>Price | Commodi<br>tyPriceStruct | all        | X       |          | M               |

#### <span id="page-758-1"></span>**9.9.7.2.1. CurrentPrice Field**

This field SHALL indicate the current price. Unlike the value returned from the [CurrentPrice](#page-756-2) attribute, the [Description](#page-755-3) and [Components](#page-755-0) fields MAY be populated based on the value of the [Get-](#page-757-1)[DetailedPriceRequestDetails](#page-757-1) field.

If the current price is unknown, or cannot be determined, the value SHALL be null.

### **9.9.7.3. GetDetailedForecastRequest Command**

Upon receipt, this SHALL generate a GetDetailedForecast Response command.

| ID | Name    | Type                               | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------|------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | Details | Commodi<br>tyPriceDe<br>tailBitmap | all        |         |          | M               |

#### **9.9.7.3.1. Details Field**

This field SHALL indicate which fields on the [CommodityPriceStructs](#page-754-0) in the [GetDetailedForecastRe](#page-758-2)[sponsePriceForecast](#page-758-2) field will be included.

# **9.9.7.4. GetDetailedForecastResponse Command**

This command SHALL be generated in response to a GetDetailedForecast Request command. The data for this command SHALL be as follows:

| ID | Name              | Type                                   | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-------------------|----------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | PriceFore<br>cast | list[Com<br>modi<br>tyPriceS<br>truct] | max 56     |         |          | M               |

# <span id="page-758-2"></span>**9.9.7.4.1. PriceForecast Field**

This field SHALL indicate the current forecast of upcoming price changes. Unlike the value returned from the [PriceForecast](#page-756-3) attribute, the [Description](#page-755-3) and [Components](#page-755-0) fields MAY be populated on each [CommodityPriceStruct](#page-754-0) based on the value of the [GetDetailedPriceRequestDetails](#page-757-1) field.

If the forecast is unable to be determined, this list SHALL be empty.

#### **9.9.8.1.1. CurrentPrice Field**

This field SHALL be the new value of the [CurrentPrice](#page-756-2) attribute.

This attribute SHALL indicate the Meter type features, decided by manufacturer. If the type is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

This attribute SHALL indicate the unique identification of the connection point for the premises for billing purposes. If the point of delivery is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

# **9.10.6.3. MeterSerialNumber Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the serial number of the meter. If the serial number is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

### **9.10.6.4. ProtocolVersion Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the underlying protocol version to express local market features. If the protocol version is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

#### **9.10.6.4.1. PowerThreshold Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum instantaneous power demand that can be distributed to the customer without any risk of overload. If the maximum instantaneous power demand is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

# <span id="page-762-2"></span>**9.11.5.1. MeteredQuantity Attribute**

The most recent summed value of a commodity delivered to and consumed in the premises. A null value indicates that metering data is currently unavailable.

#### **9.11.5.2. MeteredQuantityTimestamp Attribute**

The timestamp in UTC for when the value of the [MeteredQuantity](#page-762-2) attribute was last updated. A null value indicates that metering data is currently unavailable.

## **9.11.5.3. TariffUnit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the unit for the [Quantity](#page-762-3) field on all [MeteredQuantityStructs](#page-761-5) in the [MeteredQuantity](#page-762-2) attribute. A null value indicates that metering data is currently unavailable.

#### **9.11.5.4. MaximumMeteredQuantities Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the maximum number of [MeteredQuantityStructs](#page-761-5) in the [MeteredQuantity](#page-762-2) attribute. A null value indicates that metering data is currently unavailable.

### <span id="page-766-1"></span>**9.12.5.9. CalendarPeriodStruct Type**

This represents a sub period of a calendar, commencing on its [StartDate](#page-767-0).

**NOTE**

A 'Calendar Period', while normally considered to be a 3 or 6 month period, could be used for other arbitrary periods e.g. monthly or quarterly. The minimum resolution is 1 day, although a week would normally be the smallest interval.

| ID | Name              | Type         | Constraint        | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-------------------|--------------|-------------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | StartDate         | epoch-s      | min Start<br>Date | X       |          |        | M               |
| 1  | DayPat<br>ternIDs | list[uint32] | 1 to 7            |         |          |        | M               |

#### <span id="page-767-0"></span>**9.12.5.9.1. StartDate Field**

This field SHALL indicate the timestamp in UTC when the calendar period becomes active.

A null value SHALL indicate the calendar period becomes active immediately. See [CalendarPeriods](#page-778-0) attribute.

#### <span id="page-767-2"></span>**9.12.5.9.2. DayPatternIDs Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of [DayPatternID](#page-771-0)s for the [DayPatternStructs](#page-771-1) in use during this calendar period.

If any of the [DayPatternStructs](#page-771-1) referenced by this list has no bits set in [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2), then none of the [DayPatternStruct](#page-771-1)s referenced by this list SHALL have any bits set, and the list SHALL be treated as a rotating set of days.

If at least one of the [DayPatternStructs](#page-771-1) referenced by this list has a bit set in [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2), then:

- 1. All of the [DayPatternStructs](#page-771-1) referenced by this list SHALL have at least one bit set in [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2)
- 2. No two [DayPatternStructs](#page-771-1) referenced by this list SHALL have the same bit set in [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2).
- 3. Every bit defined in [DayPatternDayOfWeekBitmap](#page-764-2) referenced by this list SHALL be set in [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2) on one of the [DayPatternStructs](#page-771-1).

Meeting these constraints ensures that every day of the week during this week has specified day entries, and no day of the week has more than one set of day entries.

# <span id="page-767-1"></span>**9.12.5.10. DayEntryStruct Type**

This struct represents a day entry at a particular time of day, along with an optional duration and randomization parameters.

| ID | Name           | Type   | Constraint                    | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|----------------|--------|-------------------------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | DayEn<br>tryID | uint32 | all                           |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | StartTime      | uint16 | max 1499                      |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | Duration       | uint16 | max (1500<br>- Start<br>Time) |         |          |        | O               |

| ID | Name                        | Type                                          | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 3  | Random<br>izationOff<br>set | int16                                         | all        |         |          |        | [RNDM]          |
| 4  | Random<br>ization<br>Type   | DayEn<br>tryRan<br>domiza<br>tionType<br>Enum | all        |         | None     |        | [RNDM]          |

#### <span id="page-768-1"></span>**9.12.5.10.1. DayEntryID Field**

This field SHALL indicate an identifier for the day entry which is unique on the server to a set of values:

- 1. If this identifier is included in the [DayEntryIDs](#page-771-3) associated with a [DayPatternStruct](#page-771-1), then the identifier SHALL be unique to the combination of:
  - a. the [StartTime](#page-768-0)
  - b. the [Duration](#page-769-0), if indicated
  - c. the [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2) field in the containing [DayPatternStruct](#page-771-1)
- 2. Otherwise, if this identifier is included in the [DayEntryIDs](#page-770-0) associated with a [DayStruct](#page-770-1), then the identifier SHALL be unique to the combination of:
  - a. the [StartTime](#page-768-0)
  - b. the [Duration](#page-769-0), if indicated
  - c. the [Date](#page-770-2) field in the containing [DayStruct](#page-770-1)

Once an identifier has been used for a given combination above, it SHALL never be used for any other combination of these values.

# <span id="page-768-0"></span>**9.12.5.10.2. StartTime Field**

This field SHALL indicate the start time of the [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1), expressed as the number of minutes that have elapsed since midnight on the associated days.

For example, 6am will be represented by 360 minutes since midnight and 11:30pm will be represented by 1410 minutes since midnight.

This will differ on days with a day entry in or out of daylight saving time. For example, if the implementation of daylight saving time in a region means that the hour between 2am and 3am will be skipped on the day entry into daylight saving time, then 2am cannot be represented, and 3am will be represented by 120 minutes.

Similarly, if the implementation of daylight saving time in a region means that the hour between 2am and 3am will be repeated on the date of day entry out of daylight saving time, then the first 2am will be represented by 120 minutes, while the second 2am will be represented by 180 minutes, and 4am will be represented by 300 minutes. As such, the maximum start time on this day is 1499, 60 minutes longer than all other days.

[DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) on daylight saving time days SHOULD be handled by a [DayStruct](#page-770-1) in the [Individual-](#page-778-1)[Days](#page-778-1) attribute whose [Date](#page-770-2) field indicates the date of the day entry.

#### <span id="page-769-0"></span>**9.12.5.10.3. Duration Field**

This field SHALL indicate the duration of the day entry, expressed as the number of minutes since the time indicated by the [StartTime](#page-768-0) field.

If this field is omitted, the day entry SHALL end at the [StartTime](#page-768-0) of the [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) identified by the next [DayEntryID](#page-768-1) in the containing list. If the [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) is the last item in the containing list, then the day entry SHALL last until the end of the day.

### <span id="page-769-2"></span>**9.12.5.10.4. RandomizationOffset Field**

This field SHALL indicate a randomization offset for this particular day entry in seconds. If this field is not indicated, randomization SHALL use the value in the [DefaultRandomizationOffset](#page-779-1) attribute.

- 1. If the value of the [RandomizationType](#page-769-1) field is Fixed, then the value of this field MAY be negative
- 2. Otherwise if the value of the [RandomizationType](#page-769-1) field is RandomNegative, then the value of this field SHALL be less than or equal to zero
- 3. Otherwise the value of this field SHALL be greater than or equal to zero

# <span id="page-769-1"></span>**9.12.5.10.5. RandomizationType Field**

This field SHALL indicate a randomization type for this particular day entry. If this field is not indicated, randomization SHALL use the value in the [DefaultRandomizationType](#page-779-2) attribute.

If the calculated value for this field is of type None, no randomization SHALL be applied to the start of this day entry.

If the calculated value for this field is of type Fixed, then the calculated value of the [Randomiza](#page-769-2)[tionOffset](#page-769-2) field SHALL be added to the start time of the day entry.

If the calculated value for this field is of type Random, then a random number of whole seconds whose absolute value is less than or equal to the calculated value of the [RandomizationOffset](#page-769-2) field SHALL be added to the start time of the day entry.

If the calculated value for this field is of type RandomPositive, then a random non-negative number of whole seconds whose value is less than or equal to the calculated value of the [RandomizationOff](#page-769-2)[set](#page-769-2) field SHALL be added to the start time of the day entry.

If the calculated value for this field is of type RandomNegative, then a random negative number of whole seconds whose value is greater than or equal to the calculated value of the [Randomiza](#page-769-2)[tionOffset](#page-769-2) field SHALL be added to the start time of the day entry.

### <span id="page-770-1"></span>**9.12.5.11. DayStruct Type**

This represents a series of day entries over the course of a day for a specific date.

| ID | Name            | Type            | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|-----------------|-----------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Date            | epoch-s         |            |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | DayType         | DayType<br>Enum | any        |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | DayEn<br>tryIDs | list[uint32]    | 1 to 96    |         |          |        | M               |

#### <span id="page-770-2"></span>**9.12.5.11.1. Date Field**

This field SHALL indicate the date the associated set of [DayEntryStructs](#page-767-1) applies to.

#### <span id="page-770-3"></span>**9.12.5.11.2. DayType Field**

This field SHALL indicate the type of day represented by the struct.

#### <span id="page-770-0"></span>**9.12.5.11.3. DayEntryIDs Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of [DayEntryID](#page-768-1)s for the [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1)s to apply during the date specified by [Date](#page-770-2), ordered by the value of the [StartTime](#page-768-0) field.

This list SHALL NOT contain two [DayEntryID](#page-768-1)s for [DayEntryStructs](#page-767-1) with the same value of the [Start-](#page-768-0)[Time](#page-768-0) field.

If the Randomization feature is supported, every [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) whose [DayEntryID](#page-768-1) is included in this field SHALL have its [StartTime](#page-768-0) field set to a value less than the following [DayEntryStruct's](#page-767-1) [StartTime](#page-768-0) field minus the calculated value of its [RandomizationOffset](#page-769-2) field. In other words, it should not be possible for a random offset to cause a day entry to begin before the preceding day entry.

# If the [DayType](#page-770-3) field is not Event:

- 1. The [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) referenced by the first [DayEntryID](#page-768-1) in this list SHALL have its [StartTime](#page-768-0) field set to zero.
- 2. Every [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) referenced by this list SHALL have its [Duration](#page-769-0) field omitted.

#### Otherwise, if the [DayType](#page-770-3) field is Event:

1. Every [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) referenced by this list SHALL NOT have a [Duration](#page-769-0) field whose value, added to the value of [StartTime](#page-768-0) field, is greater than the value of [StartTime](#page-768-0) field on any subsequent [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) referenced by this list. In other words, day entries with a set duration can not overlap any other day entries.

### <span id="page-771-1"></span>**9.12.5.12. DayPatternStruct Type**

This represents a series of day entries over the course of a day for a given set of days of the week.

| ID | Name             | Type                                  | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------|---------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | DayPat<br>ternID | uint32                                | all        |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | DaysOfWe<br>ek   | DayPat<br>ternDay<br>OfWeek<br>Bitmap | all        |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | DayEn<br>tryIDs  | list[uint32]                          | 1 to 96    |         |          |        | M               |

#### <span id="page-771-0"></span>**9.12.5.12.1. DayPatternID Field**

This field SHALL indicate an identifier for the day pattern. It SHALL be a unique identifier for the combination of values of the [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2) and [DayEntryIDs](#page-771-3) fields.

Once an identifier has been used for this combination, it SHALL NOT be used to represent any other combination of these values.

#### <span id="page-771-2"></span>**9.12.5.12.2. DaysOfWeek Field**

This field SHALL indicate which days of the week the associated set of [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1)s applies to. If no bits are set, then this SHALL be a rotating day. See [DayPatternIDs](#page-767-2).

#### <span id="page-771-3"></span>**9.12.5.12.3. DayEntryIDs Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of [DayEntryIDs](#page-768-1) for the [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1)s to apply during the days specified by [DaysOfWeek](#page-771-2), ordered by [StartTime](#page-768-0).

This list SHALL NOT contain two [DayEntryID](#page-768-1)s for the [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1)s with the same value of the [StartTime](#page-768-0) field.

# **9.12.5.12.3.1. Day Coverage**

The [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) referenced by the first [DayEntryID](#page-768-1) in this list SHALL have its [StartTime](#page-768-0) field set to zero.

Every [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) referenced by this list SHALL have its [Duration](#page-769-0) field omitted.

Meeting these constraints ensures that there are no periods during the day which are not covered by a [DayEntryStruct.](#page-767-1)

#### <span id="page-772-1"></span>**9.12.5.15. TariffPriceStruct Type**

This indicates a price or price level for a given tariff component, as well as what type of pricing it

### represents

| ID | Name       | Type                    | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------|-------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | PriceType  | TariffPrice<br>TypeEnum |            |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | Price      | money                   | all        |         |          |        | O.c+            |
| 2  | PriceLevel | int16                   | all        |         |          |        | O.c+            |

#### **9.12.5.15.1. PriceType Field**

This field SHALL indicate the type of price for the [Price](#page-773-1) or [PriceLevel](#page-773-2) fields.

### <span id="page-773-1"></span>**9.12.5.15.2. Price Field**

This field SHALL indicate the tariff price.

#### <span id="page-773-2"></span>**9.12.5.15.3. PriceLevel Field**

This field SHALL indicate the tariff price level.

# <span id="page-773-0"></span>**9.12.5.16. TariffComponentStruct Type**

This represents components of a tariff.

Tariff components typically represent a price or price level, though they may also specify other aspects of a tariff. For example, a tariff component may indicate changes in power thresholds, friendly credit status, or the expected state of auxiliary switches.

| ID | Name                      | Type                                          | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Tariff<br>Compo<br>nentID | uint32                                        | all        |         |          |        | M               |
| 1  | Price                     | Tariff<br>PriceStruct                         | all        | X       |          |        | [PRICE].b+      |
| 2  | Friendly<br>Credit        | bool                                          | all        |         |          |        | [FCRED].b+      |
| 3  | Auxiliary<br>Load         | Auxiliary<br>LoadSwitc<br>hSet<br>tingsStruct | all        |         |          |        | [AUXLD].b<br>+  |
| 4  | PeakPe<br>riod            | PeakPeri<br>odStruct                          | all        |         | 0        |        | [PEAKP].b+      |

| ID | Name                   | Type                         | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance  |
|----|------------------------|------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|------------------|
| 5  | Pow<br>erThresh<br>old | Pow<br>erThresh<br>oldStruct | all        |         | 0        |        | [PWRTHLD<br>].b+ |
| 6  | Threshold              | int64                        | all        | X       |          |        | M                |
| 7  | Label                  | string                       | max 128    | X       |          |        | O                |
| 8  | Predicted              | bool                         | all        |         |          |        | O                |

#### <span id="page-774-0"></span>**9.12.5.16.1. TariffComponentID Field**

This field SHALL indicate an identifier for the tariff component. If the tariff component is not a prediction, this field SHALL be a unique identifier for the combination of values of the [Price](#page-774-1), [Thresh](#page-775-0)[old,](#page-775-0) [FriendlyCredit](#page-774-2), [AuxiliaryLoad](#page-774-3), and [PeakPeriod](#page-775-1) fields with the value of the [DayEntryIDs](#page-775-2) field on the encompassing [TariffPeriodStruct](#page-775-3).

Once an identifier has been used for this combination, it SHALL NOT be used to represent any other combination of these values.

### <span id="page-774-1"></span>**9.12.5.16.2. Price Field**

This field SHALL indicate the price when the tariff component is active.

When the [Predicted](#page-775-4) field is set to TRUE, a null value SHALL indicate that the price and/or price level is not yet available.

When the [Predicted](#page-775-4) field is set to FALSE, a null value SHALL indicate that the server is unable to provide a specific price or price level.

### <span id="page-774-2"></span>**9.12.5.16.3. FriendlyCredit Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the calendar is entering a friendly credit period or not.

**NOTE**

When a meter enters into a Friendly Credit Period with a usable positive credit balance, the consumer will be allowed to consume energy for the duration of the Friendly Credit Period, regardless of their credit status while in that period. If, however, the consumer had already run out of credit and supply was interrupted before entering into the Friendly Credit Period, they will not be allowed to reconnect without first adding suitable additional credit.

**NOTE**

At the end of the Friendly Credit Period, the normal delivery rules connected with the accounting functions of the meter will be resumed, and if the meter's credit balance has dropped below the disablement threshold during the Friendly Credit Period, then the meter will disconnect upon resuming normal delivery rules

#### <span id="page-774-3"></span>**9.12.5.16.4. AuxiliaryLoad Field**

This field SHALL indicate the required state of auxiliary load switches.

#### <span id="page-775-1"></span>**9.12.5.16.5. PeakPeriod Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the tariff component represents a peak period.

#### **9.12.5.16.6. PowerThreshold Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the tariff component represents a power threshold.

#### <span id="page-775-0"></span>**9.12.5.16.7. Threshold Field**

This field SHALL indicate the maximum level of consumption this tariff component applies to, in units specified by the [TariffUnit](#page-777-1) attribute. If the tariff component applies to any level of consumption, this field SHALL be null.

#### **9.12.5.16.8. Label Field**

A free-form label for the tariff component.

#### <span id="page-775-4"></span>**9.12.5.16.9. Predicted Field**

This field SHALL indicate whether the tariff component represents a price prediction.

### <span id="page-775-3"></span>**9.12.5.17. TariffPeriodStruct Type**

This represents the tariff components in effect for a set of calendar day entry IDs.

| ID | Name                   | Type         | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------------|--------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0  | Label                  | string       | max 128    | X       |          |        | M               |
| 1  | DayEn<br>tryIDs        | list[uint32] | 1 to 20    |         |          |        | M               |
| 2  | TariffCom<br>ponentIDs | list[uint32] | 1 to 20    |         |          |        | M               |

#### **9.12.5.17.1. Label Field**

A free-form label for the tariff period.

#### <span id="page-775-2"></span>**9.12.5.17.2. DayEntryIDs Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of [DayEntryID](#page-768-1)s for the [DayEntryStructs](#page-767-1) during which the tariff components are active.

Each [DayEntryID](#page-768-1) SHALL be included in at most one [DayEntryIDs](#page-775-2) field. In other words, there SHALL be only one [TariffPeriodStruct](#page-775-3) for each [DayEntryID.](#page-768-1)

#### <span id="page-775-5"></span>**9.12.5.17.3. TariffComponentIDs Field**

This field SHALL indicate a list of [TariffComponentID](#page-774-0)s for the [TariffComponentStructs](#page-773-0) active during the specified day entries.

# **9.12.6.1. TariffInfo Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate basic information about the tariff.

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

# <span id="page-777-1"></span>**9.12.6.2. TariffUnit Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the unit of the commodity for pricing.

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

# <span id="page-777-0"></span>**9.12.6.3. StartDate Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a timestamp in UTC to denote the time at which the published calendar becomes active. A start date/time of 0x00000000 shall indicate that the calendar should become active immediately.

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

#### <span id="page-777-2"></span>**9.12.6.4. DayEntries Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the list of [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1)s included in this calendar.

The maximum constraint of this attribute is intended to allow representation of seven days of tariff information at 15 minute intervals.

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

#### <span id="page-777-3"></span>**9.12.6.5. DayPatterns Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the list of [DayPatternStructs](#page-771-1) used in the [CalendarPeriodStruct](#page-766-1) in this calendar.

Each day pattern in this list SHALL define the specific schedule that applies to the days it covers.

## <span id="page-778-0"></span>**9.12.6.6. CalendarPeriods Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the list of [CalendarPeriodStructs](#page-766-1) comprising this calendar. The [Calen](#page-766-1)[darPeriodStructs](#page-766-1) in this list SHALL be arranged in increasing order by the value of [StartDate.](#page-767-0)

If and only if the value of the [StartDate](#page-777-0) attribute is null, the value of the [StartDate](#page-767-0) field on the first [CalendarPeriodStruct](#page-766-1) in the [CalendarPeriods](#page-778-0) attribute SHALL also be null, indicating that the period begins immediately. The value of the [StartDate](#page-767-0) field on any subsequent [CalendarPeriod-](#page-766-1)[Struct](#page-766-1) in [CalendarPeriods](#page-778-0) SHALL NOT be null.

The active calendar period SHALL be in effect until the [StartDate](#page-767-0) of the next calendar period.

If the calendar is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

### <span id="page-778-1"></span>**9.12.6.7. IndividualDays Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the list of days to overlay on this calendar.

The [DayStruct](#page-770-1) in this list SHALL be arranged in increasing order by the value of [Date.](#page-770-2) The [DayStruct](#page-770-1) in this list SHALL not overlap.

If the calendar is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

## <span id="page-778-2"></span>**9.12.6.8. CurrentDay Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the current day's day entries.

If the tariff is not active or CurrentDay information is not available, this attribute SHALL be null.

# <span id="page-778-4"></span>**9.12.6.9. NextDay Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the next day's day entries.

If the tariff is not active or NextDay information is not available, this attribute SHALL be null.

### <span id="page-778-3"></span>**9.12.6.10. CurrentDayEntry Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the currently active [DayEntryStruct.](#page-767-1)

If the tariff is not active or day entry information is not available, this attribute SHALL be null.

### **9.12.6.11. CurrentDayEntryDate Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the UTC date when the [CurrentDay](#page-778-2), [CurrentDayEntry](#page-778-3), and [Current-](#page-779-3)[TariffComponents](#page-779-3) attributes were last updated.

If the tariff is not active or day entry information is not available, this attribute SHALL be null.

### <span id="page-778-5"></span>**9.12.6.12. NextDayEntry Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the predicted next active [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1).

If the tariff is not active or is not available, this attribute SHALL be null.

# <span id="page-779-7"></span>**9.12.6.13. NextDayEntryDate Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the predicted UTC date when the [CurrentDay,](#page-778-2) [CurrentDayEntry](#page-778-3), and [CurrentTariffComponents](#page-779-3) attributes will update to the values in the [NextDay](#page-778-4), [NextDayEntry](#page-778-5), and [NextTariffComponents](#page-779-4) attributes, respectively.

If the tariff is not active or is not available, this attribute SHALL be null.

### <span id="page-779-6"></span>**9.12.6.14. TariffComponents Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a list of [TariffComponentStruct](#page-773-0)s for the tariff.

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be empty.

### <span id="page-779-5"></span>**9.12.6.15. TariffPeriods Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a list of [TariffPeriodStruct](#page-775-3)s for the tariff.

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be empty.

# <span id="page-779-3"></span>**9.12.6.16. CurrentTariffComponents Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a list of the currently active [TariffComponentStructs](#page-773-0).

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be empty.

# <span id="page-779-4"></span>**9.12.6.17. NextTariffComponents Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate the predicted next active [TariffComponentStructs](#page-773-0).

If the tariff is unavailable, this attribute SHALL be null.

# <span id="page-779-1"></span>**9.12.6.18. DefaultRandomizationOffset Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a default randomization offset for [DayEntryStructs](#page-767-1) in this tariff. See [RandomizationOffset](#page-769-2) for details.

#### <span id="page-779-2"></span>**9.12.6.19. DefaultRandomizationType Attribute**

This attribute SHALL indicate a default randomization type for [DayEntryStruct](#page-767-1) in this tariff. See [RandomizationType](#page-769-1) for details.
