# <span id="page-885-3"></span>**11.5.7.1. SolicitOffer Command**

Requests that the Provider initiates a new session with the Offer / Answer flow in a way that allows

for options to be passed and work with devices needing the [standby flow](#page-872-0). This command SHALL have the following data fields:

| ID | Name                          | Type                          | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance      |
|----|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|----------------------|
| 0  | Strea<br>mUsage               | Strea<br>mUsageEnu<br>m       | all        |         |          | M                    |
| 1  | Originatin<br>gEnd<br>pointID | endpoint-no                   | all        |         |          | M                    |
| 2  | VideoStrea<br>mID             | VideoStream<br>ID             | all        | X       |          | O, D                 |
| 3  | AudioStrea<br>mID             | AudioStream<br>ID             | all        | X       |          | O, D                 |
| 4  | ICEServers                    | list[ICE<br>Server<br>Struct] | max 10     |         |          | O                    |
| 5  | ICETrans<br>portPolicy        | string                        | max 16     |         |          | O                    |
| 6  | Meta<br>dataEn<br>abled       | bool                          | all        |         |          | METADATA             |
| 7  | SFrameCon<br>fig              | SFrameStruc<br>t              | all        |         |          | P, O                 |
| 8  | VideoStrea<br>ms              | list[VideoStr<br>eamID]       | 1 to 16    |         |          | [Rev >=<br>v2].b+, O |
| 9  | AudioStrea<br>ms              | list[AudioStr<br>eamID]       | 1 to 16    |         |          | [Rev >=<br>v2].b+, O |

#### **11.5.7.1.1. StreamUsage Field**

This field SHALL contain the [StreamUsageEnum](#page-816-5) that indicates the stream usage for this session and is used per [Resource Management and Stream Priorities](#page-818-2).

#### **11.5.7.1.2. OriginatingEndpointID Field**

This field SHALL indicate the endpoint that originates this command. This endpoint SHALL be used when acting as a client to invoke the commands on the Requestor cluster.

### **11.5.7.1.3. AudioStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and the [AudioStreams](#page-888-0) field used instead.

If this field is encountered from clients implementing cluster revision 1, then the following SHALL

# be done:

- If not present, no audio should be included in the resulting Offer.
- If present and null, then automatic stream assignment or creation is requested.
- If present and non-null, the specific audio stream identified by the [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) is added as an entry to the [AudioStreams](#page-888-0) list.

#### **11.5.7.1.4. VideoStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and the [VideoStreams](#page-888-1) field used instead.

If this field is encountered from clients implementing cluster revision 1, then the following SHALL be done:

- If not present, no video should be included in the resulting Offer.
- If present and null, then automatic stream assignment or creation is requested.
- If present and non-null, the specific video stream identified by the [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) is added as an entry to the [VideoStreams](#page-888-1) list.

#### **11.5.7.1.5. ICEServers Field**

This field SHALL be a list of [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) which contains the ICE servers and their credentials to use for this session. See [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) for further details.

#### <span id="page-887-0"></span>**11.5.7.1.6. ICETransportPolicy Field**

This field SHALL contain a string which dictates the gathering and usage of ICE candidates. Specifically whether all candidates are used or if restrictions are applied to only use TURN server candidates. It is important for both security and connectivity behavior, as it allows applications to define a preferred approach to network routing and privacy. This field SHALL mirror the acceptable values in the W3C WebRTC API [RTCIceTransportPolicy](https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#rtcicetransportpolicy-enum) [https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#rtcicetransportpolicyenum] enum, which are listed below for convenience:

| Value | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|-------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 'all' | This is the default setting in most cases. The ICE<br>agent can gather candidates from all available<br>network interfaces (both public and private IP<br>addresses). This setting provides the highest<br>probability of establishing a direct peer-to-peer<br>connection without the need for relay servers<br>like TURN (Traversal Using Relays around NAT). |

| Value   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|---------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 'relay' | The ICE agent will only use relay candidates pro<br>vided by TURN servers. This policy enhances pri<br>vacy and security because it prevents the disclo<br>sure of the user's private IP addresses and<br>ensures that all traffic goes through a controlled<br>relay server. However, it may increase latency<br>and dependency on the relay infrastructure. |

#### **11.5.7.1.7. MetadataEnabled Field**

This field indicates if [metadata](#page-884-3) transmission SHALL be active in this session.

#### **11.5.7.1.8. SFrameConfig Field**

This field if present indicates that [SFrame End-to-End Encryption](#page-877-0) SHALL be active in this session using the configuration provided.

### <span id="page-888-1"></span>**11.5.7.1.9. VideoStreams Field**

This field SHALL be the list of requested [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) for this session. Valid values are found in the [AllocatedVideoStreams](#page-839-3) attribute.

#### <span id="page-888-0"></span>**11.5.7.1.10. AudioStreams Field**

This field SHALL be a list of requested [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) for this session. Valid values are found in the [AllocatedAudioStreams](#page-839-2) attribute.

#### **11.5.7.1.11. Effect on Receipt**

The following process SHALL be followed when the server receives this command:

- If [HardPrivacyModeOn](#page-840-3) is true:
  - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If [SoftLivestreamPrivacyModeEnabled](#page-840-1) is true and *StreamUsage* is [LiveView:](#page-817-3)
  - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If [SoftRecordingPrivacyModeEnabled](#page-840-0) is true and *StreamUsage* is [Recording](#page-817-1) or [Analysis:](#page-817-2)
  - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If *StreamUsage* is not found in the [StreamUsagePriorities:](#page-839-0)
  - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If the *VideoStreams* or *AudioStreams* fields are present, and the *VideoStreamID* or *AudioStreamID* fields are present:

- Fail the command with INVALID\_COMMAND, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If *VideoStreamID* is present:
  - If that field is null:
    - Automatically select an existing [video stream](#page-839-3) per the [Resource Management and Stream](#page-818-2) [Priorities.](#page-818-2)
  - Create an empty *VideoStreams* and add the selected [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) as a new entry.
- If *AudioStreamID* is present:
  - If that field is null:
    - Automatically select an existing [audio stream](#page-839-2) per the [Resource Management and Stream](#page-818-2) [Priorities.](#page-818-2)
  - Create an empty *AudioStreams* and add the selected [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) as a new entry.
- If *VideoStreams* is present:
  - If the [AllocatedVideoStreams](#page-839-3) is empty:
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
  - If there are duplicate entries in *VideoStreams*:
    - Fail the command with the status code ALREADY\_EXISTS, and end processing with no other side effects.
- For each entry in *VideoStreams*:
  - If an entry for the [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) is not found in the [AllocatedVideoStreams](#page-839-3) list:
    - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If *AudioStreams* is present:
  - If the [AllocatedAudioStreams](#page-839-2) is empty:
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
  - If there are duplicate entries in *AudioStreams*:
    - Fail the command with the status code ALREADY\_EXISTS, and end processing with no other side effects.
- For each entry in *AudioStreams*:
  - If an entry for the [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) is not found in the [AllocatedAudioStreams](#page-839-2) list:
    - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If *SFrameConfig* is present:
  - If the [CipherSuite](#page-884-5) field of the passed in *SFrameConfig* is not a supported value:
    - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.

- If the length of the [BaseKey](#page-885-4) field of the passed in *SFrameConfig* does not match the expected length for a key using the [CipherSuite:](#page-884-5)
  - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.
- For each URL in the [URLs](#page-880-0) field of each [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) in the passed in *ICEServers*:
  - If the URL scheme is turns or stuns, and the UTCTime attribute of the Time Synchronization cluster is null:
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
- Create a new [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2)
- Create a new [WebRTCSessionStruct](#page-881-0) associated with the accessing fabric, populated with the passed in values from this command, the *OriginatingEndpointID* field as the [PeerEndpointID](#page-882-0), and the accessing Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context (See Chapter 4 Secure Channel, Secure Session Context section, in [\[MatterCore\]\)](#page-28-5) as the [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1). The [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1), [PeerEndpointID](#page-882-0) and the associated fabric, SHALL be used as the destination for all commands for the corresponding [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2).
- If in [standby mode:](#page-872-0)
  - Respond with a [SolicitOfferResponse](#page-890-0) with [DeferredOffer](#page-891-0) set to TRUE.
  - Perform device specific steps to exit standby mode. This SHALL take less than 30 seconds.
- Else:
  - Respond with a [SolicitOfferResponse](#page-890-0) with [DeferredOffer](#page-891-0) set to FALSE.
- If not able to meet the [Resource Management and Stream Priorities](#page-818-2) conditions or unable to provide another WebRTC session:
  - Invoke [End](#page-903-1) with Reason set to OutOfResources, and end processing with no other side effects.
- Internally increment the [ReferenceCount](#page-829-3) on any used video streams.
- Internally increment the [ReferenceCount](#page-830-1) on any used audio streams.
- Store the WebRTCSessionStruct in the [CurrentSessions](#page-885-2)
- Generate the SDP Offer and invoke [Offer,](#page-901-0) and if the passed in *ICEServers* and *ICETransportPolicy* were present, include those fields in the command.

# <span id="page-890-0"></span>**11.5.7.2. SolicitOfferResponse Command**

This command SHALL be generated in response to a [SolicitOffer](#page-885-3) command.

This response contains information about the session and streams created and/or if a deferred offer will take place.

| ID | Name                | Type                | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance                       |
|----|---------------------|---------------------|------------|---------|----------|---------------------------------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | all        |         |          | M                                     |
| 1  | DeferredOf<br>fer   | bool                | all        |         |          | M                                     |
| 2  | VideoStrea<br>mID   | VideoStream<br>ID   | all        | X       |          | SolicitOf<br>fer.VideoStre<br>amID, D |
| 3  | AudioStrea<br>mID   | AudioStream<br>ID   | all        | X       |          | SolicitOf<br>fer.AudioStr<br>eamID, D |

Upon receipt, the client SHALL create a new [WebRTCSessionStruct](#page-881-0) populated with the values from this command, along with the accessing Peer Node ID and Local Fabric Index entries stored in the Secure Session Context as the PeerNodeID and FabricIndex values, and store it in the WebRTC Transport Requestor cluster's [CurrentSessions](#page-900-4) attribute.

The session establishment SHALL be considered failed unless a [Offer](#page-901-0) command is received by the Requestor from the [PeerEndpointID](#page-882-0) / FabricIndex within 30 seconds.

#### **11.5.7.2.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the ID of the established WebRTC session.

# <span id="page-891-0"></span>**11.5.7.2.2. DeferredOffer Field**

This field SHALL indicates the delayed processing hint of the provider.

If DeferredOffer is FALSE, the VideoStreamID and AudioStreamID fields SHALL NOT be null in this response and the Provider will without delay invoke the [Offer](#page-901-0) command. If DeferredOffer is TRUE, the VideoStreamID and AudioStreamID fields MAY be non-null in this response, if the stream mapping logic can be done while in its low-power state, or they MAY be null, if it cannot. When TRUE, this is a hint to the Requestor that there will be a larger than normal amount of time before the [Offer](#page-901-0) command will be invoked and the Requestor SHOULD use this extra time gap to begin its own ICE Candidate generation until the Offer arrives. (See further details in the section [WebRTC Battery](#page-872-0) [Camera in Standby Flow](#page-872-0))

#### **11.5.7.2.3. VideoStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and is only present when clients implementing cluster revision 1 included the VideoStreamID field in the request. When included, it SHALL contain a [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) used for the session if known or null if unknown at this time.

# **11.5.7.2.4. AudioStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and is only present when clients implementing cluster revision 1 included the AudioStreamID field in the request. When included, it SHALL contain a [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) used for the session if known or null if unknown at this time.

# <span id="page-892-0"></span>**11.5.7.3. ProvideOffer Command**

This command allows an SDP Offer to be set and start a new session. This command can also be used in the re-offer flow of an existing session to change the details of the SDP (e.g. to enable/disable two-way talk).

This command SHALL have the following data fields:

| ID  | Name                          | Type                          | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance                                           |
|-----|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| 0x0 | WebRTCSes<br>sionID           | WebRTCSes<br>sionID           | all        | X       |          | M                                                         |
| 0x1 | SDP                           | string                        | all        |         |          | M                                                         |
| 0x2 | Strea<br>mUsage               | Strea<br>mUsageEnu<br>m       | all        |         |          | WebRTCSes<br>sionID ==<br>NULL, O                         |
| 0x3 | Originatin<br>gEnd<br>pointID | endpoint-no                   | all        |         |          | WebRTCSes<br>sionID ==<br>NULL, O                         |
| 0x4 | VideoStrea<br>mID             | VideoStream<br>ID             | all        | X       |          | O, D                                                      |
| 0x5 | AudioStrea<br>mID             | AudioStream<br>ID             | all        | X       |          | O, D                                                      |
| 0x6 | ICEServers                    | list[ICE<br>Server<br>Struct] | max 10     |         |          | O                                                         |
| 0x7 | ICETrans<br>portPolicy        | string                        | max 16     |         |          | O                                                         |
| 0x8 | Meta<br>dataEn<br>abled       | bool                          | all        |         |          | METADATA<br>& (WebRTC<br>SessionID ==<br>NULL)            |
| 0x9 | SFrameCon<br>fig              | SFrameStruc<br>t              | all        |         |          | P, O                                                      |
| 0xA | VideoStrea<br>ms              | list[VideoStr<br>eamID]       | 1 to 16    |         |          | [(Rev >= v2)<br>& (WebRTC<br>SessionID ==<br>NULL)].d+, O |

| ID  | Name             | Type                    | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance                                           |
|-----|------------------|-------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| 0xB | AudioStrea<br>ms | list[AudioStr<br>eamID] | 1 to 16    |         |          | [(Rev >= v2)<br>& (WebRTC<br>SessionID ==<br>NULL)].d+, O |

### **11.5.7.3.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL be a [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) and contain the ID of an established WebRTC session or null if requesting a new session.

#### **11.5.7.3.2. SDP Field**

This field SHALL contain the string based [SDP](#page-30-9) Offer. See [WebRTC Transport](#page-870-0) for further details on SDP and Offer/Answer semantics.

#### **11.5.7.3.3. StreamUsage Field**

This field SHALL contain the [StreamUsageEnum](#page-816-5) that indicates the stream usage for this session.

#### **11.5.7.3.4. OriginatingEndpointID Field**

This field SHALL indicate the endpoint that originates this command. This endpoint SHALL be used when acting as a client to invoke the commands on the Requestor cluster.

### **11.5.7.3.5. VideoStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and the [VideoStreams](#page-888-1) field used instead.

If this field is encountered from clients implementing cluster revision 1, then the following SHALL be done:

- If not present, no video should be included in the resulting Answer.
- If present and null, then automatic stream assignment or creation is requested.
- If present and non-null, the specific video stream identified by the [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) SHALL be added as an entry to the [VideoStreams](#page-888-1) list.

#### **11.5.7.3.6. AudioStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and the [AudioStreams](#page-888-0) field used instead.

If this field is encountered from clients implementing cluster revision 1, then the following SHALL be done:

- If not present, no audio should be included in the resulting Answer.
- If present and null, then automatic stream assignment or creation is requested.
- If present and non-null, the specific video stream identified by the [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) SHALL be added as an entry to the [AudioStreams](#page-888-0) list.

#### **11.5.7.3.7. ICEServers Field**

This field SHALL be a list of [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) which contains the ICE servers and their credentials to use for this session. See [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) for further details.

#### **11.5.7.3.8. ICETransportPolicy Field**

This field controls the gathering and usage of ICE candidates and SHALL have one of the values found in [ICETransportPolicy.](#page-887-0)

#### **11.5.7.3.9. MetadataEnabled Field**

This field indicates if [metadata](#page-884-3) transmission SHALL be active in this session.

#### **11.5.7.3.10. SFrameConfig Field**

This field if present indicates that [SFrame End-to-End Encryption](#page-877-0) SHALL be active in this session using the configuration provided.

#### **11.5.7.3.11. VideoStreams Field**

This field SHALL be the list of requested [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) for this session. Valid values are found in the [AllocatedVideoStreams](#page-839-3) attribute.

#### **11.5.7.3.12. AudioStreams Field**

This field SHALL be a list of requested [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) for this session. Valid values are found in the [AllocatedAudioStreams](#page-839-2) attribute.

### **11.5.7.3.13. Effect on Receipt**

The process below SHALL be followed by the server when receiving this command:

- If *WebRTCSessionID* is not null and does not match a value in [CurrentSessions:](#page-885-2)
  - Respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND
- If *WebRTCSessionID* is null:
  - If [HardPrivacyModeOn](#page-840-3) is true:
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
  - If [SoftLivestreamPrivacyModeEnabled](#page-840-1) is true and *StreamUsage* is [LiveView:](#page-817-3)
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
  - If [SoftRecordingPrivacyModeEnabled](#page-840-0) is true and *StreamUsage* is [Recording](#page-817-1) or [Analysis:](#page-817-2)
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
  - If the passed in *StreamUsage* is not found in the [StreamUsagePriorities:](#page-839-0)
    - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end pro-

cessing with no other side effects.

- If the *VideoStreams* or *AudioStreams* fields are present, and the *VideoStreamID* or *AudioStreamID* fields are present:
  - Fail the command with INVALID\_COMMAND, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If *VideoStreamID* is present:
  - If that field is null:
    - Automatically select an existing [video stream](#page-839-3) per the [Resource Management and](#page-818-2) [Stream Priorities](#page-818-2).
  - Create an empty *VideoStreams* and add the selected [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) as a new entry.
- If *AudioStreamID* is present:
  - If that field is null:
    - Automatically select an existing [audio stream](#page-839-2) per the [Resource Management and](#page-818-2) [Stream Priorities](#page-818-2).
  - Create an empty *AudioStreams* and add the selected [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) as a new entry.
- If *VideoStreams* is present:
  - If the [AllocatedVideoStreams](#page-839-3) is empty:
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
  - If there are duplicate entries in *VideoStreams*:
    - Fail the command with the status code ALREADY\_EXISTS, and end processing with no other side effects.
- For each entry in *VideoStreams*:
  - If an entry for the [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) is not found in the [AllocatedVideoStreams](#page-839-3) list:
    - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If *AudioStreams* is present:
  - If the [AllocatedAudioStreams](#page-839-2) is empty:
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
  - If there are duplicate entries in *AudioStreams*:
    - Fail the command with the status code ALREADY\_EXISTS, and end processing with no other side effects.
- For each entry in *AudioStreams*:
  - If an entry for the [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) is not found in the [AllocatedAudioStreams](#page-839-2) list:
    - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.

- If not able to meet the [Resource Management and Stream Priorities](#page-818-2) conditions or unable to provide another WebRTC session:
  - Respond with a response status of RESOURCE\_EXHAUSTED+
- If *SFrameConfig* is present:
- If the [CipherSuite](#page-884-5) field of the passed in *SFrameConfig* is not a supported value:
  - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If the length of the [BaseKey](#page-885-4) field of the passed in *SFrameConfig* does not match the expected length for a key using the [CipherSuite:](#page-884-5)
  - Fail the command with the status code DYNAMIC\_CONSTRAINT\_ERROR, and end processing with no other side effects.
- For each URL in the [URLs](#page-880-0) field of each [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) in the passed in *ICEServers*:
  - If the URL scheme is turns or stuns, and the UTCTime attribute of the Time Synchronization cluster is null:
    - Fail the command with the status code INVALID\_IN\_STATE, and end processing with no other side effects.
- Create a new [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2)
- Create a new [WebRTCSessionStruct](#page-881-0) associated with the accessing fabric, populated with the passed in values from this command, the *OriginatingEndpointID* field as the [PeerEndpointID](#page-882-0), and the accessing Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context (See Chapter 4 Secure Channel, Secure Session Context section, in [\[MatterCore\]](#page-28-5)) as the [PeerNodeID.](#page-882-1) The [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1), [PeerEndpointID](#page-882-0) and the associated fabric, SHALL be used as the destination for all asynchronous commands for the corresponding [WebRTCSessionID.](#page-878-2)
- Internally increment the [ReferenceCount](#page-829-3) on any used video streams.
- Internally increment the [ReferenceCount](#page-830-1) on any used audio streams.
- Store the [WebRTCSessionStruct](#page-881-0) in the [CurrentSessions](#page-885-2)
- Else:
  - If the accessing Peer Node ID stored in the Secure Session Context and the accessing fabric do not match the [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1) and associated fabric for the *WebRTCSessionID* entry in [Cur](#page-885-2)[rentSessions:](#page-885-2)
    - Respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND
- Respond with a [ProvideOfferResponse](#page-896-0)
- Process the SDP Offer, begin the ICE Candidate gathering phase, create the SDP Answer, and invoke [Answer](#page-901-1) on the sessions [PeerEndpointID](#page-882-0) / FabricIndex

### <span id="page-896-0"></span>**11.5.7.4. ProvideOfferResponse Command**

This command contains information about the session and streams created as a response to the requestor's offer.

This command SHALL have the following data fields:

| ID | Name                | Type                | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance                                 |
|----|---------------------|---------------------|------------|---------|----------|-------------------------------------------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | all        |         |          | M                                               |
| 1  | VideoStrea<br>mID   | VideoStream<br>ID   | all        | X       |          | WebRTCProv<br>ideOf<br>fer.VideoStre<br>amID, D |
| 2  | AudioStrea<br>mID   | AudioStream<br>ID   | all        | X       |          | WebRTCProv<br>ideOf<br>fer.AudioStr<br>eamID, D |

Upon receipt, the client SHALL create a new [WebRTCSessionStruct](#page-881-0) populated with the values from this command, along with the accessing Peer Node ID and Local Fabric Index entries stored in the Secure Session Context as the PeerNodeID and FabricIndex values, and store it in the WebRTC Transport Requestor cluster's [CurrentSessions](#page-900-4) attribute.

### **11.5.7.4.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) of the established WebRTC session.

#### **11.5.7.4.2. VideoStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and is only present when clients implementing cluster revision 1 included the VideoStreamID field in the request. When included, it SHALL contain a [VideoStreamID](#page-833-0) used for the session if known or null if unknown at this time.

#### **11.5.7.4.3. AudioStreamID Field**

This field is deprecated and is only present when clients implementing cluster revision 1 included the AudioStreamID field in the request. When included, SHALL contain a [AudioStreamID](#page-833-1) used for the session if known or null if unknown at this time.

#### <span id="page-897-0"></span>**11.5.7.5. ProvideAnswer Command**

This command SHALL be initiated from a Node in response to an Offer that was previously received from a remote peer. It SHALL have the following data fields:

| ID | Name                | Type                | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------|---------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | all        |         |          | M               |
| 1  | SDP                 | string              | all        |         |          | M               |

This command SHALL respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND if the WebRTCSessionID does not match an entry in [CurrentSessions,](#page-885-2) or if the matching entry's associated fabric and PeerNodeID do not match the accessing fabric and the Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context of the session this command was received on.

#### **11.5.7.5.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) of the established WebRTC session.

#### **11.5.7.5.2. SDP Field**

This field SHALL contain the string based [SDP](#page-30-9) Answer. See [WebRTC Transport](#page-870-0) for further details on SDP and Offer/Answer semantics.

### <span id="page-898-0"></span>**11.5.7.6. ProvideICECandidates Command**

This command allows for string based [ICE candidates](https://rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8839#section-5.1) [https://rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8839#section-5.1] generated after the initial Offer / Answer exchange, via a JSEP [onicecandidate](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9429#section-4.1.20) [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/ html/rfc9429#section-4.1.20] event, a DOM [rtcpeerconnectioniceevent](https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcpeerconnectioniceevent) [https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#domrtcpeerconnectioniceevent] event, or other WebRTC compliant implementations, to be added to a session during the gathering phase. This is typically used for STUN or TURN discovered candidates, or to indicate the end of gathering state.

| ID | Name                | Type                         | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------|------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID          | all        |         |          | M               |
| 1  | ICECandi<br>dates   | list[ICECan<br>didateStruct] | min 1      |         |          | M               |

This command SHALL respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND if the *WebRTCSessionID* does not match an entry in [CurrentSessions](#page-885-2), or if the matching entry's associated fabric and [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1) do not match the accessing fabric and the Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context of the session this command was received on.

## **11.5.7.6.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) of the established WebRTC session.

### **11.5.7.6.2. ICECandidates Field**

This field SHALL contain a list of [JSEP](#page-30-15) compliant [ICE Candidate Format](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9429#section-3.5.2.1) [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/ html/rfc9429#section-3.5.2.1] objects.

# <span id="page-898-1"></span>**11.5.7.7. EndSession Command**

This command instructs the stream provider to end the WebRTC session.

| ID | Name                | Type                        | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------|-----------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID         | all        |         |          | M               |
| 1  | Reason              | WebRTCEn<br>dReaso<br>nEnum | all        |         |          | M               |

#### **11.5.7.7.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) of the established WebRTC session.

#### **11.5.7.7.2. Reason Field**

This field SHALL be one of the values in [WebRTCEndReasonEnum](#page-878-1).

#### **11.5.7.7.3. Effect on Receipt**

The process below SHALL be followed by the server when receiving this command or when the Provider detects a MEDIA\_TIMEOUT:

- If *WebRTCSessionID* does not match a value in [CurrentSessions:](#page-885-2)
  - Fail the command with the status code NOT\_FOUND, and end processing with no other side effects.
- If the accessing fabric and Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context do not match the associated fabric and [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1) field of the *WebRTCSessionID* entry in [CurrentSessions:](#page-885-2)
  - Fail the command with the status code NOT\_FOUND, and end processing with no other side effects.
- Internally decrement the [ReferenceCount](#page-829-3) on any used video streams.
- Internally decrement the [ReferenceCount](#page-830-1) on any used audio streams.
- Remove the entry in the [CurrentSessions](#page-885-2) for *WebRTCSessionID*.

# <span id="page-899-0"></span>**11.6. WebRTC Transport Requestor Cluster**

The WebRTC transport requestor cluster provides a way for stream consumers (e.g. Matter Stream Viewer) to establish a WebRTC connection with a stream provider that implements the [WebRTC](#page-883-0) [Transport Provider Cluster.](#page-883-0)

# <span id="page-899-1"></span>**11.6.1. Revision History**

The global ClusterRevision attribute value SHALL be the highest revision number in the table below.

| Revision | Description                                                  |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Initial version of the WebRTC Transport<br>Requestor Cluster |
| 2        | Add multi stream support                                     |

# <span id="page-900-0"></span>**11.6.2. Classification**

| Hierarchy | Role        | Scope    | PICS Code |
|-----------|-------------|----------|-----------|
| Base      | Application | Endpoint | WEBRTCR   |

# <span id="page-900-1"></span>**11.6.3. Cluster ID**

| ID     | Name                       |
|--------|----------------------------|
| 0x0554 | WebRTC Transport Requestor |

# <span id="page-900-2"></span>**11.6.4. Attributes**

| ID     | Name    | Type       | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Access | Confor<br>mance |
|--------|---------|------------|------------|---------|----------|--------|-----------------|
| 0x0000 | Cur     | list[WebRT | all        |         |          | R A S  | M               |
|        | rentSes | CSession   |            |         |          |        |                 |
|        | sions   | Struct]    |            |         |          |        |                 |

# <span id="page-900-4"></span>**11.6.4.1. CurrentSessions Attribute**

This attribute SHALL be a list of [WebRTCSessionStruct](#page-881-0), which represents all the active WebRTC Sessions on this Node.

# <span id="page-900-3"></span>**11.6.5. Commands**

| ID   | Name              | Direction          | Response | Access | Quality | Confor<br>mance |
|------|-------------------|--------------------|----------|--------|---------|-----------------|
| 0x00 | Offer             | client ⇒<br>server | Y        | O      | L       | M               |
| 0x01 | Answer            | client ⇒<br>server | Y        | O      | L       | M               |
| 0x02 | ICECandi<br>dates | client ⇒<br>server | Y        | O      | L       | M               |
| 0x03 | End               | client ⇒<br>server | Y        | O      | L       | M               |

### <span id="page-901-0"></span>**11.6.5.1. Offer Command**

This command provides the stream requestor with WebRTC session details. It is sent following the receipt of a [SolicitOffer](#page-885-3) command or a re-offer initiated by the Provider.

| ID | Name                   | Type                          | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|------------------------|-------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID    | WebRTCSes<br>sionID           | all        |         |          | M               |
| 1  | SDP                    | string                        | all        |         |          | M               |
| 2  | ICEServers             | list[ICE<br>Server<br>Struct] | max 10     |         |          | O               |
| 3  | ICETrans<br>portPolicy | string                        | max 16     |         |          | O               |

This command SHALL respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND if the WebRTCSessionID does not match an entry in [CurrentSessions,](#page-900-4) or if the matching entry's associated fabric and [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1) do not match the accessing fabric and the Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context (see Chapter 4 Secure Channel, Secure Session Context section, in [\[MatterCore\]\)](#page-28-5) of the session this command was received on.

#### **11.6.5.1.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the ID of the established WebRTC session.

# **11.6.5.1.2. SDP Field**

This field SHALL contain the string based [SDP](#page-30-9) Offer. See [WebRTC Transport](#page-870-0) for further details on SDP and Offer/Answer semantics.

#### **11.6.5.1.3. ICEServers Field**

This field SHALL be a list of [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) which contains the ICE servers and their credentials to use for this session. See [ICEServerStruct](#page-879-0) for further details.

#### **11.6.5.1.4. ICETransportPolicy Field**

This field controls the gathering and usage of ICE candidates and SHALL have one of the values found in [ICETransportPolicy](#page-887-0).

#### <span id="page-901-1"></span>**11.6.5.2. Answer Command**

This command provides the stream requestor with the WebRTC session details (i.e. Session ID and SDP answer), It is the next command in the Offer/Answer flow to the [ProvideOffer](#page-892-0) command.

| ID | Name                | Type                | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------|---------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | all        |         |          | M               |
| 1  | SDP                 | string              | all        |         |          | M               |

This command SHALL respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND if the WebRTCSessionID does not match an entry in [CurrentSessions](#page-900-4), or if the matching entry's associated fabric and [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1) do not match the accessing fabric and the Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context of the session this command was received on.

#### **11.6.5.2.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) of the established WebRTC session.

#### **11.6.5.2.2. SDP Field**

This field SHALL contain the string based [SDP](#page-30-9) Answer. See [WebRTC Transport](#page-870-0) for further details on SDP and Offer/Answer semantics.

### <span id="page-902-0"></span>**11.6.5.3. ICECandidates Command**

This command allows for the object based [ICE candidates](https://rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8839#section-5.1) [https://rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8839#section-5.1] generated after the initial Offer / Answer exchange, via a JSEP [onicecandidate](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9429#section-4.1.20) [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9429#section-4.1.20] event, a DOM [rtcpeerconnectioniceevent](https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcpeerconnectioniceevent) [https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcpeerconnectioniceevent] event, or other WebRTC compliant implementations, to be added to a session during the gathering phase. This is typically used for STUN or TURN discovered candidates, or to indicate the end of gathering state.

| ID | Name                | Type                         | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------|------------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID          | all        |         |          | M               |
| 1  | ICECandi<br>dates   | list[ICECan<br>didateStruct] | min 1      |         |          | M               |

This command SHALL respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND if the WebRTCSessionID does not match an entry in [CurrentSessions](#page-900-4), or if the matching entry's associated fabric and [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1) do not match the accessing fabric and the Peer Node ID entry stored in the Secure Session Context of the session this command was received on.

#### **11.6.5.3.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) of the established WebRTC session.

#### **11.6.5.3.2. ICECandidates Field**

This field SHALL contain a list of [JSEP](#page-30-15) compliant [ICE Candidate Format](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9429#section-3.5.2.1) [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/

html/rfc9429#section-3.5.2.1] objects.

# <span id="page-903-1"></span>**11.6.5.4. End Command**

This command notifies the stream requestor that the provider has ended the WebRTC session.

| ID | Name                | Type                        | Constraint | Quality | Fallback | Confor<br>mance |
|----|---------------------|-----------------------------|------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| 0  | WebRTCSes<br>sionID | WebRTCSes<br>sionID         | all        |         |          | M               |
| 1  | Reason              | WebRTCEn<br>dReaso<br>nEnum | all        |         |          | M               |

#### **11.6.5.4.1. WebRTCSessionID Field**

This field SHALL contain the [WebRTCSessionID](#page-878-2) of the established WebRTC session.

#### **11.6.5.4.2. Reason Field**

This field SHALL be one of the values in [WebRTCEndReasonEnum](#page-878-1).

#### **11.6.5.4.3. Effect on Receipt**

The process below SHALL be followed by the server when receiving this command:

- If WebRTCSessionID does not match a value in [CurrentSessions](#page-900-4):
  - Respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND
- If the accessing Peer Node ID stored in the Secure Session Context and the accessing fabric do not match the [PeerNodeID](#page-882-1) and associated fabric for the WebRTCSessionID entry in [CurrentSes](#page-900-4)[sions](#page-900-4):
  - Respond with a response status of NOT\_FOUND
- Remove the entry in the [CurrentSessions](#page-900-4) for WebRTCSessionID

# <span id="page-903-0"></span>**11.7. Push AV Stream Transport Cluster**

This cluster implements the upload of Audio and Video streams from the [Camera AV Stream Man](#page-818-0)[agement Cluster](#page-818-0) using suitable push-based transports. Push AV Stream Transport is the transmission of a stream of media to a server, initiated by the activation of an associated trigger. A push transport can be triggered from a camera operating in an always-on mode for supporting 24/7 style recording, triggered by events based on motion zones defined in the [Zone Management Cluster](#page-254-0), or manually triggered using commands or bindings.

A push transport SHALL be allocated before it is intended to be used, and then it is subsequently started when its configured trigger is activated.

An allocated push transport consists of five main logical things:

- A container format, which specifies how the individual media frames are formatted or multiplexed together
- An ingestion format which specifies how it is signaled and transmitted to the far end.
- A trigger which specifies when transport will occur.
- Which media stream/s to package together in the container format.
- Various options to the above.

All push transport [ingest methods](#page-920-0) SHALL use TLS as specified by the core specification. TLS Client Certificates SHALL be used for Authorization and Identification of a Node on the underlying TLS connection (see Chapter 14, TLS Certificate Management and TLS Client Management sections in [\[MatterCore\]](#page-28-5)). Nodes supporting this cluster SHALL also support the TLS Client Management Cluster and its dependencies.

# <span id="page-904-0"></span>**11.7.1. CMAF Ingestion**

CMAF Ingestion as defined in [DASH-IF Live Media Ingest Protocol](#page-29-10) version 1.2 and newer SHALL be supported.

Nodes SHALL support both [Interface-1: CMAF Ingest](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#interface-1) [https://dashif.org/Ingest/#interface-1] and [Interface-](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#interface-2)[2: DASH and HLS Ingest](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#interface-2) [https://dashif.org/Ingest/#interface-2].

Nodes SHALL use [HTTP/2](#page-30-16) or newer, for all CMAF Ingestion HTTP based operations.

Nodes using [CMAFIngest](#page-921-0) as the ingestion method SHALL use [CMAF](#page-920-1) as the [container format](#page-920-2).

# <span id="page-904-2"></span>**11.7.1.1. Background**

The Matter Node is considered the CMAF [ingest source](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#ingest-source) [https://dashif.org/Ingest/#ingest-source]. The CMAF [receiving-entity](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#receiving-entity) [https://dashif.org/Ingest/#receiving-entity] is the server that the Matter Node will send the media stream to. The receiving-entity details along with the media streams that make up the [ingest-stream](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#ingest-stream) [https://dashif.org/Ingest/#ingest-stream] are provisioned in a [TransportOptionsStruct](#page-929-0). Matter's implementation of CMAF Ingest allows for optional end-to-end media encryption using the standard procedure defined in [CENCISOBMFF](#page-29-11) and [CENC.](#page-29-12) [CENC](#page-29-12) is an ISO standard for supporting end-to-end encryption of CMAF media files. Controllers/Ecosystems MAY utilize CENC in their deployments, but management and generation of the CENC key is outside the scope of this standard. Matter supports both initial CENC key assignment using the [CMAFContainerOptionsStruct](#page-923-0) struct via the [AllocatePushTransport](#page-935-0) command and CENC key-rotation by a Controller after initial provisioning using the [ModifyPushTransport](#page-939-0) command. When CENC mode is active, Nodes SHALL use the AES-128 CBC cbcs mode of CENC as defined in Section 10.4 of [ISO-23001:7-2023](#page-29-12) or later.

In CMAF, the basic units of the protocol are Segments, Tracks, and Sessions.

#### <span id="page-904-1"></span>**11.7.1.1.1. Segment**

A Segment is a fixed duration [ISOBMFF](#page-29-13) file which contains the Audio, Video, and/or Metadata samples themselves. A Segment MAY multiplex Audio and Video if configured to do so, otherwise the Segment would contain a single type of media.

#### <span id="page-905-0"></span>**11.7.1.1.2. Track**

A Track is a symbolic name applied to a sequence of one or more [Segments](#page-904-1), of the same media type, from the same source. In Matter, an [Audio Stream](#page-833-1) maps to an audio Track, a [Video Stream](#page-833-0) maps to a video Track, and one or more [metadata content](#page-832-0) maps to a metadata Track. All Segments within the same Track utilize the same fixed duration, except the last Segment which may be less than or equal to that duration. Additionally, all Segments within the same Track are sequentially numbered per the [Segment Numbering](#page-906-0) rules.

A single CMAF Track SHALL NOT contain both audio and video in the same Segment. In MP4 terms, a CMAF Track is non-interleaved audio and video. A CMAF Track MAY contain interleaved [meta](#page-832-0)[data content](#page-832-0) inside the video or audio MP4 [Segment](#page-904-1) file.

#### <span id="page-905-1"></span>**11.7.1.1.3. Session**

A Session is defined as the set of one or more [Tracks,](#page-905-0) that lasts for a duration of time. The duration of a Session can be variable or fixed. The Session's duration is based on the duration of the [Trigger](#page-919-4) [Type](#page-919-4) that caused its transmission to occur. In Matter's CMAF usage, a Session can be considered a low level logical event, though one delineated only by Motion detection, Command invocation timings, or fixed durations.

### <span id="page-905-2"></span>**11.7.1.2. Operation**

CMAF at its core is a sequence of HTTP PUT/POST operations for each media [Segment,](#page-904-1) within each [Track,](#page-905-0) within each [Session.](#page-905-1) Every operation is sent to a unique URL, which is known as the [POST\\_URL](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#post_url) [https://dashif.org/Ingest/#post\_url]. Each unique URL contains information about the Session, Track, and Segment. Each unique URL is comprised of two components that are concatenated together.

The first component of the POST\_URL is a static value called the [publishing\\_point\\_URL](https://dashif.org/Ingest/#publishing_point_url) [https://dashif.org/Ingest/#publishing\_point\_url]. The publishing\_point\_URL contains the scheme, hostname of the server, and whatever initial URL path components the receiving-entity would like to receive. Typically, deployments encode user specific information or other ecosystem specific items within the initial URL path values in the publishing\_point\_URL.

For Matter deployments, the publishing\_point\_URL SHALL use the https scheme, SHALL NOT contain the URL fragment character #, SHALL NOT contain the URL query character ?, and SHALL end with a URL forward slash character /. The publishing\_point\_URL MAY contain as many URL path components as fit within the allocated space of the [URL](#page-931-0) field. Any publishing\_point\_URL issued to a Matter device SHALL allow for one or more Sessions.

An example of a publishing\_point\_url is: [https://ingest.example.com/](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/) [provider\\_supplied\\_arbitrary\\_data/in/base/part/of/url/](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/)

The second component of the POST\_URL is a dynamically computed string that includes the [Session](#page-905-1) name, [Track](#page-905-0) name, and [Segment](#page-904-1) name. Each of these three values are placed in that order as extended paths at the end of the publishing\_point\_URL. The Session and Segment names also contain numerically increasing portions of their string, which allows for the receiving-entity to determine the event time bounds information along with the individual segment information.

An example of the second component is: session\_1/media1/segment\_1001.m4s. In this example, session\_1 is the session name, media1 is the track name, and segment\_1001.m4s is the segment name.

For Matter deployments, the extended path SHALL be comprised of the three elements in the following order: session\_name/track\_name/segment\_name and each sub-portion SHALL follow these rules:

session\_name: Consists of the fixed value session\_ followed by a monotonically increasing *Session-Number* numeric string managed by this cluster. *SessionNumber* SHALL be of type uint64 and start with value 1 when a transport is first allocated.

track\_name: Consists of a provisioned string provided in the [VideoStreamName](#page-922-0) or [AudioStream-](#page-923-1)[Name](#page-923-1) fields.

segment\_name: Consists of the fixed value segment\_ followed by a monotonically increasing *SegmentNumber* numeric string managed by this cluster, followed by a period ., followed by the media type's [Segment Extension](#page-906-1).

When the fixed and variable pieces are put together the extended paths are: session\_<SessionNumber>/<TrackName>/segment\_<SegmentNumber>.<SegmentExtension>

### <span id="page-906-0"></span>**11.7.1.3. Segment Numbering**

In Matter's usage of CMAF, *SegmentNumber* SHALL be of type uint16 and start at 1001 for each [Track](#page-905-0) within each [Session.](#page-905-1) In practice, a *SegmentNumber* will likely never exceed 9999 due to the Session length duration limit.

Implementations SHALL keep an internal value on the Transport which tracks the current Segment Number for each Track.

### <span id="page-906-1"></span>**11.7.1.4. Segment Extension**

In Matter's usage of CMAF, the following table SHALL determine the value for *SegmentExtension*:

| Extension | Mime-Type         | Usage                                     |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| m4s       | video/iso.segment | When the track contains video<br>or audio |

### <span id="page-906-2"></span>**11.7.1.5. Track Naming**

The CMAF Track Name is populated from the [VideoStreamName](#page-922-0) or [AudioStreamName](#page-923-1) fields of the associated stream entry in the [VideoStreams](#page-931-1) or [AudioStreams](#page-931-2) lists for that transport. CMAF Track Names are not user visible so the Controller MAY use any naming scheme they wish.

The Track Name is placed in the computed extended path fields portion of the CMAF POST\_URL.

#### <span id="page-906-3"></span>**11.7.1.6. Session Numbering**

In Matter's usage of CMAF, there are two types of [Session](#page-905-1) durations that affect when the *Session-Number* changes for an allocated transport.

- Fixed duration Sessions are used with [Continuous](#page-920-3) triggers. These sessions SHALL have a fixed duration of five minutes.
- Variable duration Sessions with max durations are used with [Motion](#page-920-4) and [Command](#page-920-5) triggers. These sessions SHALL have a minimum duration of two segments, and a maximum duration of five minutes.

Implementations SHALL persistently store the following internal values on the Transport:

- A *SessionNumber* of type uint64.
- A *SessionStartedTimestamp* of type systime-ms.

*SessionNumber* SHALL initially start at 1. It SHALL increment by 1, with every Trigger activation, or if the current SystemTimeStamp value at the time of a transmission is greater than 5 minutes past the *SessionStartedTimestamp*. Upon incrementing the *SessionNumber*, the *SessionStartedTimestamp* SHALL be set to the current SystemTimeStamp value.

## **11.7.1.7. Multiple Tracks**

In some ecosystem topologies it can be advantageous to send multiple streams/resolutions/encodings of the same content. For example, content analysis could be done more efficiently on a smaller resolution, while storage uses a higher resolution.

Another possible topology is one where the ecosystem wants to store multiple sizes of the same content to allow for adaptive streaming playback. In this topology lower bandwidth viewers can receive a smaller resolution, while high bandwidth viewers receive a higher resolution.

Either style of deployment can be achieved by having provisioned Transports request more than one stream of a given type concurrently in the [VideoStreams](#page-931-1) or [AudioStreams](#page-931-1) lists when configuring the transport.

For a given transport, track names, video stream IDs, and audio stream IDs, SHALL all be unique.

### **11.7.1.8. CMAF Interface-2 Upload Deviations**

This specification is deviating from and extending the base CMAF specification.

The first change dictates a specific order of HTTP operations for initial manifest/playlists uploads, init segment uploads, regular segment uploads, and final manifest/playlist uploads.

The second change specifies a particular syntax be used in DASH manifests and HLS playlists for initial uploads, and a different syntax for the final manifest/playlist upload. This is to allow the CMAF server receiving the content to definitively know when a [CMAF Session](#page-905-1) begins and ends, by just parsing the contents of the DASH manifest file or the HLS media playlist.

The third change dictates a Matter specific HTTP header to be included on certain Interface-2 HLS Segment uploads to remove the need for intermediate HLS playlist uploads after each Segment has been transmitted.

#### **11.7.1.8.1. DASH Upload Deviations**

When [Interface-2 DASH](#page-922-1) mode is selected, a Session is uploaded using the following order and rules:

- 1. The manifest filename SHALL always be session\_name/index.mpd.
- 2. The Session upload SHALL start with the initial manifest file.
- 3. When the initial manifest is uploaded at the start of a Session, it SHALL set the type attribute to dynamic in the root MPD tag of the XML and use the SegmentTemplate syntax for loading segments.
- 4. Track uploads SHALL begin only after the initial manifest file completes uploading, and Tracks SHOULD be uploaded in parallel.
- 5. Each Track in the Session SHALL then follow this process:
  - a. The Track's init segment is uploaded as session\_name/track\_name/track\_name.init
  - b. Each Segment within the Track is uploaded in order, one at a time.
- 6. When the final Segment of the last Track completes uploading, the manifest file SHALL be uploaded again, but setting the type attribute to static in the root MPD tag. In this final manifest file, the SegmentTemplate SHALL include a SegmentTimeline element that accurately describes the duration of all uploaded segments.

With the ordering and rules specified above, the following state tracking can be used at the CMAF Server for DASH mode:

- The contents of a session\_name/index.mpd manifest file for which the root tag MPD contains the attribute type set to the value "dynamic" indicates the start of a new CMAF Session.
- The Representation tags in the manifest file will indicate how many Tracks will be uploaded.
- The contents of a session\_name/index.mpd manifest file for which the root tag MPD contains the attribute type set to the value "static" indicates the end of a new CMAF Session.

#### **11.7.1.8.2. HLS Upload Deviations**

When [Interface-2 HLS](#page-922-2) mode is selected, a Session is uploaded using the following order and rules:

- 1. The multi-variant playlist filename SHALL always be session\_name/index.m3u8.
- 2. The Session upload SHALL start with the multi-variant playlist file.
- 3. Track uploads SHALL begin only after the multi-variant playlist file completes the upload, and Tracks SHOULD be uploaded in parallel.
- 4. Each Track in the Session SHALL then follow this process:
  - a. The Track's initial media playlist is uploaded as session\_name/track\_name/index.m3u8. This initial media playlist SHALL NOT contain #EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE, #EXT-X-ENDLIST, #EXTINF, or segment lines.
  - b. The Track's init segment is uploaded as session\_name/track\_name/track\_name.init
  - c. Each Segment within the Track is uploaded in order, one at a time.
  - d. Each Segment uploaded SHALL add an additional HTTP header called X-EXTINF-duration. This headers value is the duration decimal-floating-point value in seconds of the #EXTINF:

segment tag in an HLS playlist (see section 4.4.4.1 of [RFC 8216bis](#page-30-17)). For example: X-EXTINFduration: 4.00000 for a segment that is exactly 4.000000 seconds long. The CMAF Server can thus synthesize and automatically append the two lines per Segment needed (#EXTINF tag and Segment URL) to keep the live media playlist updated.

e. When the final Segment of the Track completes uploading, the media playlist SHALL be uploaded again, but this time adding a #EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD line before the #EXT-X-INDE-PENDENT-SEGMENTS line, adding all #EXTINF and Segment lines, and adding a #EXT-X-ENDLIST tag as the last line in the playlist.

With the ordering and rules specified above, the following state tracking can be used at the CMAF Server for HLS mode:

- The upload of the session\_name/index.m3u8 multi-variant playlist file indicates the start of a new CMAF Session.
- Counting the number of lines in the multi-variant playlist which contain the strings EXT-X-MEDIA or EXT-X-STREAM-INF will indicate how many Tracks will be uploaded.
- The contents of a session\_name/track\_name/index.m3u8 media playlist file does not contain the string EXT-X-ENDLIST indicates the start of a CMAF Track.
- The contents of a session\_name/track\_name/index.m3u8 media playlist file containing the string EXT-X-ENDLIST indicates that this CMAF Track has completed uploading.
- When the number of completed Tracks equals the number of Tracks listed in the multi-variant playlist file, the CMAF Session has completed uploading.

# <span id="page-909-0"></span>**11.7.2. CMAF Ingest Examples**

This section provides URL examples for [Interface-1](#page-922-3), [Interface-2 HLS](#page-922-2), and [Interface-2 DASH](#page-922-1) showing the computed filenames for the manifests, playlists, init segments and media segments in their upload order.

#### **11.7.2.1. Interface-1 Examples**

#### **11.7.2.1.1. Single Track**

Using the examples and rules above the sequence of POST\_URL values for a three segment session using just a video track would be:

- [https://ingest.example.com/provider\\_supplied\\_arbitrary\\_data/in/base/part/of/url/session\\_1/](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/video.init) [video/video.init](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/video.init)
- [https://ingest.example.com/provider\\_supplied\\_arbitrary\\_data/in/base/part/of/url/session\\_1/](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/segment_1001.m4s) [video/segment\\_1001.m4s](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/segment_1001.m4s)
- [https://ingest.example.com/provider\\_supplied\\_arbitrary\\_data/in/base/part/of/url/session\\_1/](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/segment_1002.m4s) [video/segment\\_1002.m4s](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/segment_1002.m4s)
- [https://ingest.example.com/provider\\_supplied\\_arbitrary\\_data/in/base/part/of/url/session\\_1/](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/segment_1003.m4s) [video/segment\\_1003.m4s](https://ingest.example.com/provider_supplied_arbitrary_data/in/base/part/of/url/session_1/video/segment_1003.m4s)

#### **11.7.2.1.2. Separate Tracks**
